Sūta said: Thus questioned by them at that time, the Asura, a great devotee of the Lord and filled with devotion for the Blessed One, related it to the Brahmins.
Prahlāda said: O gods upon earth, listen to this supreme, eternal secret which has not been told to anyone; I shall speak of it in great detail.
When he set his mind upon returning to Dvārakā, the ancestors who had been liberated from Naraka sang in heaven.
As many steps as a person takes on the path of Kṛṣṇa, for every step he obtains the fruit of an Aśvamedha sacrifice.
He who urges other men toward the pilgrimage of the God of gods undoubtedly attains the station of Viṣṇu. || 21 ||
He who provides shelter to one traveling to Dvārakā, as well as sweet words, indeed rejoices and sports [in heaven]. || 22 ||
The man who provides a vehicle for one whose body is exhausted on a journey shall go to heaven by means of a celestial chariot yoked with swans.
Listen also to what happens for one who, with devotion, gives food to a person traveling on a journey who is hungry at midday. (24)
Whatever merit a man obtains on earth by performing a śrāddha at Gayā, that same merit is gained through the gift of food, resulting in inexhaustible satisfaction for the ancestors.
But the man who gives a pair of sandals to those going toward Dvārakā travels upon the shoulder of an elephant by the grace of Kṛṣṇa. (26)
But that fool who creates an obstacle for those going toward Dvārakā sinks into the Raurava hell for the duration of an entire kalpa. || 27 ||
That fortunate man who gives a water-pot to one standing on the road obtains the fruit of a thousand gifts of drinking-water stations. || 28 ||
He who provides anointing of the feet and the washing of the feet for one traveling on a journey shall attain all his desires. (29)
O best of Brahmins, there is no one more fortunate than he who hears a verse of Viṣṇu or the song sung by Him on the road, or who gives a gift [for that purpose]. (30)
That best of men who beholds the temple of Lord Kṛṣṇa, which has its residence upon the peak of Kailāsa and is as stainless as a white cloud; || 31 ||
Seeing from afar a golden pitcher joined with a banner, he abandons his vehicle and, having fallen to the ground, rolls about.

The sin committed in the five slaughterhouses, as well as whatever unrighteousness has been done, the insects, worms, and moths killed while walking on the road, the food of others, the water of others, the sight of the untouchable, and contact with them—all that goes to destruction upon seeing the banner of the Blessed One. (34)
One should recite the Thousand Names, or else the King of Hymns (Stavarāja), or indeed the Gajendramokṣaṇa, while walking slowly along the path.

Singing in many ways of the various manifestations of the Blessed One, rejoicing again and again along with those dancing in a state of joy, and himself dancing while filled with delight, the devotee shall go to the city of Hari.
This is the place where Viṣṇu sports, bestowing both worldly enjoyment and liberation; upon seeing it in the Kali age, liberation itself arises for men. (37)
Prahlāda said: Formerly, the high-minded Bṛhaspati of noble intellect was questioned by the king of the gods, who had bowed down with supreme devotion. (38)
Indra said: "Out of favor, please tell me the greatness of Dvārakā, so that people may obtain an increase in dharma according to their respective portions throughout the four ages. (39)
Having heard these words of Mahendra, O best of sages, Bṛhaspati spoke to Mahendra, who was surrounded by the gods.
Bṛhaspati said: O best of gods, Kṛta, Tretā, Dvāpara, and Kali—this is declared by the best of sages to be the Caturyuga (the cycle of four ages) according to its true nature. || 41 ||

In the Kṛta age, Dharma has four feet, as does the fruit of the Vedas and other scriptures; likewise, sacred fords, charity, austerity, knowledge, meditation, long life, and freedom from disease [abound]. (42)
O Lord, this entire age called Tretā is deficient by one quarter; O Vāsava, in the Dvāpara age, however, two quarters of all this are lost.
In the first division of the Kali age, all of that will remain by only one quarter; thereafter, everything will perish, without a doubt.
Mantras, sacred fords, sacrifices, as well as austerity and rites directed toward the gods, even the Vedas and the scriptures—indeed, all these shall go to utter destruction.
O Lord of the Immortals, kings will for the most part become barbarians (mleccha), and the world will cast reproach upon the virtuous who observe their vows. (46)
Prahlāda said: O twice-born ones, having heard these words of Bṛhaspati regarding the holy ford, all the gods trembled with fear born from contact with the Mlecchas. (47)
Filled with humility, they questioned Bṛhaspati, the preceptor of the gods: "The defect born from association with barbarians is not purified even by the Gaṅgā. (48)
Please, out of your grace, tell us of a place free from the Kali age, where we may go to dwell and attain supreme liberation. (49)
"By what means shall we become liberated from suffering and free from affliction? Out of compassion, be gracious and tell us the sacred path for our welfare. (50)
Prahlāda said: Having heard these words of the lord of the gods, the best of the Aṅgirases, the priest of the deities, reflected for a long time and spoke these words. (51)
Bṛhaspati said: "Indeed, there is a holy place (tīrtha) five krośas in extent, the most excellent among all holy places, renowned by the name Dvārakā, which is free from the defects of the Kali age."
This place was created by Viṣṇu as a destination for the world; it bestows liberation even upon those devoid of knowledge during the Kali age. (53)
The field of meritorious actions is like a saline soil that destroys sin; indeed, once sins have been destroyed there, they do not sprout again.
There are thirty-five million sacred fords here upon the surface of the earth.
Thus, Dvārakā, endowed with sacred fords (tīrthas), is the bestower of liberation there; having attained this supreme human birth, it should be visited with great effort. (56)

Prahlāda said: Having heard the words of Bṛhaspati, Śatakratu (Indra) then spoke: "O Vācaspati, come with me to the great prosperity of Dvāravatī. What fruit is said to result from going there and beholding Lord Kṛṣṇa?"
O Guru, tell me of other principal holy sites there, as well as the fruit obtained from bathing in the Gomatī and at its confluence.
Bṛhaspati said: "Listen, dear one, I shall describe the majesty arising from Dvārakā, where the Blessed Keśava sports in human form. (59)
That Nārāyaṇa, the Lord who pervades the universe, is to be meditated upon at the outset; he alone, the chief of deities, resides in the city of Dvāravatī.
In the Kali age, for embodied beings, taking even a single step toward the city of Dvāravatī yields the merit of a thousand sacrifices.
Those best of men who go to the beautiful city of Kṛṣṇa in the Kali age, they go to the abode of Hari accompanied by hundreds of millions of their ancestors.
For those who meditate with their mental faculty upon the journey toward Dvārakā, the sin committed during ten thousand previous births is dissolved.
In whose embodied being the thought of beholding Kṛṣṇa arises, his sin passes away in a thousand ways upon the sight of His face. 64.
Those who went to Dvārakā and those who died in the presence of Kṛṣṇa—there is no return for them until the dissolution of all beings. 65.
O gods, Mathurā, Kāśī, and likewise Avantī are easily accessible; Ayodhyā is easily accessible in this world, but Dvārakā is difficult to attain in the Kali age.
Having gone to the beautiful city of Kṛṣṇa and remaining in the presence of Kṛṣṇa for six months, they are to be known as liberated while living; this is the truth, O best of gods.
O beloved, the Lord of the Dead washes away the sin residing in the hearts of those who long in their minds for the place where Kṛṣṇa plays.
Even the most terrible sins remain in the body only so long as a man does not go toward Dvāravatī in the Kali age. (69)
In ancient times, Brahmā established the enumeration of the merits of sacred fords (tīrthas) for charity, study, and knowledge; however, in the Kali age, he excluded Dvāravatī from this reckoning.
But that man who goes to Cakratīrtha, even by chance, shall go to the supreme state along with twenty-one generations of his lineage.
Even if one goes to Cakratīrtha out of greed, through some transgression, or with hypocrisy or deceit, one shall not enter into worldly existence again.
Whatever fruit is proclaimed to result from the casting of bones at Prayāga, that same fruit, multiplied a hundred-thousandfold, results from the casting of bones at Cakratīrtha.
On this very earth, that supreme sacred site is highly celebrated; it is renowned as Cakratīrtha, which destroys even the sin of killing a Brahmin.
Whosoever among men shall be born in that family hereafter on earth, they shall all go to the city of Viṣṇu by casting their bones into the Cakra-tīrtha.
What is the use of many sons who merely serve to fill a count? It would be better to have a single son who goes to Cakratīrtha. (76)
What is the use of heated asceticism, what is the use of charity or Vedic study? Even in every possible state of existence, one is liberated if one has gone to the city of Kṛṣṇa.
Even by the most terrible defects created by the Kali age, a human being is never tainted upon seeing the face of Kṛṣṇa in the Kali age. (78)
O son, charity, study, and purity are not the causes; for even one of low caste or evil nature goes to the City of Kṛṣṇa, if [he dies there]. (79)
Whatever fruit is obtained at Vārāṇasī, Kurukṣetra, and the Narmadā, that fruit is attained day by day in Dvāravatī within half a moment.
Blessed among the blessed, they are deities even among the gods—those whose minds are fixed upon Kṛṣṇa and never falter. (81)
Having bathed at the confluence of the Gomatī and the ocean on the occasion of Śravaṇa-dvādaśī, and having beheld the son of Kṛṣṇa, one is never tainted by sin anywhere.
On whichever month's twelfth day (dvādaśī) a person reaches Kṛṣṇakrīḍāpurī and beholds it, they are liberated from the abyss of worldly existence.
O Lord of the Gods, those whose lives depart while in the abode of Kṛṣṇa during the Kali age shall not return from heaven even in hundreds of millions of kalpas.
O child, those humans on the surface of the earth who have not seen the God, the slayer of Kaṃsa, in Dvāravatī should be known as being still within the womb. 85.
Dwelling in Dvārakā is difficult to attain; beholding Kṛṣṇa is difficult to attain; bathing in the Gomatī is difficult to attain; and the Lord of Rukmiṇī is difficult to attain.
In the Kṛta age, austerity is supreme; in the Tretā age, knowledge is said to be supreme; in the Dvāpara age, sacrifice is supreme; but in the Kali age, the glorification of Keśava is supreme.
Whatever fruit is obtained by giving thousands of loads of gold, ten million times that is obtained by beholding the face of Hari, the bestower of all things. (88)
Whatever is given at Dvārakā, as well as at Śaṅkhoddhāra, and what is given at the great holy site of Piṇḍāraka, shall become inexhaustible. || 89 ||
Whatever has been given, such as cows, buffaloes, and the like, as well as gold and garments; a bull, the gift of land, silver, and likewise the giving of a daughter in marriage. || 90 ||
And whatever else, O Lord of Gods, one bestows upon these three recipients, that is declared to be the cause of liberation for both the ancestors and oneself. (91)
Since this field is proclaimed in the world as being like saline soil, therefore all gifts given here have been declared by the great seers to be liberating.
Whatever one performs there—whether giving gifts or sporting and bathing—the Blessed One Madhusūdana has declared that its fruit is infinite.
For one who has gone to Dvāravatī and beheld Kṛṣṇa, there is no state of being a preta, nor is there the agony of Yama or of hell. (94)
In the Kali age, when the offering of funeral cakes (piṇḍa) is made even with mere water at the Gomatī river, the ancestors attain satisfaction lasting until the dissolution of all beings.
O best of gods, those householders who constantly remember the beautiful city of Kṛṣṇa are worthy of homage by all the worlds and the gods. 96.
Knowledge of Brahman, the performance of Śrāddha at Gayā, death among herds of cows, and residence for men in Dvārakā—this is the fourfold liberation. 97.
They are liberated either through the knowledge of Brahman, or by dying at Prayāga, or else merely by bathing in the Gomatī in the presence of Kṛṣṇa. (98)
"I have achieved my purpose and performed my merit," says the great ocean; "and my body has been purified by immersion in the waters of the Gomatī. (99)
Even the most terrible sins remain within the body only so long as one does not perform a bath in the Gomatī with its sin-removing waters. (100)
Having bathed at Cakratīrtha in the Gomatī at Rukmiṇīhrada, and having beheld the beautiful face of Kṛṣṇa, a man shall deliver a hundred generations of his lineage.
And those men who, endowed with devotion to Hari, constantly remember Kṛṣṇa in Dvāravatī, become indeed cleansed of sin and go to the supreme realm of Murāri. (102)
One who has not yet washed his feet should first pay homage to Gaṇeśvara; thereby the destruction of all obstacles occurs—of this there is no doubt. || 103 ||
One should affectionately prostrate like a staff before Kṛṣṇa, the son of Devakī, who is dark-complexioned like the petal of a blue lotus; one should likewise prostrate before his elder brother. 104.
Whatever sin was committed in childhood, as well as in youth and manhood, shall perish by the sight of Lord Kṛṣṇa; there is no doubt in this matter. || 105 ||
Whatever sin has been accumulated through speech, mind, or action over a thousand lifetimes—that shall perish; of this there is no doubt. (106)
Whatever fruit is obtained by giving thousands of loads of gold, that fruit is multiplied ten millionfold by beholding the face of Kṛṣṇa.
And having paid homage to the Lord of Gods, the lotus-eyed Acyuta, to Durvāsas, the Great Lord, the protector of Dvārakā; 108.
Having bowed with supreme devotion to him who was accompanied by Vainateya, he again approached the auspicious gate, which resembled the gateway to heaven.

Having rested for half a muhūrta, surrounded by friends and kinsmen, the wise man should summon the Brāhmaṇas residing there who are experts in mantras; then, having brought the materials for worship, he should proceed to the sacred ford (tīrtha).

Prahlāda said: Thereafter, O best of the twice-born, one should go to the Gomatī, which has Kṛṣṇa as its refuge. By the mere sight of her, one is liberated from all sins; being completely freed from all evils, one attains union with Kṛṣṇa. || 1 ||
One should bow down to the water of the Gomatī, which destroys the flood of misfortunes, eliminates inauspiciousness, and grants all desires to human beings.
One should bow down to the water of the Gomatī, which destroys great sins, grants a destination to those without one, and has been obtained through the power of past merit.
The sages said: O Lord of Daityas, we have a doubt that you ought to dispel here; O high-minded one, who is this Gomatī, and by whom was she brought there?
"O best of the Bhāgavatas, for what purpose have you come here to the abode of Varuṇa? Tell me all of this in detail."
Prahlāda said: In ancient times, when all had become a single ocean and both the mobile and immobile worlds had perished, Brahmā then arose from the lotus-navel of Viṣṇu.
Commanded by the Lord, Brahmā was instructed: "Create various progeny. Thus was the Creator (Dhātṛ) commanded by Hari for the purpose of creation.
Having said "So be it," Brahmā then set his mind upon creation; he immediately created from his mind the Kumāras, Sanaka and the others. Brahmā spoke these words: "O sons, create progeny."
Having heard the words of Brahmā, they spoke with palms joined in reverence: "O Blessed One, O Lord, we desire to behold the form of the Blessed One."
"We shall not follow the bondage that takes the form of creation, which is difficult to overcome. Having spoken thus, all those youths, Sanaka and the others, departed.

Taking their stand in the western direction on the shore of the lord of rivers and streams, desiring to behold the form of the Great-Souled One which consists of radiant energy, they fixed their minds upon Him and performed supreme austerity.
After many thousands of years, when the Supporter of the Earth was propitiated, he emerged from the waters, having split them, in an invincible form of radiant energy.
The Sudarśana [discus], which subdues many daityas, shatters numerous mechanical devices, possesses the brilliance of ten million suns, and has a thousand spokes.
Seeing that supreme and excellent weapon of the Blessed One, all the sons of Brahmā were struck with wonder as they looked at one another.
Beholding them in such a state, an incorporeal voice spoke: "O sons of Brahmā, the Blessed One will soon manifest himself."
"O twice-born ones, let an offering be prepared quickly for the worship of the Blessed One; let the weapon of the Lord of the World be presented swiftly. (16)
Having heard those words from the sky, they praised Sudarśana.

The sages said: O you who consist of light, salutations be unto you; salutations to you, O beloved of Hari! O Sudarśana, salutations be unto you, the thousand-spoked, imperishable, and undecaying one. (18)
Salutations to you who are the form of the sun; salutations to you who are the form of Brahman. Salutations to you, the unerring one; repeated salutations to you, the wheel of the chariot.
In this manner, they honored him with flowers as well as unbroken grains (akṣata).
Having praised the beloved of Hari with various hymns and having propitiated that one with the beautiful navel, they bowed down, eager for a vision of the Lord.
Remembering in their minds the god Brahmā, their own father, he understood their thought and then spoke to Gaṅgā.
"O best of rivers on earth, because you went to the cow for the sake of Hari so swiftly, O highly fortunate one, you are therefore held in high esteem by me."
On earth, you shall become well-known by the name Gomati. || 23 ||
"Follow Vasiṣṭha and go quickly to the earth; follow your father like a daughter, and become the daughter of Vasiṣṭha. (24)
"So be it," said the goddess, and she set out for the abode of Varuṇa; Vasiṣṭha went ahead, and Gaṅgā followed behind him.
Seeing her accompanied by Vasiṣṭha as she was proceeding toward the western ocean, all those highly fortunate men paid homage to her.
He appeared right there where those sages were stationed, desiring to behold the four-armed form of Hari endowed with splendor.
Seeing the highly fortunate Vasiṣṭha following the river that purifies the gods as she approached, they scattered flowers over her from all sides.
Having worshipped with divine garlands, fragrant scents, perfumes, incense, and unbroken grains (akṣata), they spoke with joyful minds, saying, "Excellent! Excellent! (29).
Seeing Vasiṣṭha at their head, those twice-born ones then rose up; having performed the hospitable rites such as offering the Arghya water, they spoke this with great joy: || 30 ||
"Since this best of rivers has been brought here into this world by you, she shall therefore attain fame in the world as 'your daughter'. (31)
Since this place was reached by the cow from heaven and was thus considered by me, it shall indeed attain fame in the world by the name Gomatī.
By the mere sight of this, human beings shall attain liberation; how much more so, then, by performing bathing, giving gifts, and other rites, do they go to the abode of Hari? (33)
Having offered that very arghya, those lords of yogis praised Hari, the Supreme Person reclining upon Śeṣa, with the Puruṣasūkta.

While they were thus offering praise, Hari appeared before them, clothed in yellow silk garments and adorned with a forest garland; his limbs were anointed with divine unguents and he was decorated with celestial ornaments. (35)
The god was seated upon his remaining throne, with many divine weapons raised aloft; he wore a blazing crown and diadem, and shimmering makara-shaped earrings.
He bestows devotion and fearlessness, is peaceful, marked with the Śrīvatsa, and possesses mighty arms; his face is ever-gracious, he is dark as a rain-cloud, and has four arms.
Seeing him, who was enchanting and graced by Lakṣmī intent on massaging his feet, all the sages were filled with the highest joy; they praised Viṣṇu with the Viṣṇu-sūktas originating from the Vedas.
While they were thus praising him, Viṣṇu, who is compassionate toward the distressed, spoke with a very gracious mind to those best of the twice-born.
The Blessed Lord said: "O princes, I am pleased; I shall grant you whatever you desire. You shall be endowed with knowledge and remain untouched by my māyā."
"O Brahmins, because I have been propitiated with water by those seeking liberation, therefore this supreme holy ford is the highest bestower of all desires. (41)
O brahmins, it was for your benefit that my Sudarśana discus first emerged before me, having pierced through the waters.
"Therefore, this shall become renowned as Cakratīrtha; my own residence shall also be permanently established here in the great ocean."
O best of the twice-born, those men who perform a bath here at Cakratīrtha, even incidentally, have liberation held in the palm of their hand.
O best of the twice-born, you too should always remain here, existing in the atmosphere as wind, granting all desires.
Prahlāda said: Having heard that, with a joyful mind, he prepared the arghya offering for the purifier of the gods; having washed the feet of Hari, he then held the water upon his head.
Having washed the feet of Hari, she entered the abode of Varuṇa; there, that Gomatī, which removes great sins, went to the ocean.
Having granted the boon, Viṣṇu then vanished right there; the sons of Brahmā, Sanaka and the others, remained in that place with concentrated minds.
Thus, that Gomatī was born there, flowing toward the ocean; she is declared to be the remover of all sins, and she is known as the ancient Gaṅgā. (49)

Thus ends the fifth chapter, titled "The Description of the Origin and Greatness of the Gomatī River, preceded by the Account of the Manifestation of the Lord through the Power of Sanatkumāra’s Austerities," within the Dvārakā-māhātmya, the fourth section of the seventh book (Prabhāsa-khaṇḍa) of the Śrī Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a compendium of eighty-one thousand verses. || 5 ||
The sages said: "Excellent, excellent, O illustrious one, O Prahlāda, best of the asuras! For by you, the Lord Hari has been revealed to us even in the midst of the Kali age."

This narrative, arising from the milk-ocean of your mouth, is like nectar; no satiety arises for the sages as they drink it with their ears. O mighty-armed one, relate in great detail the pilgrimage to the sacred fords (tīrthayātrā).
We must go there where the Gomatī flows, where the Blessed One resides, beholding Cakratīrtha.
O dear one, O high-minded one, lift up those who have fallen into the ocean of existence from that very sea of worldly life, and tell us the procedure for the pilgrimage to sacred sites.
Prahlāda said: Having gone to the bank of the Gomatī, one should prostrate before her like a staff; then, having washed one's hands and feet and placed kuśa grass upon the hands.
Having taken a bright fruit together with unbroken grains (akṣata), one should, being purified and facing the east, offer the arghya according to the prescribed rite.
O auspicious Gomatī, now that the noble son of Vasiṣṭha has returned from the world of Brahmā, I offer this arghya for the sake of purifying all my sins.
O daughter of Vasiṣṭha, O goddess worshipped by the gods, O illustrious one; O goddess saluted by the three worlds, O Gomatī, take away my sin!
Having uttered this, O best of the twice-born, and having taken earth with his hand while recollecting Viṣṇu in his mind, he should pronounce this mantra: ||| 9 ||
O Earth, traversed by horses, traversed by chariots, and traversed by Viṣṇu; you were lifted up by the boar-like Kṛṣṇa with his hundred arms.
O Earth, take away my sin that has been accumulated by me in the past; through the sin destroyed by you, may I remain purified for a year. (11)
Having thus smeared himself with clay, he should perform his bath according to the prescribed rule; having bathed with the mantra "āpo asmān," hear what fruit he shall obtain. (12)
Whatever merit is found at Kurukṣetra when the sun is eclipsed by Rāhu, that same merit is obtained simply by bathing in the Gomatī in the presence of Kṛṣṇa.
Having bathed there with devotion in this manner, one should perform the rites as prescribed; filled with sincere intent, one should offer libations to the gods, the ancestors, and human beings.
Those who reside in the Raurava hell and those who have attained the state of insects—by the gift of water from the Gomatī, they attain liberation; of this there is no doubt. (15)
Even without unbroken *darbha* grass, or likewise without meditative visualization, one obtains the fruit of a *śrāddha* at Gayā by means of water alone in the Gomatī. (16)
Then, having invited Brahmins who are knowers of the Vedas residing on the bank, and having worshipped the Viśvedevas and others, he should perform the Śrāddha for the ancestors. || 17 ||
Endowed with supreme faith, having performed the funeral rite according to the prescribed rules, one should then give a sacrificial fee consisting of gold as well as silver.

[One should give] a cow with horns adorned with gold, her hooves decorated with silver, her tail adorned with gems, covered with cloth, having a copper-colored back, and accompanied by her calf. || 29 ||
Having honored a Brahmin with garments, ornaments, and decorations, one should give him a gift accompanied by seven kinds of grain, saying, "May Viṣṇu be pleased with me."
Having dismissed these Brāhmaṇas as far as the boundary, with his senses restrained, he should give gifts according to his ability to the poor, the blind, and the wretched.
The Gomatī river, bathing with cow dung, the gift of a cow, gopi-candana, and the sight of Gopinātha—these five things beginning with the letter 'ga' are difficult to obtain. (22)
Therefore, one should perform the gift of a cow on the bank of the Gomatī; by doing so, O best of the twice-born, a man becomes one who has fulfilled his purpose. (23)

Those who have gone to the terrible hell, those who have come to the state of hungry ghosts (pretas), and those who, through the ripening of past karma, have attained the state of stationary beings (sthāvaras); || 24 ||
In the Kali age, whoever belongs to the paternal side or those born into the maternal lineage—all of them attain liberation simply by the sight of the Gomatī.
O best of Brahmins, those men by whom the Śrāddha rite is performed at the Gomatī undoubtedly attain the fruit of the horse sacrifice (Aśvamedha). || 26 ||
Whatever merit is proclaimed to come from bathing at the Gaṅgā at Prayāga, a man who performs a Śrāddha at the Gomatī attains that same merit.
Indeed, the ancestors born in that family go to the world of Viṣṇu; their sin, spanning many thousands of births, perishes—of this there is no doubt. (28)
Whatever sin has been committed through speech, through action, or likewise through the mind—all that indeed goes to dissolution by the sight of the Gomatī. (29)
O twice-born ones, for that man who performs a ritual bath in the Gomatī during the month of Kārttika, the Blessed One, together with Lakṣmī, becomes pleased; of this there is no doubt.
With a well-concentrated mind, he should daily satisfy the consumer of the oblation; and every day, food consisting of the six flavors should be given to the twice-born.
One should worship Lord Kṛṣṇa every day, intent on devotion; O best of Brahmins, one must abide by some form of discipline or other.
With the permission of the Brāhmaṇas, a man should undertake the observances there when the month of Kārttika is complete and the day of awakening (Bodhavāsara) has arrived. || 33 ||

One should bathe the Lord of Gods with the five nectars (pañcāmṛta) and with water from sacred fords; and one should devoutly anoint Dāmodara, Hari, the Lord of Gods, with sandalwood paste mixed with saffron and combined with musk.
One should worship the one whose banner is Garuḍa with flowers born of water, with tulasī, with karavīra, and with whatever flowers grow in that region.
One should offer beautiful food offerings with the thought, "May Viṣṇu be pleased with me," as well as through song, instrumental music, dance, and the recitation of sacred texts.
One should keep a vigil at night with various kinds of hymns; having invited Brāhmaṇas with devotion, one should feed them according to one's capacity. (37)
Then, O best of Brahmins, at the end of the month of Kārttika, one should worship the God who has Garuḍa as his banner while he stands upon his chariot at the confluence of the Gomatī and the ocean.

Having bathed and offered libations to the ancestors, one should worship Janārdana; having honored the Lord of Ramā with fine garments and ornaments, one should bring the vow to completion with the permission of the brahmins. (39)
O best of brahmins, he who thus bathes in the presence of Kṛṣṇa during the month of Kārttika, being liberated from all sins, goes to the world of Viṣṇu.
That man who, being constantly contented along with his wife, performs the Māgha bath in the Gomatī with devotion at the rising of Vainateya (the Sun), [attains the highest state]. || 41 ||
Sesame seeds together with gold should be given to the most excellent of Brahmins; likewise, sweetmeats mixed with molasses, accompanied by ritual fees (dakṣiṇā), should be offered every day.
Men should perform a fire-oblation daily with sesame seeds soaked in clarified butter; for the purpose of the oblation one should tend the fire, but never for the sake of warding off the cold. (43)
He who bathes with devotion in the Gomatī during the month of Māgha, which is dear to Mādhava, and at its conclusion offers red garments, a tunic, and a turban; || 44 ||
One should devoutly give a pair of sandals and especially saffron, as well as a woolen blanket cooked with oil, saying: "May Viṣṇu be pleased with me. (45)

And the destiny that is ordained for those who die in battle amidst a tumult of weapons while performing their master’s service, or for those who die for the sake of cows and for the sake of Brahmins; || 46 ||
And she is declared to be present at the Māgha bath in the Gomatī; of this there is no doubt. For him, there is the fruit of all gifts as well as the fruit of all sacred fords (tīrthas). || 47 ||
By performing the Māgha bath, a man goes to the eternal world of Viṣṇu; by worshipping Janārdana, he attains all his desires. (48)
O Brahmins, he who spends the entire month of Māgha at the confluence of the Gomatī and the ocean with the permission of the Brāhmaṇas shall attain complete perfection in everything.
O best of the twice-born, even sinners who have bathed in the waters of the Gomatī attain the destination of those who perform sacrifices, by the grace of the wielder of the discus.
That state of the wielder of the discus (Viṣṇu) which lies above the stations of Brahmā and Rudra is said to be attained merely by bathing in the Gomatī in the presence of Kṛṣṇa.
Whatever sin lies in betraying a friend, and whatever sin lies in killing one's teacher—that same sin he incurs who causes the abandonment of a pilgrimage.
Sinful ones who have seized the property of Brahmins, as well as those who have seized the property of the gods, are purified merely by bathing in the Gomatī; of this there is no doubt. (53)
Whatever merit a man obtains by granting fearlessness to those who are afraid, that same merit he attains merely by bathing in the Gomatī. || 54 ||
By granting fearlessness to the frightened, one obtains desired sons; there is no doubt about this. Furthermore, one who desires wealth obtains abundant and powerful riches. (55)
At the confluence of the Gomatī and the Nīra, O brahmins, one shall obtain all desired objects; having fulfilled his purpose, he shall be liberated from his debt to the ancestors.
Whatever sin has been accumulated through thought, word, and deed—all that perishes by the confluence of the waters of the Gomatī. (57)

Clad in yellow garments, likewise mounted upon Garuḍa, wearing a forest garland, four-armed, and anointed with divine perfumes and unguents, O Brahmins, he goes to the abode of Viṣṇu, which is characterized by the absence of rebirth.
Merely by bathing in the Gomatī, a human being—of this there is no doubt—is liberated from all sins and goes to the eternal Viṣṇu.

Thus ends the sixth chapter, titled "Description of the Greatness of Bathing, Giving Gifts, and Other Rites at the Confluence of the Gomatī and the Ocean," in the fourth section (Dvārakāmāhātmya) of the seventh book (Prabhāsakhaṇḍa) of the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, consisting of eighty-one thousand verses.
Śrī Prahlāda said: O best of the twice-born, from there one should go to the great ocean known as Rathāṅga, where stones marked with the discus are seen, which bestow liberation.
Those who daily worship the Lord of the World with devotion, and who always gaze upon Janārdana with unblinking eyes; || 2 ||
And that which was directly seen by the Blessed One, Kṛṣṇa, with his own eyes—that supreme tīrtha of Hari known as Cakra destroys all sins. (3)
Its supreme renown extends throughout the three worlds, including all that is mobile and immobile; it is more purifying than Prayāga and is indeed a bestower of liberation.
Wherein the limbs of embodied beings, marked with the discus, are worshipped even by the gods within six months; of this there is no doubt.
That sacred place (tīrtha), by the mere sight of which even a man is liberated from sin—even through incidental contact—is remembered as the most excellent purifier among all sacred places.
Having gone there, O best of the twice-born, and having joyfully washed his feet, hands, and face, he should again prostrate himself like a staff.
Having prostrated and taken the arghya-water provided with the five jewels, along with flowers, unbroken grains of rice, perfumes, fruits, gold, and excellent sandalwood; || 8 ||
Taking the prepared water for respectful offering (arghya), one should recite this mantra while facing westward with self-restraint, or facing toward the great ocean.
Oṃ, salutations to you who possess the form of Viṣṇu; salutations to you, the discus of Viṣṇu. Accept this water offering given by me, and become the granter of all desires.
"Agni is splendor, and Rudra is Mṛḍaya; Viṣṇu is the placer of seed and the navel of immortality. Speaking this word of truth, O Vāḍavas, one may then plunge into the lord of rivers. (11)
O Brahmins, having taken earth mixed with water that has fallen from the hand of a deity, and having placed it upon his head, he should perform his bath according to the prescribed rite.
One should satisfy the ancestors, the gods, and human beings in their proper order; having thus performed the libation, one should then sprinkle the sacrificial materials with devotion.
O best of the twice-born, the fruit that is said to result from a thousand horse-sacrifices properly performed is obtained merely by bathing at Cakratīrtha.
O best of the twice-born, that fruit which is proclaimed for worshipping Mādhava at Prayāga on the full moon day of Māgha is said to be obtained merely by bathing at Cakratīrtha.
Then, endowed with faith, one should perform a śrāddha for the ancestors; [one should worship] the Viśvedevas with gold and the ancestors likewise with silver.
Having satisfied them with food, as well as with garments, ornaments, and decorations, one should give gifts according to one's own ability to the poor, the blind, and the miserable.
O best of the twice-born, at Cakratīrtha, the most excellent of sacred sites, one should especially perform the gift of jewels for the sake of pleasing the Lord of the Universe.
One should indeed give a cart yoked with oxen, provided with all coverings and equipped with its accessories, saying, "May Viṣṇu be pleased with me."
Having adorned a well-trained horse, endowed with good character and equipped with its trappings, one should give it to a Brahmin along with a sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā).
O best of the twice-born, when this is done, a man becomes one who has fulfilled his purpose; his ancestors, born of three lineages, attain liberation.
Those who have gone to the womb of hungry ghosts, those who have become insects, and those who are being cooked in the hell known as Mahāraurava; || 22 ||
They all attain satisfaction through the power of Cakratīrtha; O best of the twice-born, when a śrāddha is performed there, one obtains the fruit of a śrāddha at Gayā.
O best of the twice-born, by bathing at Cakratīrtha, a man attains that destination which is ordained for those devoted to their mothers and for those who perform sacrifices.

O best of Brahmins, when the moon has waned, a śrāddha is highly commended; during a solar eclipse, it is especially so, and is remembered to yield the fruit of Kurukṣetra. This applies likewise to bathing, giving gifts, and the libations offered to the ancestors.
And Cakratīrtha is highly praised; there should be no doubt about this. || 26 ||
O Brahmins, Cakratīrtha is always purifying; of this there is no doubt. Any man who, having come on a pilgrimage, performs a śrāddha ceremony there—
O best of the twice-born, having worshipped Madhusūdana at Cakratīrtha while honoring the foremost of the brahmins, one shall attain the presence of Viṣṇu.

Whatever karma has been committed by speech, whatever has been done by deed, and whatever has been accumulated by the mind—that sin is destroyed merely by bathing; there is no doubt in this matter. || 29 ||

Thus ends the seventh chapter, titled "Description of the Greatness of Cakratīrtha Situated on the Banks of the Confluence of the Gomatī and the Ocean," in the Dvārakāmāhātmya, the fourth section of the Prabhāsakhaṇḍa, within the Skanda Mahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses.
Prahlāda said: "Do not go to the celestial river Gaṅgā, nor to the Kālindī, nor to the Sarasvatī. O best of the twice-born, go instead to the confluence of the Gomatī and the ocean. (1)
Where all desires are attained with ease, of this there is no doubt; where the ocean sports with the surging waves of the Gomatī’s waters.
The sin-destroying bank of the Gomatī is reached by meritorious men; where it merges with the ocean, it is the destroyer of great sins.
O best of the twice-born, where the Gomatī joins with the ocean, that place is declared to be the gateway to liberation in the Kali age; of this there is no doubt.
Whatever merit one quickly obtains at the confluence of the Gaṅgā and the ocean, that same merit one attains at the confluence of the Gomatī and the ocean.
Having paid homage to the Lord of Waters and to Gomatī, the best of rivers, one should offer the arghya according to the prescribed rite, having placed kuśa grass in both hands.
O best of Brahmins, having gathered together with the Brahmins who always dwell at that sacred ford, one should offer the arghya according to the rule with this mantra.
With devotion, I shall offer this arghya to the God, the Supreme Self; protect me, a terrible sinner; salutations to You who possess the form of a deity. (8)
O King of Tīrthas, salutations to you, O great ocean, mine of jewels! O Govinda, together with the Gomatī, accept this arghya; salutations be to you.
Having offered the *arghya* and tied his topknot, and having recollected the Lord reclining upon the waters, he should perform his bath facing east, and then likewise facing west.
Having bathed with supreme devotion, he should then satiate the ancestors; having worshipped the Viśvedevas and others, he should perform the Śrāddha for the ancestors.
One should give the prescribed sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā) with the thought, "May Viṣṇu be pleased with me. O best of Brahmins, gold should especially be given as a gift.
"May Viṣṇu, the Lord of the World, together with Lakṣmī, be pleased with me; [I offer] the garments of the husband and wife, as well as the tunic and the turban. (13)
Having performed all the great gifts at the confluence of the Gomati and the ocean, one becomes the lord of the seven islands and is glorified in the world of Viṣṇu.
He who gives the gift of the "man of gold" (tulāpuruṣa) at the confluence of the Gomatī and the ocean, having become the lord of the seven continents, is glorified in the world of Viṣṇu. || 15 ||
He who would weigh himself against gold or silver, or against garments, or even saffron, or likewise fruits or liquids; || 16 ||
Having enjoyed vast pleasures as well as captivating desires, that man, being honored by the gods, goes to the abode of Viṣṇu.
By giving gifts of gold and silver, as well as a horse and a cow, at the confluence of the Gomatī, one shall attain all desires.
And he who, having bathed at the confluence of the Gomati and the ocean, being pure and remembering Hari, should give a gift of land—there is indeed no one more blessed than him. (19)
Furthermore, the man who performs the gift of a daughter in marriage or the gift of knowledge, having bathed at the confluence of the Gomatī, goes to the abode of Brahmā.
Whoever, with a concentrated mind, should give a golden cow, a ghee cow, or even the gift of the Brahmāṇḍa, his merit is infinite.
Likewise, by giving a cow made of salt or even a cow made of water at the confluence of the Gomatī and the ocean, one goes to the supreme abode.
And by bathing at all the beginnings of the Yugas at the confluence of the Gomatī and the ocean, and by satiating the ancestors with libations, one shall attain the imperishable world.

And on the full moon days of Āṣāḍhā, Māgha, and Kārttika, at the confluence, a man who desires the imperishable state should perform libations for the ancestors, ritual bathing, the Śrāddha ceremony, the worship of Agni, and likewise give gifts.
O highly fortunate one, just as the satisfaction of the ancestors through a śrāddha at Gayā is indeed inexhaustible, so too is it through a śrāddha at the confluence of the Gomatī and the ocean.
O best of the twice-born, one should likewise perform bathing, giving gifts, and the libation for the ancestors on the Pañcakās as well as on the Aṣṭakās.
During the Vaidhṛti and Vyatīpāta yogas, during the shadow of the elephant (Gajacchāyā), on the sixth lunar day known as Kapilā, and likewise on the twelfth days (Dvādaśīs). || 27 ||
Having bathed at the confluence of the Gomatī, one should especially give gifts; one attains a stainless state where, having gone, one does not grieve.
On the Śrāddha fortnight, on the new moon day at the confluence of the Gomatī and the ocean, one easily attains merit equal to that of Gayā by offering a funeral cake (piṇḍa).

Therefore, O best of the twice-born, you should all with every effort perform the śrāddha rite at the confluence of the Gomatī on the new moon day at the end of the fortnight dedicated to the ancestors.
Even if a Śrāddha is performed by one ignorant of the Vedas, or even if it should be defiled, the merit gained from performing the fortnightly Śrāddhas is obtained in a single day.
Devoid of faith, devoid of mantra, or likewise devoid of a worthy recipient; lacking the necessary materials, lacking the proper time, and deprived of mental composure. (32)

Indeed, during the fortnight of the Śrāddha, on the new moon day at the confluence of the Gomatī and the ocean, everything becomes complete and the satisfaction of the ancestors becomes inexhaustible.
The Gomatī, the Kamalā, and likewise the Candrabhāgā—these three rivers having joined together, entered the abode of Varuṇa.
A man who performs the Śrāddha at the end of the fortnight obtains that same merit which is gained by offering funeral cakes (piṇḍas) at Gayā or by casting bones into the waters at Prayāga.
If one desires the effortless attainment of bathing in all sacred fords, one should indeed perform a bath with devotion at the confluence of the Gomatī and the ocean.
But for those by whom the complete worship of the ancestors has been performed on every single fortnight, it becomes fully perfected at the confluence of the Gomatī and the ocean.

O twice-born ones, when the Śrāddha is performed on the new moon day and during the fortnight of the ancestors, even a woman who is childless or one who bears only female offspring shall [attain success]. (38)

Likewise, O Brahmins, a woman whose son has died should perform a bath at the confluence; she is liberated from all defects at the confluence of the Gomati and the ocean. Having bathed there, she attains happiness and long-lived progeny. (39)
Whatever gifts whatsoever exist upon the earth, all of those indeed should be given at the confluence of the Gomati and the ocean.
O best of Brahmins, one should always, and especially on all sacred festival days, perform a ritual bath with self-restraint at the confluence of the Gomatī and the ocean.
O twice-born ones, by the mere sight [of it], the destruction of sin occurs; through prostration, the mind attains satisfaction, and through immersion, liberation itself is attained.
When a śrāddha is performed, the ancestors attain eternal satisfaction; through giving, the fulfillment of one's heart's desires arises—of this there is no doubt. (43)

O tigers among sages, those fortunate ones who have performed the libations for their ancestors and the śrāddha ceremony at the confluence of the Gomatī and the ocean have indeed accomplished all that was to be done.
Some indeed on the father’s side, and likewise on the mother’s side, as well as on the father-in-law’s side, and those others who are friends and kinsmen; || 45 ||
Those who have attained the state of immovable beings, and those who have attained the state of persons; those who have become piśācas, and those who have come to the state of pretas. || 46 ||
And those who have gone to the state of animals, and those who have become insects—all of them attain liberation merely by bathing; of this there is no doubt. || 47 ||
How much more so, then, by performing faithful acts such as giving gifts at the confluence of the Gomatī; a human being attains liberation there, of this there is no doubt. (48)
By bathing at the confluence of the Gomatī and the ocean on the occasion of the Śravaṇa-Dvādaśī yoga, one attains liberation, having gone where one does not grieve.

Having abandoned all other holy places, a man who bathes at the confluence of the Gomatī and the ocean and likewise performs a śrāddha shall have fulfilled his purpose; indeed, by worshipping Vāmana, he attains the supreme world.
That man who, having bathed properly, should worship the one whose banner is Garuḍa, having put on yellow garments and being adorned with divine ornaments; || 51 ||

Beheld by the celestial women, with the enemy of the serpents (Garuḍa) as his banner, having become four-armed and adorned with a forest garland, that man, being praised by sages, goes to the abode of Viṣṇu.
Having bathed at the confluence of the Gomatī, a man becomes one who has fulfilled his purpose, at that place where the powerful Viṣṇu slew the Daitya.
O twice-born ones, the discus was indeed previously washed by Kṛṣṇa himself; for that very reason, it is renowned throughout the three worlds as Cakratīrtha.
In that place there are stones marked with the discus which bestow liberation; by worshipping them, Kṛṣṇa, the Lord of the World, becomes present.
If it should be found in that very place together with twelve wheels. || 56 ||
He who is marked with a single wheel at Dvāravatī is beautiful and should be known as the twelvefold self, the bestower of liberation upon all embodied beings. || 57 ||
This [first] is named Sudarśana, for it indeed bestows the single fruit of liberation; Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa, formed by the two [mantras], bestows the fruits of both worldly enjoyment and liberation. (58)
With three [syllables], he is indeed Trivikrama, the bestower of the fruits of the three aims of life; joined with four, he is the granter of prosperity and the slayer of enemies. (59)
Vāsudeva, who removes the fear of birth and death, [is worshipped] with five; Pradyumna, who bestows fortune and splendor, is [worshipped] with exactly six.
Cakraga is proclaimed here as being marked with seven [lines], and Puruṣottama, who bestows devotion, is marked with eight. (61)
The Navavyūha bestows everything that is difficult even for the gods to obtain; the tenth, Daśāvatāra, grants a kingdom—of this there is no doubt. (62)
The one residing in the disc bestows sovereignty with eleven [spokes], and the twelvefold self likewise grants nirvāṇa with twelve.
Beyond this, O fortunate ones, are those who bestow both happiness and liberation.
For here those stones are marked with the discus of Kṛṣṇa.
By the mere touch of them, one is liberated from all sins; having bathed at Cakratīrtha, a man is marked with the discus of Kṛṣṇa.
Having worshipped the Wheel-bearer Hari, one should meditate upon the Eternal One; such a man is never born without a son, nor poor, nor diseased. (66)
Sins such as the killing of a Brahmin, born of the actions of mind, speech, and body—all of these go to dissolution by the mere sight of one marked with the discus even once. (67)
Whether in a barbarian land or even in an auspicious one, if the mark of the discus is seen, that very place is a field of Hari that grants liberation; of this there is no doubt.
Even when the time of death has arrived, if a man meditates upon Hari and bears the mark of the discus on his body, he goes to the supreme abode.

When the mark of the discus resides in his heart, he becomes purified at that very moment; the messengers of Yama do not approach him in fear, for he possesses the weapon of Kṛṣṇa. He attains the world of Viṣṇu—of this there is no doubt.

Even one of evil conduct [is liberated]; how much more so one who is righteous and pure! Having bathed at the confluence of the Gomatī and likewise at Cakratīrtha, a human being is released from terrible sins; there is no doubt in this matter.
Those characterized by passion (rājasa) attain goodness (sattva) and the eternal dharma of Viṣṇu; this is proclaimed as the truth due to the majesty of that sacred field (kṣetra). 72.
Whatever in the worship of Viṣṇu may be characterized by tamas or even rajas, that too attains the state of sattva, just as a river does upon reaching the ocean.
O Brahmin, Dvārakā is difficult to attain; the water of the Gomatī is difficult to attain; keeping a vigil at night is difficult to attain; and the sight of Kṛṣṇa is difficult to attain.

Thus ends the eighth chapter, titled "Description of the Greatness of Cakratīrtha, Preceded by the Greatness of Bathing at the Confluence of the Gomatī and the Ocean," in the Dvārakāmāhātmya, the fourth section of the Prabhāsakhaṇḍa, within the Śrī Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a compendium of eighty-one thousand verses. || 8 ||
Prahlāda said: O best of the twice-born, one should then go to the seven highly renowned ponds, which pacify all sins and increase prosperity and intelligence.
And when Hari, the Lord of the World, having been propitiated, appeared while being praised by the sages along with Lakṣmī; || 2 ||
Then they performed an offering for Hari with the celestial Gaṅgā, as she stood on his left side, prepared to consecrate Padmā.
These seven twice-born sons of Brahmā, Sanaka and the others, having each separately created pools with their minds, sprinkled the daughter of the ocean.
Then the Lakṣmī-hradas were proclaimed by the Goddess, designated right here; however, at the end of the Dvāpara age, they came to be known by the name of Rukmiṇī.
Furthermore, it became known as Rukmiṇī-hrada in the Kali age; and because it was resorted to by Bhṛgu, it is remembered as Bhṛgutīrtha.
Having gone there, O highly fortunate ones, having washed his feet with earth, and having sipped water (performed ācamana), he, being restrained and pure, should take up kuśa grass and face the east.
Having taken a full *arghya* offering consisting of fruit, flowers, unbroken rice grains (*akṣata*), and so forth, and having placed silver upon his head, he should utter this mantra: || 8 ||
With devotion, I shall offer the arghya oblation into the lake named after Rukmiṇī, for the destruction of all sins and for the gratification of Rukmiṇī.
Then, O Brahmins, having placed the *tāraka* mantra upon his head, he should perform his bath; thereafter, he should offer libations to the gods, to human beings, and especially to the ancestors.
Then, having invited Brahmins with devotion, one should perform the Śrāddha ceremony; thereafter, one should give sacrificial fees (dakṣiṇā), consisting of silver and gold.
Especially should delicious fruits be offered; O best of the twice-born, one should provide a meal for the couple with sweet food.
The wives of Brahmins and other women should be honored according to one's ability with bodices and red garments, saying, "May Rukmiṇī be pleased. (13)
O best of the twice-born, when this has been performed, a man becomes one who has accomplished his purpose; he attains all desires and goes to the world of Viṣṇu. || 14 ||
And Fortune always dwells in his house; of this there is no doubt. He possesses health, contentment of mind, and never any agitation.
There shall be inexhaustible satisfaction for the ancestors, and one's progeny becomes steadfast; the man shall never be lacking in strength and shall possess long life. (16)
He who bathes in the Rukmiṇī lake becomes wealthy everywhere; O Brahmins, such a man is never forsaken by fortune, nor is he ever overtaken by misfortune.
There is no enmity or quarrel for him who has bathed in the Rukmiṇī-hrada; likewise, there shall be no coming and going, nor wandering through saṃsāra.
Whence could there be suffering or grief for him who has bathed in the Rukmiṇī-hrada, being liberated from all sins and freed from great fear? (19)
Having obtained all desires here in this world, the man goes to the abode of Viṣṇu.
Prahlāda said: O best of the twice-born, one should then go to the sin-destroying holy site known as Kṛkalāsa, the unsurpassed Nṛga-tīrtha. || 1 ||
Where the protector of the earth, Nṛga, assuming the form of a lizard, attained the supreme goal after meeting with Kṛṣṇa. || 2 ||
The sages said: Who was this king named Nṛga, and how did he come into contact with Kṛṣṇa? By what deed did he become a chameleon? Tell us that in detail.
Prahlāda said: O Brahmins, there was a king named Nṛga, a sovereign ruler endowed with power; he was intelligent, steadfast, skillful, illustrious, and possessed of all virtues.
Even hundreds of thousands of rulers of the earth were under his sway; he was surrounded by multitudes of elephants, horses, and chariots, as well as many foot soldiers.
He possessed an army for that king and likewise an inexhaustible treasury; he was constantly devoted to his guru and intent upon the worship of the deities.
O best of Brahmins, that king gives great gifts every day; indeed, that most excellent of monarchs constantly bestows a thousand cows.
Having washed his feet with devotion and seated him upon an auspicious seat, one should clothe him in two beautiful linen garments and anoint him with fragrant unguents.

Having honored him with flower garlands and fragrant incense, he then gave a cow along with a sacrificial fee to each brahmin with devotion, saying, "May Viṣṇu be pleased with me," accompanied by offerings of betel leaf.
O best of the twice-born, as he thus bestowed gifts, performed sacrifices, and enjoyed pleasures, time passed by.

Once, O best of the twice-born, that king spoke with faith to Jaimini, who was firm in his vows and averse to accepting gifts; standing with palms joined in reverence, the king addressed these words to him.
"O illustrious one, lift me up; have mercy, O treasure of asceticism! Out of compassion for me, please accept this cow given by me. (12)
Having heard those words of his, although he was unwilling, the brahmin, out of respect for the king and feeling ashamed, said, "So be it."
Then, having washed his feet, he held the water over his head [as an offering], along with a cow possessing golden horns and adorned with silver hooves.
Having worshipped a cow with a jeweled tail, a bronze milking vessel, and covered with white cloth, he gave her, along with a priestly fee, to the best of Brahmins.
Having followed her as far as the boundary, the king was indeed filled with joy; she was a young woman, white as a swan, renowned by the name Haṃsī.
Having taken the cow, that best of Brahmins reached his own home and tied her with a rope along with her calf; he then gave her fresh grass.
Then, at midday, the brahmin took her—who was thirsty despite having been well-satiated with fodder—and led her out, bound by a rope, toward a body of water.
On the road, crowded with elephants and horses, she became terrified at the sight of a camel; then, snatching the cow from the hand of the brāhmaṇa, she fled.
Searching the entire earth, that bull among the twice-born did not see her; meanwhile, that cow had fled to that great royal herd of cattle.
On the second day, that best of kings again summoned the Brahmin and, having honored him according to the rules with devotion, [presented him] with garments, ornaments, and decorations.
And that king gave the cow to Somaśarman according to the prescribed rites; having accepted it, the bull among the twice-born departed from the royal palace.
Hoping that the king was a knower of dharma and learned, that brahmin wandered everywhere searching for his cow, deeply distressed.
On the road, he saw [the cow] following behind Somaśarman; having seen that cow, the sage Jaimini spoke to him.
"How is it that you, like a bandit, have seized my cow and are carrying her away? Hearing his words, he was struck with amazement at the mention of a "bandit."
"O best of the twice-born, why do you call me a thief of cows when I am leading this cow, which I received from the king, to my own home? (26)
The Brahmin said: "I too received this cow from the king; of this there is no doubt. O Brahmin, how can you take her to your home while I am alive? (27)
He said, "Today she was obtained by me; why do you speak falsely to me? He replied, "She was obtained by me yesterday; you wish to take her away by force. (28)
Enraged, Somaśarman spoke these words: "This is mine! And the other, his eyes red with blazing anger, said: "This is mine! (29)
Thus, those two brahmins, engaged in dispute, arrived at the king’s gate, quarreling fiercely and desiring to give up their lives. (30)
Seeing the two Brahmins enraged and cursing each other, the gatekeeper respectfully informed the king.
Disregarding the two Brahmins who were then disputing and filled with wrath, the king, his mind agitated by desire, did not go outside.
Thus disputing, the two remained together for three nights; then, having been disregarded by the king, they became angry with the monarch.
Enraged and filled with indignation, they spoke these words to the king: "Since you disregard us and do not depart from the palace. (34)
"Since you, as the teacher of living beings, will not employ them according to justice, you shall therefore become a lizard; of this there is no doubt. (35)
Having thus uttered the curse, those two brahmins gave the cow to another; then, hungry and overcome with exhaustion, they set out for their own homes. (36)
As the two were setting out, Nṛga arrived at the gate and stood before them; prostrating like a staff and quickly joining his palms in reverence, he spoke.
Your words are never in vain; it shall be exactly so and not otherwise. Having shown compassion toward me, please instruct me on how this curse may end.
Having heard those words of his, they spoke these words to the king: "The Blessed One, the son of Devakī, [will appear] at the end of the Dvāpara Yuga. (39)
O King, Hari will manifest in the house of Vasudeva; by his mere touch, there shall be liberation from the curse.
Having spoken thus, those two brahmins then departed for their own abodes; the king, having enjoyed various pleasures and having given away gifts in abundance, [remained]. (41)
Having performed various sacrifices and having met the law of time, he then went, O brahmins, to the abode of Dharmarāja.
Then Yama addressed that best of kings with hospitable greetings: "O King, first tell me whether good deeds or evil deeds must be experienced by you; I shall then provide for that. (43)

Nṛga said: "If there was any evil deed committed by me, let it be expiated first. Having been thus commanded by Yama himself, 'Become a lizard,' I then attained the state of a lizard for thousands of years."
One day, all the Yādava youths, accompanied by Kṛṣṇa, went to the forest to hunt deer, O Brāhmaṇas. || 45 ||
Afflicted by thirst at midday, they were searching for water in a lake, where they saw a very large being and a chameleon situated there.
The young princes of the Yadu clan exerted every effort to lift it up; however, being dragged by them, it did not budge due to its great weight.
When they were all unable [to lift it], they reported it to Kṛṣṇa and Rāma; then Kṛṣṇa saw him, thinking he was Nṛga, and as if smiling.
The Lord of the Universe cast it away with his left hand as if in sport; touched by the Blessed One, he was released from the bond of the curse.
Having cast off his body, the king—adorned with divine garlands and unguents and filled with supreme devotion—spoke this with palms joined in reverence: || 50 ||
Salutations to you, O support of the universe, the cause of creation, preservation, and destruction; salutations to you, the thousand-headed Brahman of infinite power.
To him who was thus praising Him, the Blessed One, the son of Devakī, said: "I am pleased; I grant you a boon, whatever dwells in your mind."
"By whom, through my sight and touch, the worlds of the merit-makers are revealed. Thus addressed by the god, his hair stood on end with joy.
He said: "O Keśava, if you are pleased, and if a boon is to be granted to me, let this pit become famous by my name."
"O Govinda, by your grace, may he who, having bathed with supreme devotion, shall gratify the ancestors, go to the world of Viṣṇu. (55)
Having spoken thus, the Blessed One returned once more to Dvārāvatī.
And that king, adorned with divine garlands and unguents, went by celestial chariot to the abode of Viṣṇu, extolled by the gods.
Prahlāda said: From that time forward, O best of Brahmins, that well has been known by the name of Nṛga; and by the granting of a boon from Kṛṣṇa, it is purifying for all embodied beings.

Having gone there, O best of the twice-born, one should indeed offer the arghya according to the prescribed rite, along with fruits, flowers, unbroken grains (akṣata), and sandalwood paste, O gods on earth.
Salutations to you, Viṣṇu, the Supreme Soul, whose form is the universe; O Lord of Gods, accept this water offering in this well named after the Ṛgveda.
Then, O best of the twice-born, one should bathe after smearing mud with one's hand, and should offer libations to the ancestors, the gods, and human beings in their proper order.
Then, filled with faith, one should perform the śrāddha for the ancestors; one should provide food to the brahmins and give them a sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā) according to one's ability.
In particular, a well-adorned cow along with her calf should be given; one should also give a bed with its furnishings, saying, "May Viṣṇu be pleased with me."
And one should always give gifts according to one's own capacity, free from stinginess regarding wealth, to the poor, the blind, the miserable, and those who dwell on its banks.
O best of Brahmins, by merely bathing there, one obtains the fruit of giving a cow; and by performing the ancestral Śrāddha rite for the ancestors, one does not fall into a degraded womb.
That man who performs a Śrāddha and likewise an offering of water (tarpaṇa) at Kṛkalāsa shall go to the world of Viṣṇu together with his ancestors.
In this way, the fulfillment of one's desires and the journey shall become fruitful; one obtains the fruit of all sacred fords—of this there is no doubt. (67)
Prahlāda said: O best of the twice-born, one should then go to the sacred ford (tīrtha) originating from Viṣṇu’s foot, by the mere sight of which one obtains the fruit of bathing in the Gaṅgā.
O best of the twice-born, I have previously described the origin of that [deity], by the mere remembrance and recitation of which there is the destruction of sin.
She was brought by the high-souled Hari for the sake of Rukmiṇī; by merely sipping a mouthful of her water, one obtains the fruit of a horse sacrifice.
Born from the foot of Viṣṇu, she is renowned as Vaiṣṇavī; having gone there, O highly fortunate one, and having taken the water-offering (arghya) according to the prescribed rite, || 4 ||
I bow to you, O Blessed One, born from the soles of Viṣṇu’s feet; O Goddess Gaṅgā, accept this water offering together with Hari.
Having uttered this, O best of the twice-born, and having taken earth with his hand, he should, facing east and remaining self-controlled, perform his bath without indolence.
One should satisfy the gods, the ancestors, and human beings with sesame seeds and unbroken grains; having presented offerings and then invited the Brahmins.
Endowed with supreme faith, the wise man should perform the śrāddha ceremony; he should give the prescribed sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā), such as gold and silver.
Gifts should be given according to one's ability to those who are distressed, blind, and miserable; O best of the twice-born, gold in particular should be bestowed.
Then, sandals should be given, as well as a water-pot to the twice-born, along with curd-rice mixed with salt, vegetables, and cumin.
One should have Rukmiṇī clothed in red garments and bodices, as well as the wives and husbands of Brahmins, with the words: "May Viṣṇu be pleased with me. (11)
When this is done, O best of the twice-born, a man becomes one who has fulfilled his duty, just as the ancestors obtain imperishable satisfaction through a śrāddha performed at Gayā.
The ancestors born of his three lineages go to the world of Viṣṇu; he lives endowed with prosperity and accompanied by sons and grandsons.
Keśava, together with Rukmiṇī, is always pleased with him; the Lord grants all his desires pertaining to both this world and the next.
He who listens with devotion to this incomparable majesty arising from the feet of Viṣṇu during the time of Hari is liberated from all sins.
Having heard this meritorious chapter, one is liberated from all sins.

Thus ends the eleventh chapter, titled "Description of the Majesty of Viṣṇupada Tīrtha," in the fourth section, the Dvārakāmāhātmya, of the seventh book, the Prabhāsakhaṇḍa, of the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a compendium of eighty-one thousand verses.
Prahlāda said: Thereafter, O best of the twice-born, one should go to Gopracāra; having bathed there with devotion, a man obtains the fruit born of the gift of a cow.
O best of the twice-born, that place where the Lord of the World, surrounded by the deities, bathes in the month of Nabhasya is declared to be Kaṭadāna on the twelfth lunar day.
The sages said: O Lord of Daityas, how did that sacred ford (tīrtha) known as Gopracāraka come to be there? Tell us the truth regarding that place where Janārdana performed his ablutions.
Prahlāda said: When Kaṃsa, the king of the Bhojas, had been slain by Kṛṣṇa of immeasurable splendor, and the high-souled one had consecrated Ugrasena in Madhupurī; || 4 ||
He who is dear to Gokula sent Uddhava to Gokula for the sake of doing what was pleasing to his friends and to the community of cowherds and cowherdesses.
Having paid homage to Govinda, he departed for Nanda’s cowherd settlement, assuming an attire similar to his with garments, ornaments, and decorations.
Seeing his beloved follower of Govinda at the end of the day, he honored Uddhava with garments, ornaments, and decorations.
When he had finished eating and was rested, Yaśodā, who is deeply affectionate toward her son, her eyes filled with tears of joy, asked Hari about his well-being.
I hope my two sons, Rāma and Kṛṣṇa, the best of the Yadus, are well; I hope Govinda remembers his companions, the cowherd boys.
Will Govinda, the Lord of Mathurā, come to Gokula? Will this son deliver Gokula from the ocean of suffering? (10)
Having spoken thus, Yaśodā and Nanda, their eyes filled with tears, wept long and piteously, overcome by affection for their son.
Then Uddhava, seeing those two facing a threat to their very lives, restored them to life with sweet messages from Kṛṣṇa imbued with affection.
Your elder brother pays homage to you and to your lordship; he has inquired after your health, and both of you remain in well-being. (13)
The powerful Lord of the Daśārhas will arrive soon, accompanied by Rāma; having come here, the Lord of the World will bring about your welfare.
Having thus been comforted by Kṛṣṇa’s messages, Uddhava then slept soundly on his bed, welcomed by Nanda and the others.
Then, seeing the chariot at Nanda’s gate, the gopīs were struck with wonder; suspecting it might be Kṛṣṇa’s arrival, they cried out, "Who is this? Who is this? (16)
The mighty-armed one, accompanied by attendants dressed as Kṛṣṇa, arrived at the house of King Gopāla in a chariot with the splendor of the sun. || 17 ||
Having come together, all those women of Vraja, emaciated by grief, questioned that messenger of Kṛṣṇa in a secluded place.
The illustrious gopīs said: Why have you arrived here? What indeed is your business here today? For, disguised in the form of a bandit, you surely wish to destroy us. (19)
Having first caused the multitude of women to drink the poison from his lower lip, he fled, having already destroyed their hearts and other vital organs by that Kṛṣṇa.
Having spoken thus, those gopīs, overwhelmed by grief, fainted; gazing at that servant of Kṛṣṇa, they fell upon the surface of the earth.
Seeing those people whose hearts were captivated by love for Kṛṣṇa, Uddhava then consoled them with words that were pleasing to the ear.
Uddhava said: "The Blessed One, the descendant of Daśārha, being tormented by the arrows of Kandarpa, neither eats nor sleeps, as he ponders your matter day and night."
Having heard those words of his, Lalitā, overwhelmed with anger, her eyes copper-red, then spoke to Uddhava while weeping.
Lalitā said: "You are untruthful, one who has broken the bounds of propriety, cruel, and a favorite of cruel people; do not speak before us of that man of undisciplined soul. (25)
"Fie, fie upon him of sinful conduct! Fie, fie upon him of cruel intent! That fool Hari has abandoned the womenfolk and gone to Dvāravatī. (26)
Śyāmalā said: "O virtuous ladies, do not speak further of that unfortunate, meritless, and evil-minded man; tell me another story. (27)
Dhanyā said: "By whom has this messenger of the wicked person been brought here? Let that sinner go back by the same path by which he came, so that he does not return again. (28)

Viśākhā said: "O virtuous women, for one who possesses neither good character nor noble birth, and who feels no fear of committing sin—the birth and deeds of such a man are known to be fit for the killing of a woman. Association with that man, who is devoid of human purpose, is useless. (29)
Rādhā said: "O virtuous women, for one who feels no fear of committing sin in the killing of living beings, there can be no doubt whatsoever regarding the killing of a wife."
Śaibya said: "Tell me the truth, O illustrious one: what does that best of the Yadus do? Having been united with the women of the city, would he remember our conversation? (31)
Padmā said: "O noble Uddhava, beloved of the women of Nāgarī, when will the scion of the Daśārhas, whose eyes are as broad as lotus petals, arrive here?"
Bhadrā said: "Alas, Kṛṣṇa! Alas, best of cowherds! Alas, beloved of the gopīs! O mighty-armed one, deliver the gopīs from the ocean of worldly existence! (33)
Prahlāda said: Thus, lamenting with various words, those women of Vraja wept piteously, O Goddesses, as they remembered the deeds of Kṛṣṇa.
Hearing their lamentation, filled with devotion and affection, he was struck with great wonder and exclaimed, "Excellent! Excellent! (35).
Uddhava said: Neither Brahmā, nor Hara, nor the gods, nor the great sages follow their true nature; therefore, all the women of Vraja are blessed.
The birth, life, youth, and wealth of all those women are truly fruitful, whose devotion to the Blessed One is unwavering. (37)
The gopīs said: "Show us Govinda well! Show us our beloved well! Lead us properly to that very place where Acyuta resides. (37)
Prahlāda said: Having heard their speech and their many lamentations, Uddhava, overwhelmed with affection, said to them, "So be it. (39)
Then all those women of Vraja, filled with joy and longing for the sight of Kṛṣṇa, followed along with Uddhava.
Singing the beloved songs and accounts of His childhood deeds, the women of Vraja proceeded slowly together with Uddhava.
Then, having seen the rows of gardens and groves in the city of Yadu, they said: "Today we shall behold the Lord named Kṛṣṇa, the joy of Nanda."
Then, by going to Dvāravatī and by meditating upon the Lord of Lakṣmī, they were liberated from all impurities and had all their bonds shattered.
Then all of them arrived at the shore of Lake Māyasa; having prostrated before them, Uddhava spoke to the cowherd women, whose deity was Kṛṣṇa.
"Stay here, O mothers; the mighty-armed Kṛṣṇa, whose eyes are like lotus petals, will come to this very place and will bring about your welfare."
The gopīs said: "O Uddhava, whose is this lake here, adorned with cranes and filled with variegated lotuses, white water-lilies, night-blooming lilies, and blue lotuses? (46)
Uddhava said: There was a great Daitya named Maya, a master of illusion renowned throughout the world; by him a beautiful lake was constructed, which became famous after his name. (47)
The illustrious gopīs said: "Quickly bring Govinda here; show us the Infallible One, who produces joy for the eyes and destroys the threefold suffering. (48)
Having heard those words of the gopīs, Uddhava then had Śrī Kṛṣṇa brought by swift-moving messengers.
Seeing the son of Devakī approaching swiftly on his vehicle—resplendent with a beautiful form and adorned with a forest garland—|| 50 ||
He wore a blazing crown and tiara, shimmering crocodile-shaped earrings, bore the Śrīvatsa mark, possessed mighty arms, and was clothed in yellow silk garments.
His head was covered by parasols held by the foremost of the Vṛṣṇis, and he was praised by the chief bards amidst the sounds of singing and musical instruments.
He was surrounded on all sides by the people of the city and the countryside, as well as by Vaiṣṇavas; he beheld a lake adorned with cranes and graced by pairs of swans.
Seeing Acyuta approaching—the beloved of the world, so enchanting—those women of Vraja, having finally beheld their dear one after a long time, were utterly transfixed with wonder.
Regaining consciousness after a long time, they lamented in great distress: "O Lord! O Beloved! O Kṛṣṇa! O Enchanting Lord of Vraja! (55)
How can you be so wicked and heartless, having abandoned even those cowherd boys who raised you in childhood and played with you? (56)
There is no righteousness in you, nor kindness, nor truth, nor even friendship; having abandoned your father and mother, how will you attain a happy state? 57.
"O Lord, the abandonment of one's devotees is censured in all the scriptures; O Hero, by abandoning us in the forest, you have disregarded dharma. (58)

Prahlāda said: Having heard the lamentation of those gopīs, O son of Nanda, the all-pervading Lord, who knows the inner feelings of all and has no other refuge, the Master of Vraja consoled those women of Vraja with his words.
Through internal instruction, the Lord taught those cowherd women.
The Blessed Lord said: "There is never any separation from me for you in every respect; I dwell eternally in the hearts of all beings without distinction. (61)
I am the source of all; from me come the gods together with Indra, the Ādityas, Vasus, Rudras, Sādhyas, Viśvedevas, and the hosts of Maruts.
Brahmā, Rudra, and Viṣṇu, as well as the great sages beginning with Sanaka, the senses, the mind, the intellect, and likewise the qualities of sattva, rajas, and tamas—these all abide within it.
Desire, anger, greed, delusion, and egoism—all these without exception proceed from me, O Gopīs. (64)
Having understood this, O highly fortunate ones, do not let your minds become impure; being stainless, contemplate me eternally within all beings. 65.

Prahlāda said: Having heard Kṛṣṇa’s words, those cowherd women—their bonds shattered, their doubts and afflictions liberated, and overflowing with the bliss of his vision—those wives of the cowherds, with pure minds, spoke to Kṛṣṇa. (66)
The gopīs said: Today our birth has become fruitful; today our eyes have attained their purpose, O Govinda, since we behold you, the beloved of the women of the city.

Those devoid of merit do not behold the Supreme Person known as Kṛṣṇa; even though we have been awakened by your words endowed with logic and meaning, O Madhusūdana, Māyā still does not depart from our hearts.
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: "O women of Vraja, by seeing and touching this, you shall be liberated from all bonds; and having bathed here, you will obtain all your desires."
The Gopīs said: "The wonderful power of this lake has indeed been described by you. O Lord of the World, O delighter of the Vṛṣṇis, tell us the ritual procedure in detail. (70)
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: "Since a meeting with you has occurred here for me, I must indeed always bathe here according to the prescribed rule. (71)
He who, having bathed with supreme devotion on the twelfth day of the bright fortnight of the month of Śrāvaṇa, being self-controlled and pure, shall gratify the ancestors; || 72 ||
Having given gifts according to his ability, dedicating them to me as well as to the ancestors, he indeed attains the world of Viṣṇu, surrounded by his ancestors.
Having reached the Māyā-tīrtha and having placed kuśa grass in both hands, one should take a single fruit and offer it as an arghya with the mantra. || 74 ||
O Lord of the Earth, lift me up who have fallen into the blind well of the household, ensnared by hundreds of cords of illusion; accept this offering of water, salutations be unto you! (75)
The Arghya-mantra: He who, having bathed, satisfies the ancestors with supreme devotion from the heart, and performs the Śrāddha ceremony endowed with the highest devotion to the ancestors; || 76 ||
Then one should give a sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā), as well as silver and gold; specifically, milk-rice with sugar should be offered.
"Since my vision has been attained by you all together with butter, ghee, an umbrella, and a woolen rug and deerskin, I must therefore always come to this reservoir. (78)
O beloveds, whoever performs a bath here in the lake of Maya obtains the fruit of bathing in the Gaṅgā, as well as the imperishable realm of Viṣṇu.

His ancestors, born of his three lineages, attain liberation; and he himself, endowed with sons and grandsons and possessed of wealth and grain, shall enjoy happiness for as long as he lives and, at the end, go to the city of Hari.
