Thus ends the twelfth chapter, titled "Description of the Greatness of the Lake Constructed by Maya," in the Dvārakā-māhātmya, the fourth section of the Prabhāsa-khaṇḍa, within the Śrī Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a compendium of eighty-one thousand verses.
Śrī Prahlāda said: Having heard these words of Kṛṣṇa, the gopīs, their minds filled with joy, bathed in that lake and were liberated from all bonds. (1)
Overflowing with supreme bliss born from the sight of Kṛṣṇa, the gopīs spoke these sweet words to Mādhava: || 2 ||
The Gopīs said: Blessed is that foremost of Daityas, Maya, by whom this lake was created, wherein you, O Lord of the World, shall meet with the gods.
If you are pleased, O Blessed One, and if we are worthy of your grace, then, O scion of the Vṛṣṇis, cause us also to build the best of all sacrificial halls.
Indeed, by chanting [your name] in this world of mortals, by beholding you, and by meditating upon you day and night, we shall attain the supreme goal. || 5 ||
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: "O virtuous ladies, I shall do what is pleasing to you, for you are my wives; I must always favor you, as I am ever won over by devotion."
Prahlāda said: Having spoken thus, the Blessed Lord Kṛṣṇa, out of a desire for the welfare of the gopīs, created another lake in the vicinity of that lake.
That lake was deep with clear water, adorned with lotus petals, and graced by pairs of swans and cranes, as well as by ruddy geese.
It was adorned with clusters of white, blue, and red lotuses and water-lilies, and was frequented by the foremost of the twice-born, as well as by Siddhas and Vidyādharas.
It was frequented by the women of the Yadus as well as by the Yadu youths; day and night it was completely filled with all the people of the countryside.
Seeing that reservoir completely filled with surging waves of water, Kṛṣṇa then spoke these words to the group of gopīs out of joy: || 11 ||
"O cowherd women, behold this bright lake nearby, filled with clear and pleasant water, like the minds of virtuous people. (12)
And because this lake was created by you, it shall therefore become famous by your names. (13)
The word "gopracāra" shall be a term expressive of both "cow" and "speech," and it shall attain renown in the world as a name for you along with me. (14)
"Since this lake was created for the sake of doing what is pleasing to you, it shall therefore attain fame in the world as 'Gopī-saras' (The Lake of the Cowherd Women). || 15 ||
The Gopīs said: "If we are worthy of your grace, O Vārṣṇeya, then this lake has been made in our name; tell us, what else may we request?"
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: "Let that which is desired be requested—whatever dwells in your minds. Since you have come here with devotion, there is nothing that cannot be given by me."
The gopīs said: "O Blessed One, if you are pleased, and if a boon is indeed to be granted to us, then, O Kṛṣṇa, O Mādhava, you should always travel by means of a human vehicle. (18)

"Having come here, one must indeed bathe according to the prescribed rule during this month of Nabhasya; for wherever you are, O Keśava, there also are the gods, the sacrifices, and the sacred fords."
Wherever you are, there also are gifts, vows, and restraints; likewise the syllable Om, the Vaṣaṭ-call, the Svāhā-call, and the Svadhā-call.
Bhūr, bhuvaḥ, svaḥ, mahar, loka, janaḥ, satyam, and likewise tapaḥ—the entire universe, including gods, asuras, and humans, is indeed composed of you. (21)
Therefore, O Janārdana, Lord of the World, when you have bathed here, the three worlds will undoubtedly have bathed as well. || 22 ||
Indeed, the Gaṅgā, who purifies the three worlds, is the water from your feet; Lakṣmī resides upon the region of your chest, and the goddess Sarasvatī is in your mouth. (23)
And since you, O Lord of the Universe, consist of all beings, please tell us, O mighty-armed Lord of the World, having shown compassion, what you will bestow upon men in the future Kali age. (24)
Now, tell us the fruit obtained by those who have come on a pilgrimage, by those who reside here for six months, and by those who dwell here permanently. (25)
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: O cowherd girls, since I am pleased with you, listen without any doubt to the fruit that indeed belongs to those men who have bathed in the Gopikāsara lake. (26)

[One should give] the [cow], together with its appurtenances and her calf, adorned with garments and ornaments, accompanied by the prescribed sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā), to a Brāhmaṇa who maintains a household.
By giving a cow to one who is of virtuous conduct, pure, poor, and imitative [of the donor's virtues], one obtains that same fruit merely by bathing. || 28 ||
O Goddesses, as many steps as a person takes while walking with Kṛṣṇa, for that many lifetimes do they dwell in the abode of Hari.
Accompanied by Kṛṣṇa, the cowherd women go along with the sounds of singing and musical instruments, praising Govinda with various hymns of praise.
For those men, no torment arises within their mother’s womb; having attained all desires, they shall in the end reach the world of Viṣṇu.
Having offered the *arghya* according to the prescribed rule, the wise man, endowed with supreme faith, O virtuous ladies, should perform the bath with this mantra.
Salutations to You, Viṣṇu, the Supreme Self, who has assumed the form of a cowherd; O Lord of the World, accept this water offering during the cow-pasturing ceremony; salutations be unto You! (33)

Having offered the *arghya* according to the prescribed rule and having smeared [his body] with clay using his hand, he should bathe endowed with faith and offer libations to the ancestors and the deities.
Then, with devotion, one-pointed mind, and composure, he should perform the Śrāddha ceremony; he should give the prescribed sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā), namely silver and gold.
In particular, betel-leaf and collyrium should be given; likewise, fine silk garments and saffron-dyed cloths should be bestowed.

One should also give garments and ornaments for the husband and wife according to one's means; cows and bulls capable of bearing the yoke should be given to the twice-born; and gifts should be given to the poor, the blind, and the miserable according to one's ability. (37)
By acting thus, a man shall properly attain the highest goal; his ancestors, born of three lineages, go to the supreme world.
One who desires sons obtains beloved and delightful sons. || 39 ||
Whatever desire a person may long for, whether it be heaven, liberation, or anything else, he attains all of that who bathes in the Gopikāsaras lake.
"As long as worlds shall exist, so long indeed shall this lake endure; and as long as the lake exists, so long shall your fame remain. (41)
As long as one's fame endures among human beings, so long is one honored in heaven; those who are liberated from all sin shall go to the supreme goal.
"O Gopīs, this lake, which is always full of water, is that very merit; it must indeed be entered by me with self-restraint during the month of Nabhasya. (43)
Whether you contemplate me as your husband or again as Brahman, you shall indeed attain the supreme goal.
Prahlāda said: Then, permitted by the Blessed One, those cowherd girls paid homage to Govinda and all departed as they had come. (45)
The Blessed Lord Govinda, accompanied by Uddhava, having dismissed the cowherd women, Kṛṣṇa entered his own abode.

Thus ends the thirteenth chapter, titled "Description of the Greatness of Gopīsarastīrtha," in the fourth section, the Dvārakāmāhātmya, of the seventh book, the Prabhāsakhaṇḍa, within the Śrī Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a compendium of eighty-one thousand verses. || 13 ||
Śrī Prahlāda said: There are many holy places that produce great wonders; yet, when the terrible Kali age arrived, they all fled into the ocean.
O Brahmins, listen as I proclaim them by way of summary; O best of Brahmins, [I shall describe] them in brief and the rites that pertain to them. (2)
Having removed the burden of the earth and having established the virtuous on the path of truth, Kṛṣṇa departed for Dvāravatī, surrounded by the hosts of the Vṛṣṇis.
Then Brahmā, surrounded by the deities—Varuṇa, Yama, and Kubera, as well as Sūrya and Candramas—came for the purpose of seeing him.
Having arrived with Kṛṣṇa and accomplished his own purpose, the Creator then established a sacred ford (tīrtha) celebrated on earth by his own name.
Known as Brahmakuṇḍa, auspicious and the remover of all sins, he established the Lord of a thousand rays upon its bank.
Indeed, Brahmā, the grandfather of the worlds, is the root of the gods; because it was established by him, it is known as Mūlasthāna.
Having seen that Brahmatīrtha, Candra then created a lake; indeed, that pond named after Candra destroys all sins.
Seeing him endowed with such splendor, the best of the gods were overjoyed and said to the Creator of the World: "Listen indeed to our words."
O bull among gods, he who performs a bath here shall satisfy the ancestors and worship the Lord of Gods at Mūlasthāna.

O best of the twice-born, on the seventh day of the bright fortnight of the month of Māgha, that man who, endowed with devotion, performs a ritual bath here becomes completely liberated from all sins and is provided with wealth and grain. (11)
O Lord of Gods, having bathed the primary image and anointed it with unguents, one shall worship it with garments and other offerings, as well as with ornaments according to one's own capacity.
By means of flowers, incense, and the like, as well as with food offerings, a person attains all desires and goes to the world of Brahmā. || 13 ||

Then, having seen Sāvitrī who had indeed been established by Brahmā, and having constructed a divine abode and installed his own form therein, the Grandfather himself then bestowed a name upon that goddess.
He who beholds Kṛṣṇa himself with devotion, having seen the Lord of the World, shall become happy through Sāvitrī and attain all his desires. (15)

Longevity, health, sovereignty, and indeed the continuation of progeny—neither misfortune, nor poverty, nor folly shall befall that man who beholds this ritual procedure, nor shall he have any fear of disease. (16)
Having gone there, one should bathe the Goddess with saffron and safflower, clothe her in garments, and worship her with various kinds of flowers.
Having worshipped with supreme devotion by means of food offerings, fruits, betel, necklaces, and lamps, one shall obtain a fruitful pilgrimage.
Neither widowhood, nor misfortune, nor barrenness, nor the death of offspring shall befall those men by whom this rite has been observed; in their lineage, progeny is born.
Therefore, with every effort, one should observe the ritual with a pure disposition; Kṛṣṇa will be thoroughly pleased, and the pilgrimage shall become fruitful.
Prahlāda said: Having seen the most beautiful lake established by Brahmā, the illustrious Indra created another most beautiful lake. || 21 ||
The Lord of the Gods established a Liṅga of incomparable splendor; by bathing in it, a man attains the station of Indra.

Therefore, the name Indrapada is well-known upon the surface of the earth; because the Liṅga was installed by Indra along with Bhāvanā, it is famous by Indra’s name or remembered as Indreśvara. || 23 ||
O twice-born ones, its fame is incomparable, for it is a sign of prosperity; by the mere sight of it, one is liberated from all sins. (24)
O best of the twice-born, by bathing at Indrapada on the eighth and fourteenth lunar days, an inexhaustible satisfaction arises for one's ancestors.
By worshipping Indreśvara, a man attains the state of liberation; he should be worshipped especially when the sun is situated in Capricorn.

Indeed, by filling the linga at the time of the northern solstice transit, and especially on Śivarātri, having worshipped it together with Umā and performed a vigil at night, one shall attain the supreme world.
Prahlāda said: Having seen that Brahma-tīrtha as well as the Śakra-saras, one shall attain oneness of form with Viṣṇu by beholding them. || 28 ||
The Lord of gods, the Blessed One, the husband of Pārvatī, created a lake with very clear and pure water, adorned with lotus petals.

Seeing that lake, which was covered on all sides with blue lotuses, adorned by cranes, and possessed of bottomless waters, the wielder of the Pināka bow, whose banner bears the bull, bathed there himself along with Brahmā and Viṣṇu.
Having seen that lake, all those gods—Brahmā, Viṣṇu, the Suras, and the Asuras—were greatly delighted and, gazing upon the Lord of Pārvatī, they spoke.
"O gods, because this great lake was created by the Lord, it shall become well-known by the name Mahādevasaras. (32)
Whoever performs a bath here, as well as the libation for the ancestors and the ancestral rite (śrāddha) for the ancestors with devotion, shall go to the supreme goal.
All the gods will become exceedingly well-pleased, there is no doubt; and by the sight of Mahādeva’s lake, one is liberated from sin.
And having seen that most beautiful lake of Maheśa, Pārvatī likewise created there a lake of incomparable splendor.
Known as Gaurīsara, it is the destroyer of all sins; having bathed there with devotion, a person shall not meet with an evil fate.
There shall never be misfortune for women, nor widowhood at any time; having bathed in the excellent Gaurītīrtha, one shall attain all desires.
Then Varuṇa, having beheld those holy shrines and being endowed with devotion to Viṣṇu, created a divine lake.
That place on earth named Varuṇapada causes the destruction of sins; and on the full moon day of the month of Nabhasya, having satiated the ancestors and the deities, [one attains great merit].
Having performed the ancestral rite (śrāddha) according to the prescribed rules, endowed with faith toward the ancestors, one attains the highest world, reaching which one does not grieve.
One should give water-pots provided with curd and rice, as well as cows, garments, and jewels, saying, "May Viṣṇu be pleased with me."
Having seen the lake of the Lord of Waters, the Lord of Wealth created a lake well-known on the surface of the earth by the name Yakṣādhipasaraḥ.
Likewise, having worshipped the ancestors and the deities there with devotion, a person attains all desires; he should also give clothing to a twice-born man.
Prahlāda said: Having heard that Viṣṇu was the bestower of boons, O sons of Brahmā, the Mandākinī was brought down to the surface of the earth by Vasiṣṭha for the sake of his brothers.
Ambarīṣa and all the others arrived at Dvāravatī, which was protected by Kṛṣṇa; and there they beheld the Gomatī river as it flows toward the ocean.
The Lords of Creatures likewise established holy fords for the deities, sacred shrines, and the Pañcanada Tīrtha.
The five rivers, summoned there, arrived accompanied by the gods; Gomatī went to Marīci, and likewise Lakṣmaṇā to Atri.
The Candrabhāgā went to Aṅgiras, Kuśāvatī to Pulaha, and likewise Jāmbavatī went to Kratu for the sake of purification.
Having bathed in them, those illustrious sons of Brahmā, the ascetics known as the Pañcanadas, then gave him that name.
Therefore, that Pañcanada Tīrtha is the destroyer of all sins; men who seek heaven and liberation should bathe there at that time.
Having gone there, being well-restrained and taking the arghya with a fruit, O brahmins, he should indeed offer the arghya according to the rule with this mantra: || 51 ||
These five excellent rivers, brought by the sons of Brahmā, O goddesses, accept this arghya for the pacification of all sins. 52.

Thus ends the mantra for the arghya offering. Having performed his bath according to the prescribed rule, a man should gratify the ancestors; then, endowed with supreme faith, he should perform the śrāddha ceremony according to the prescribed rule.
Then, the five jewels and seven types of grain should be given to the twice-born; and one should give gifts to the poor, the blind, and the wretched according to one's own capacity.
He attains all desires and goes to the world of Viṣṇu; accompanied by sons and grandsons, he shall obtain supreme happiness.
Those who have gone to the womb of a preta and those who have become insects—all these ancestors born of the three lineages attain liberation. || 56 ||
Having heard this meritorious chapter, one rejoices in the world of Śiva; liberated from all sins, he goes to the supreme state.
Prahlāda said:
Having heard that their own father, the god Brahmā, had arrived, Sanaka and all the others went to pay homage to the Grandfather.
Seeing him, the creator of the world, they prostrated themselves upon the ground like a staff; then, seeing his sons, he took hold of them and embraced them.
Questioned by them regarding his health, and having questioned them in turn, he said to them: "Blessed are you by whom the Blessed One has been propitiated; we too are likewise blessed."
"Indeed, they have attained supreme perfection through the vision of the Blessed One; yet, O sons, it was not fully understood by you because of your ignorance and childish intellects."
When Mahādeva is honored, Keśava is pleased with him; but when the Blue-throated One is not honored, Hari does not accept the worship. Therefore, with every effort, let Nīlalohita be worshipped.
Hearing those words of hers, the sons of Brahmā then departed, [thinking], "By what means does the worship of Kṛṣṇa, when performed, always reach completion? || 6 ||
Having gone before the temple of the gods, the great sages perfected in yoga, motivated by devotion to Śiva, installed a liṅga.
Having installed the Śiva-liṅga for the purpose of bathing, all those excellent sages, the seers of strict vows, then constructed a well.
Seeing that lake, which was filled with water, perfectly pure, and resembling nectar, all the sages were overjoyed and exclaimed, "Excellent! Excellent! (9).
O twice-born ones, having seen the Śivaliṅga that had been installed, Brahmā, the grandfather of the worlds, was pleased and then spoke these words to his sons.
Brahmā said: "Since Śiva has been installed by you who are perfected in yoga, he shall therefore attain renown in the world as Siddheśvara."
Near Śitikaṇṭha, this well was made by the sages; therefore, it shall become famous in the world as Ṛṣitīrtha.

O best of Brahmins, even without performing ancestral rites (śrāddha), giving gifts, or offering libations to the ancestors, one is liberated along with the ancestors by the mere act of bathing with devotion.
Those who are speakers of untruth and those who are devoted to reviling others are purified merely by bathing at Ṛṣitīrtha; of this there is no doubt. (14)

O best of the twice-born, bathing is highly recommended during the equinoxes (viṣuva), as well as on the anniversaries of the Manus (manvādī), and likewise on the first day of the Kṛta Yuga in the month of Māgha.

O twice-born ones, what need has he of anything else who dwells on Śivarātri at the Liṅga known as Siddheśa after bathing in the Tīrtha created by the Sages? O highly fortunate ones, having gone there and obtained the supreme fruit, [one attains liberation]. || 16 ||
Having offered the *arghya* according to the prescribed rite and having placed *kuśa* grass in his hands, he says: "O gods and great sages perfected in yoga, please accept this *arghya*. (17)
And at the sin-destroying Ṛṣitīrtha, which is endowed with Siddheśvara, one should offer water for honor (arghya), apply earth to the body, and perform a bath with a concentrated mind.
One should satisfy the ancestors, the gods, and human beings in their proper order; thereafter, endowed with faith, one should perform the Śrāddha rite for the ancestors.
And likewise, one should give a sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā), free from stinginess regarding one's wealth; especially should fruits that are full of juice be offered.
One should give śyāmāka and nīvāra grains, coral, skins, the seven types of grain, śāli rice, and parched flour mixed with jaggery.
Having thus offered perfumes, garlands, betel, garments, and likewise milk—having performed all of this in full—a man becomes one who has accomplished his purpose.
Having worshipped Mahādeva, Siddheśvara, the Lord of Umā, the birth of a mortal becomes fruitful and his life becomes well-lived. || 23 ||
He who, having bathed at Ṛṣitīrtha, beholds Śiva as Siddheśvara—his ancestors are satisfied, and his grandfathers are likewise satisfied.

Those men who are devoted to Siddheśvara shall become possessed of sons even if they are sonless, and those who already have sons shall possess grandsons; likewise, those who are destitute shall become wealthy.
When the Lord of Siddhas is propitiated, evil deeds go to destruction, meritorious deeds increase, and the fulfillment of one's heart's desires occurs. (26)
Having bathed at the Ṛṣitīrtha and beheld Hara as Siddheśvara, a man attains all his desires; there is no need for deliberation on this matter.

On Śivarātri especially, Siddheśa is fully worshipped; whatever desire one may long for, he grants it—of this there is no doubt. For the Lord is like a wish-fulfilling gem, or indeed an inexhaustible treasure. (28)
Having heard this supreme, meritorious chapter which removes all sins, a person endowed with faith attains the highest abode. (29)

Thus ends the fifteenth chapter, titled "Description of the Greatness of Ṛṣitīrtha and Siddheśvara," in the fourth section, the Dvārakāmāhātmya, of the seventh book, the Prabhāsakhaṇḍa, within the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a compendium of eighty-one thousand verses. || 15 ||
Prahlāda said: Thereafter, O best of the twice-born, one should go to the unsurpassed Gadātīrtha, where a man who bathes with devotion obtains the fruit born of the gift of land.
One should satisfy the ancestors, the gods, and the sages in their proper order; and one should perform a śrāddha ceremony there for the sake of the satisfaction of the ancestors.
Having worshipped with devotion the Lord of Gods, Viṣṇu, in the form of the Boar at Gadātīrtha, a man is glorified in the world of Viṣṇu.
From there, one should go to Nāgatīrtha, a lake of supreme excellence, where a man, having bathed properly, shall attain the world of the Nāgas.
From there, one should go to Bhadratīrtha, a lake honored by the three worlds; by merely bathing there, a man obtains the fruit of [giving] sesame seeds and a cow.
From there, one should go to Citrātīrtha, a most beautiful lake; by merely bathing there, a person obtains the fruit of [giving] a cow filled with ghee.
O brahmins, when Dvārāvatī was indeed submerged by the ocean, its many meritorious sacred fords were covered by water and dust.
Indeed, there are some visible ones and others that are invisible; O best of Brahmins, I shall describe all of them in their entirety.
From there, one should go to the Candrabhāgā, which destroys all sins; by bathing there with devotion, a person obtains the fruit of the Vājapeya sacrifice.
And there is the goddess Caṇḍārcitā, the daughter of Yaśodā and Nandana; she is a maiden (kaumārikā) holding a spear in her hand and bearing a sword and shield.
She was indeed the sister of Rāma and Kṛṣṇa, the destroyer of the Daityas such as Keśin; by the mere sight of her, one may obtain all desires. (11)
From there, O best of brahmins, one should go to the sacred ford known as Mahiṣa, by the mere sight of which one is liberated from all sins.
From there, one should go to the holy ford (tīrtha) known as Muktidvāra, which destroys all sins.
Where the Gomatī was brought by the sage Vasiṣṭha, bathing there in the Kali age is equivalent to bathing in the Gaṅgā. || 14 ||
Since the Gomatī has issued forth from here and entered the abode of Varuṇa, a person who bathes there with devotion shall obtain the fruit of an Aśvamedha sacrifice. || 15 ||
For penance was performed by Bhṛgu where Ambikā was established; therefore, the Goddess is heard of as being famous on earth as "Worshipped by Bhṛgu" (Bhṛgvarcitā). || 16 ||
By the mere remembrance of which a person attains supreme perfection—that [place] where many Śiva-liṅgas exist upon the surface of the earth. || 17 ||
From there, O best of brahmins, one should go to the supreme lake of the Kālindī; the Kālindī, daughter of the Sun, created that unsurpassed lake.
Having bathed there with devotion, a person shall not fall into an evil state; from there, one should go to Sāmba-tīrtha, which destroys all sins.
And having performed the ancestral rite (śrāddha) according to the rules, one obtains the fruit born from the gift of a cow.
And one should go to the Śāṅkara Tīrtha, which purifies the three worlds; having bathed there with devotion, a man shall obtain much gold.
From there, one should go to the Nāgasaras, a sacred ford that destroys sin; by offering libations to the ancestors according to the prescribed rites, one shall attain the world of the Nāgas.
From there, one should go to the river Lakṣmī as it flows toward the ocean; by the mere sight of her, one is liberated from all sins.
O best of Brahmins, when the śrāddha is performed, the ancestors attain liberation; through giving, the fulfillment of one's desires occurs—of this there is no doubt. (24)
From there, one should go to Kaṃbusaras, a sacred ford that destroys sins; when libations and the Śrāddha rite are performed there, one indeed obtains the fruit of the Agniṣṭoma sacrifice.
From there, one should go to Kuśatīrtha; having bathed, one should offer libations to the ancestors and, having given gifts according to one's ability, one shall attain the stainless world. || 26 ||
And right there is Dyumnatīrtha, which destroys all sins; by performing a śrāddha ceremony at that very place, one obtains the fruit of a horse sacrifice.
From there, one should go to Kuśatīrtha, where the satisfaction of the ancestors becomes inexhaustible through the performance of śrāddha and libations; of this there is no doubt. (28)
From there, one should go to the auspicious Jālatīrtha, which removes all sins, where the Yadu princes were cursed by Durvāsas out of anger.
There, the Lord of Umā became the god Jāleśvara; by beholding Jāleśvara, a person is instantly liberated from sin.
And by worshipping the God with devotion, one shall attain the world of Śiva.
Then a person should indeed go to Cakrasvāmīsūtīrtha; having performed ablutions and offered libations to the ancestors, he shall attain the world of Viṣṇu.
The holy ford established by Jaratkāru destroys all sins; having bathed there, O best of the twice-born, one shall not meet with an evil fate.
Then, O best of the twice-born, one should go to the holy ford named Khañjanaka; there was once a Daitya named Khañjanaka who was endowed with exceeding strength.
Then there is the holy site (tīrtha) known by his name, Khañjanaka; having bathed there, a man goes to the world of Soma, without a doubt. || 35 ||
O best of the twice-born, there are many well-guarded sacred fords (tīrthas); O lords of brahmins, one should go to them for the removal of all sins. (36)
Thence, O best of the twice-born, one should go to the sacred ford of Ānaka-dundubhi; next is the supreme Śūratīrtha, and beyond that, the Gadatīrtha.
And there is the tīrtha of Gāvalgaṇa, as well as that of the high-souled Akrūra; then the tīrtha of Baladeva and another belonging to Ugrasena. (38)
Then there is the sacred ford of Arjuna, as well as the Subhadrā-tīrtha; and first of all, the Devakī-tīrtha and the Rohiṇī-tīrtha. (39)
There is the sacred ford of Uddhava, as well as the one named Sāraṅga; then there is the sacred ford made by Satyabhāmā, and beyond that, Bhadrātīrtha.
There is the holy ford of the high-souled Rāma, the son of Jamadagni, as well as Bhāsa-tīrtha in that very place, and beyond that, Śuka-tīrtha.
There is also the holy ford of Kardama and that of the high-souled Kapila; likewise, Soma-tīrtha and Rohiṇī-tīrtha are located right there.
These and others have been briefly recounted by me to you; they remove all sins in this world and grant liberation, of this there is no doubt. (43)
O best of the twice-born, at the onset of the Kali age, the sacred fords (tīrthas) have become hidden; they have been submerged by the ocean, by dust, and even by water.
Thus have I described to you in brief the extensive details of the sacred fords (tīrthas), according to the measure of my own understanding. What else do you wish to hear? 45.
O twice-born ones, he who hears this pilgrimage with supreme devotion, being liberated from all sins, goes to the world of Viṣṇu.

Thus ends the sixteenth chapter, titled "Description of the Greatness of the Multitude of Tīrthas," in the fourth section, the Dvārakāmāhātmya, of the seventh book, the Prabhāsakhaṇḍa, within the Śrī Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a compendium of eighty-one thousand verses. || 16 ||
Prahlāda said: Having performed his ablutions in the sacred fords according to the rules and having bestowed the sacrificial fees, he should then worship the Supreme Person known as Kṛṣṇa.
The sages said: "O best of Daityas, we desire to hear in brief the ritual procedure for the worship of Kṛṣṇa, together with its practical application, exactly as it is."
And who are the gatekeepers there? Who is in front and who is behind? By whom, O Daitya, is this city protected on all sides as it stands? (3)
"O knower of the ritual, you who are dear to the singular feet of Kṛṣṇa, please tell [me] how they are to be worshipped in due order and in brief, according to the rules."
Śrī Prahlāda said: O Brahmins, listen to the worship of Kṛṣṇa in the Kali age, as previously heard according to the injunctions, O best of Brahmins, exactly and in due order. (5)
Listen with full concentration to the deities stationed at the eastern gate: first, Jayanta is to be worshipped, the auspicious remover of all sins. (6)
Indeed, he was established by the king of the gods for the sake of worshipping Keśava. O best of beings, listen as I describe his very own attendants.
Vajranābha, Sunābha, Vajrabāhu, Mahāhanu, Vajradaṃṣṭra, Vajradhārī, Vajrahā, and Vajralocana. || 8 ||
Śvetamūrdhan, Śvetamālin, and the followers of Jayanta—these, with weapons raised in their hands, protect him day and night.
At the eastern gate, well-armored and acting as sentinels, the Lord of Men and Vināyaka stand for the sake of protection at the eastern gate.
The youthful Sun-god Sūrya, the goddesses together with their mothers, Lord Īśvara, Durvāsas, and Takṣaka, the king of the Nāgas. || 11 ||
Senānī Kārttikeya and the Rākṣasa Mahāhanu were there, as was the Dānava named Dīrghanakha, who was well-established [there].
The Gandharva Viśvāvasu, the excellent Apsaras Menakā, and the venerable sage Vasiṣṭha accompanied by Sanatkumāra. || 13 ||
These are to be worshipped in the east, including the great tree Nyagrodha; for these are situated at the eastern gate. Now hear from me concerning those in the southeast.
Then there was Jvālāmukha, Raktākṣa, Smāśānanilaya, and Kratha; they were flesh-eaters, consumers of blood, black in color, and wore matted hair that was black. || 15 ||
Trāsana and Bhañjana, stationed in the south-eastern direction, protect that quarter; listen now to me as they stand armored for the south.
Daṇḍapāṇi, Mahānāda, Pāśahasta, Sulocana, Anivartyakrama, and likewise Dundubhinisvana. || 17 ||
Kharasvana, Ghargharavāk, Maunapriya, and Mallikākṣa—these are the gatekeepers who bow down to them. (18)
For the purpose of guarding the southern gate, there are Dundubhi and Vināyaka, as well as Mahiṣārka, Sūrya, Bhūṣaṇa, and likewise Īśvara.
And likewise the goddess Caṇḍikā, the Rākṣasa Ūrdhvabāhu, Padmākṣa the Kṣetrapāla, and the Nāga Aśvatara. || 20 ||
The Gandharva Citrāṅgada and the excellent Apsaras Urvaśī; the king of all trees, the great tree Śāla; (21)
Sanātana, the best of sages, and Agastya of great asceticism—these two, being well-composed, guard the gateway in the southern direction.
A singer, a dancer, naked, wearing a blanket, fond of fire, laughing, with distorted eyes, with contorted eyebrows, and yawning. || 23 ||
O twice-born ones, Muśalin stands ready as their lord; they protect the western quarter, the direction of Nirṛti—now hear of others.
Svastika, Śaṅkhamūrdhan, Nīlavāsas, and Śubhānana; Pāśahasta, Śūlahasta, Ekapāda, and Ekalocana. || 25 ||
In the western direction, there is likewise the Vināyaka Puṣpadanta; Uddhavārka, Sūrya, Śiva, and Satrājiteśvara. || 26 ||
The Gandharva named Tumburu, the excellent Apsaras Ghṛtācī, Mahodara the lord of the Nāgas, and the Rākṣasa Ghaṭotkaca; || 27 ||
The Daitya named Pañcajana, the sage Kaśyapa himself, the goddess named Kapālinī, and the great tree Aśvattha. || 28 ||
Kapila and Kṣetrapāla protect the western direction; they are likewise to be saluted and worshipped. Now hear of others belonging to the northwest.
Bhañjana, Bhairava, Kālika, Ghaṭodara, Jhañjhakāmardana, Piṅga, Ruru, Sarvabhuja, and Vraṇin. (30)
O best of Brahmins, Supārśva is the lord of these, standing armored while protecting the northern quarter; and Śyāmala is the leader of the Gaṇas in that northern direction.
Manvantaka, Virūpākṣa, Golaka, Śveta, Saṃpluta, Unmatta, and Prabhu—these protect the northern direction.
Sūrya is indeed at Mūlasthāna, as is Maheśvara Indreśa; the goddess is named Kaṇṭheśvarī, and the Kṣetrapāla is Khañjana. || 33 ||
Vāsuki the king of the nāgas, the Dānava Kūrmapṛṣṭha, Sanaka the best of sages, and likewise the Rākṣasa Golaka. (34)
The Gandharva named Nārada and the excellent Apsaras Rambhā—these are to be worshipped with effort, as is the great tree named Plakṣa.
The lord of the Yakṣas named Savitṛ, who is dark-complexioned, should be worshipped with great effort; O best of Brahmins, I shall now describe those who are situated in the northeastern direction.
Durdhara, Bhairavārāva, Kiṅkiṇīka, Mahābala, Karāla, Vikaṭa, Mūla, Balibhukta, and Balipriya. || 37 ||
O best of the twice-born, among these guardians of the fields and their wives, Jayanta is the leader, the lord, the master, and likewise the protector.
As the protector of the city-dwellers, he restrains and favors them; and taking Jayanta’s command, they slay the wicked.
Lord Jayanta, the protector who eternally dwells at Nāgasthala, surrounded by the serpent kings, should be worshipped with great effort. || 40 ||
And these, with faces fond of meat, indeed protect the northeastern quarter. The thousand-headed god Śeṣa, the Nāga, is stationed on the ground; as are Ananta, Vāsuki, Takṣaka, and Padma.
Śaṅkha, Kambalaka, the nāga Aśvatara, Muktaka, Kāliya, Janaka, and Aparājita; || 42 ||
There are thousands of Nāgas with Karkoṭaka at their head; they are to be worshipped with perfumes, flowers, offerings, incense, and lamps. || 43 ||
Then, having worshipped Devaśa, the best of protectors, with milk-rice, meat, various kinds of food, and likewise with wine; || 44 ||

O best of the twice-born, having worshipped with offerings of perfumes, flowers, incense, garments, ornaments, and the like, one should then go to Kṛṣṇa, the son of Devakī; there, first of all, Gaṇeśa known as Rukmi is to be worshipped.
The sages said: How is it that Rukmi, the lord of the Daityas, who was wicked and yet attained the status of a Gaṇa, is worshipped daily by men as a person at the very gate of the Blessed Lord?
Śrī Prahlāda said: When Bhīṣmaka prepared to give Rukmiṇī to Kṛṣṇa, Rukmin, filled with hatred and anger toward that, turned to the King of Cedi.
When the Blessed One, having routed all the kings led by Jarāsaṃdha in battle, carried away Rukmiṇī from the abode of Ambikā.
Then the mighty-armed and powerful Rukmī, son of Bhīṣmaka, declared: "I shall not turn back from the battle without having slain that Yādava."
O twice-born ones, having thus spoken, he made this vow in the hearing of all the kings; then, fully equipped for battle, he rushed forth.
O twice-born ones, he fought with Kṛṣṇa using only a portion of an akṣauhiṇī; while fighting with Kṛṣṇa, his vigor was destroyed as he was being struck down.
Having been bound by the Blessed One there and having undergone deformity itself, he was released from bondage by Rāma and set his mind upon death.
Seeing her brother resolved upon death, Rukmiṇī, the princess of Vidarbha, said to Kṛṣṇa: "Bring my brother back to me."
Then, having granted his consent for the sake of pleasing him, Janārdana made [him] the foremost among his attendants (pārṣadas) as the destroyer of obstacles.
For this reason, O Brahmins, he is always worshipped first; one should satisfy him with perfumes, incense, unbroken grains, garments, and sweetmeats.
When he is satisfied, the Lord of the World is satisfied; it is not otherwise.
Śrī Prahlāda said: One should worship Gaṇanātha, Rukmin adorned with golden ornaments, as well as Durvāsas, Kṛṣṇa, and Balabhadra, with devotion.
One performs great sacrifices with abundant and excellent sacrificial fees, while another beholds Kṛṣṇa, the Lord of Gods; indeed, the fruits of these two are equal.
One person, with a concentrated mind, constructs ponds, wells, and tanks; another beholds Kṛṣṇa, the Lord of Gods—indeed, both of them obtain equal fruit.
One person gives cows, land, sesame seeds, gold, and so forth day after day; another beholds Kṛṣṇa, the Lord of Gods; indeed, the fruits for both of them are equal.
One who is engaged in breath control (prāṇāyāma) and the like, and devoted to recitation and meditation, perceives the Lord of Gods, Kṛṣṇa; for these two indeed obtain equal fruit.
Having bathed well alone and with a concentrated mind at sacred fords such as the Jāhnavī and others, one person beholds Kṛṣṇa, the Lord of Gods; indeed, the fruits of these two acts are equal.
By beholding Trivikrama, who traversed the three worlds with three strides, one is liberated from the three types of sins.
The sages said: How did this form of Traivikrama come to the surface of the earth? And at what time did it attain its blackness through the placement of the *kalās*?
O Daitya, you ought to sever our doubt entirely; let the origin of Durvāsas and Kṛṣṇa be told.
Prahlāda said: "O best of the twice-born, listen to how the Trivikrama form, having been joined with Durvāsas, appeared upon the surface of the earth."
Formerly, at the end of the Kṛta Yuga, Purandara was defeated by Bali and ousted from his position; for that reason, Madhusūdana [incarnated]. (11)
From Kaśyapa, Vāmana was born; from him came Trivikrama, Hari, the slayer of Madhu, who traversed the worlds measured by three strides.
The Blessed One, Kṛṣṇa, who dwells in the depths of Pātāla, performed an offering; being satisfied by the Daitya through his exclusive devotion, he [granted him a boon].
Then Hari himself, purchased through devotion, dwelt there; for the sake of bestowing grace, the Blessed One became the gatekeeper.
And the venerable Durvāsas, the son of Atri and best of sages, while wandering through sacred fords for the sake of liberation, contemplated the Field of Liberation (Muktikṣetra).
Reflecting thus with his vision of knowledge, O twice-born ones, that great sage went to where the Gomatī meets with the Cakratīrtha.
Recognizing that as a field of liberation, he set his mind upon going; thus he passed beyond cities, villages, gardens, and forests.
Having reached the region of Ānarta, he entered the land of the Daityas, which was devoid of the study of the Vedas and the utterance of "vaṣaṭ," and utterly lacking the sound of the Vedas.
It was inhabited and protected by Kuśa, the king of the Daityas, and was crowded with many Mlecchas and people who earned their living through unrighteousness.
Knowing that it was near, the twice-born man went to Cakratīrtha; having bathed at the holy confluence and performed his daily rites, he thought, "I shall attain liberation."
Having made this resolve, the sage then departed quickly; having bathed, he thought, "I shall go swiftly, leaving the land of the Daityas behind. (21)
Thinking thus, he proceeded quickly along the path; and having seen the holy confluence of the Gomatī with the ocean, || 22 ||
Having placed two garments there, having applied earth and cow-dung, and having tied his topknot and held *kuśa* grass in his hands, he remained self-restrained.
Just as that brahmin was bathing, he was spotted by the evil-minded Daityas, who cried out, "Who is this? Let him be killed! Let him be killed! (24)
"Who is this lowest of men who bathes in the land protected by us? Saying this, they struck him with their knees and fists.
"I am a Brāhmaṇa; I must not be killed. Having heard this, [the king] was deeply pained. But seeing that Brāhmaṇa being struck by those evil-minded men, he [intervened]. || 26 ||
And a great asura named Uru restrained them; they seized his garments and threw those kusha grasses into the water.
Seizing his feet and cursing him, those evil-minded men dragged him; having grasped the sage by the foot, they led him to the boundary and abandoned him there.

Seeing him then nearly unconscious, they spoke in anger: "If he comes here again, we shall certainly kill him; there is no doubt. Having seen those regions of Ānarta and that body of water there," [they said].
Having fallen into a life-threatening danger, he then became lost in thought: "If I were to curse the Daityas, what would be the use of my asceticism? (30)
Or else, if I, having fallen from my vows, should cast off this body, who would uphold my side, and who would grant me life? (31)

"And who here will cause me to perform my ablutions at Cakratīrtha? Or who is capable of conquering these hosts of Daityas in a great battle, except for that lotus-eyed one who bestows fearlessness upon his devotees? (32)

Who else but the one who holds the discus in his hand—He who is the leader of Brahmā and the other gods, and who is compassionate toward those who have come for refuge—could be the bestower of happiness to me today? (33)
Having meditated thus for a very long time and having recognized him as a dweller of the netherworld, Ātreya went to the surface of the earth, seeking refuge in Viṣṇu.
Emaciated and distressed by his fasts, he entered the earth and reached the palace of the king of the Daityas, which was filled with Gandharvas and Apsarases.
Then Durvāsas entered that place, which was graced by the powerful Viṣṇu, the chief of the gods, with a delighted inner soul.
Then, seeing Durvāsas approaching, the lord of the Daityas rose to meet him, honored him, and seated him upon his own throne.
Having offered the madhuparka and the cow, as well as the arghya, he stood at his side and, bowing down, said: "O Brahmin, how have you come here? (38)
Seated comfortably there, that sage beheld Trivikrama standing at the gateway of the lord of the Daityas, free from fear from any quarter.
Upon seeing that Lord of the gods of gods, marked with the Śrīvatsa and possessing four arms, that best of sages wept and cried out, "Save me! Save me! (40).
O Janārdana, O Keśava, be the refuge for those who are terrified by the fear of saṃsāra, for the suffering, and for those overwhelmed by enemies. 41.
For me, tormented by suffering, harassed by enemies, defeated, wretched, and oppressed by hunger. (42)
O Keśava, protector of the brāhmaṇas, become the refuge of this brāhmaṇa, whose observances are incomplete and who has been tormented by the Dānavas. (43)
Having said this, he showed his body mangled by the Daitya; and seeing that insult to the brāhmaṇa, Vāmana became enraged.
"O Brahmin, by whom has this rule been insulted, and by whom has it been violated? Tell me, O illustrious one, while I stand here as the guardian of dharma. (45)
Durvāsas said: O Madhusūdana, having recognized through my knowledge that this was the Tīrtha of Liberation, I went with great joy on a pilgrimage to the Cakratīrtha to bathe.
While I was still unwashed from my bath, I was seen by the invincible Daityas; I was seized by the neck, O Kṛṣṇa, and likewise struck with their fists.
Having forcibly seized my garments and the *kuśa* grass along with the unbroken rice grains (*akṣata*), he threw them into the water and, grasping my feet, pulled me toward himself.
Having cast me onto the edge of the boundary, those lowest of Dānavas said: "If you come here again, we shall kill you; of this there is no doubt. (49)
"I have bathed at Cakratīrtha, O Lord, and I shall now take my meal; therefore, O Govinda, bathe me and make my religious observance fruitful."
"By your grace, having bathed and eaten with a joyful mind, I shall fulfill my vow and wander this earth. (51)

Thus ends the eighteenth chapter, titled "The Description of the Account of the Defeat of Durvāsas by the Rākṣasa," within the "Māhātmya of Cakratīrtha" in the "Māhātmya of Dvārakā," the fourth section of the seventh book, the Prabhāsakhaṇḍa, of the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a compendium of eighty-one thousand verses. || 18 ||
Prahlāda said: Having heard that and having reflected again and again, the Lord of the gods spoke these words there to the sinless Durvāsas.

The Blessed Lord said: "O best of Brahmins, I am dependent on others; I have been purchased by your devotion and not otherwise. I am indeed a follower of Bali's commands and remain under the control of the lord of the Daityas."
Therefore, O best of Brahmins, entreat Bali, the son of Virocana; at his command, I shall now do whatever you desire.
Having heard those words, the brahmin quickly spoke to Bali: "You are the most excellent among sacrificers, and you are considered the greatest among givers."
You are the shore beyond and the shore near for compassion; show mercy toward me! O illustrious one, dispatch the Lord for the suppression of the Daityas.
"By your grace, I shall become one who has bathed and whose observances are complete. Hearing those words, the Daitya, his mind not at all delighted, then said this to Durvāsas: "It will not be so."
"O best of Brahmins, request anything else that dwells in your mind; I shall grant it without a doubt, even if it should be very difficult to obtain."
O twice-born one, I would even give up my own self, but I shall not abandon Hari; how could I forsake Keśava, whom I have obtained through many meritorious deeds?
Durvāsas said: "Know that I am not excessively greedy; what else do I request? O Daitya, protect my life and send Janārdana to me."
Bali said: "O Brahmin, you know how Hiraṇyākṣa was struck down, and how [Viṣṇu], having become the Sacrificial Boar, forcibly held up the earth in the heavens."
And just as the all-pervading Lord, in the form of Narasiṃha, slew Hiraṇyakaśipu—the foremost of the Daityas who was incapable of being slain by the Daityas and Dānavas. || 11 ||
In the same way, Viṣṇu, the best of gods, slew Vṛtra, the demon Namuci, and the one known as the Lord of Laṅkā by means of his illusory power for the sake of the gods.
First, having become a dwarf, he indeed begged for three paces of land; then, becoming Trivikrama, he took away my worlds.
If, by the power of my merit, Viṣṇu should somehow be obtained by me, I shall not abandon the Lord of the World, the Master who assumed the illusory form of Vāmana. (14)
Durvāsas said: "I shall not eat without bathing at the confluence of the Gomatī and the ocean; if you do not send Hari, then I shall cast off this body."
Bali said: "Let that which is destined to be happen; do as you know best. I shall not relinquish these two steps, which are bowed to by Brahmā, Rudra, and Indra. (16)
Then, seeing those two disputing, that Lord of the Universe, the God who is kind to Brahmins, spoke with compassion to that Brahmin.
"Be at ease, O best of the twice-born; I shall bathe you there without a doubt, after I have slain all the hosts of Daityas at the confluence of the Gomatī and the ocean. (18)
Prahlāda said: Having heard the words of the Blessed One regarding the brahmin, the king of the Daityas then fell at his feet and firmly grasped them.
Then, having placed his feet upon Bali, the Lord Viṣṇu—holding the conch, discus, and mace in his hands—attained prosperity, accompanied by Durvāsas.
Seeing Durvāsas and Janārdana then setting out, the infinite Puruṣa went forth, as did the wielder of the club and the one whose weapon is the plow.
Muśalī went ahead, and then Viṣṇu Trivikrama followed; O brahmins, Durvāsas followed after them outside the surface of the earth.
Having pierced through the netherworld (rasātala), they all rose up with great haste and appeared right there at the confluence of the Gomatī and the ocean.
Then Saṃkarṣaṇa and Janārdana, both equipped with firm bows, said to that brahmin: "Perform your bath as you please."
Having heard their words, the twice-born man performed his bath with haste; having bathed, he began to perform his necessary daily rites.

Thus ends the nineteenth chapter, titled "The Description of the Rules for Durvāsas’s Daily Rites, including His Bath and Other Duties," following the Meeting of Kṛṣṇa, Balarāma, and Durvāsas at Cakratīrtha, within the Dvārakāmāhātmya, the fourth section of the Prabhāsakhaṇḍa, in the seventh part of the Śrī Skanda Mahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses.
Prahlāda said: Then, hearing the sound of the Vedic chanting, the Dānava Durmukha, his eyes bloodshot with anger, spoke thus to Durvāsas.
"O twice-born one, if you were indeed released while being struck by us, why have you returned again to meet your death, O evil-minded one? (2)
Having spoken thus, that lowest of Dānavas rushed forward to strike with his fist; as he was running toward him, Durvāsas, the best of sages, spoke to him.
"Do not touch me, O most sinful one, for I am a brahmin who has performed his daily rites. Seeing that dānava intent on killing the brahmin, Viṣṇu [intervened]. (13)
Then, enraged on account of Durvāsas, the Lord of the World effortlessly severed his head with a razor-edged discus.
Prahlāda said: Having seen Durmukha slain, the Dānava Duḥsaha then cried out loudly to the sons of Diti, "Come quickly! (6)
Then, having heard that Durmukha had been slain and that Durvāsas had again been rescued there by Viṣṇu, all the hosts of Daityas [were struck with fear].
Kūrmapṛṣṭha, Golaka, Krodhana, Vedadūṣaka, Yajñaghna, Yajñahantṛ, Dharmāntaka, and Tapasvin—these eight were born here. (8)
These and many others, with various weapons in their hands and eyes bloodshot with rage, were likewise cursing the Brahmin.
Then, having surrounded Ātreya, Viṣṇu, and Saṃkarṣaṇa with javelins, slings, maces, and *bhuśuṇḍi* weapons, [they attacked].
Overwhelmed by rage, they fought with various kinds of missiles; Viṣṇu was surrounded on all sides by the Dānavas, who were terrible to behold.
And Saṃkarṣaṇa shone like the moon and the sun amidst clouds, having taken up two divine bows and quickly fixed swift arrows to them.
In that great battle, those two struck the Daityas with volleys of arrows; being slaughtered in the conflict by Viṣṇu, they fled in all directions.
Seeing the Dānavas fleeing and others slain by Viṣṇu, Golaka and Kūrmapṛṣṭha took heart and turned back.
Golaka struck Saṃkarṣaṇa with three arrows; seeing Ananta distressed, Golaka became overwhelmed with rage. || 15 ||
Springing up with speed, he struck Durvāsas on the head; beaten by that blow of the fist, he fell to the ground and cried out.
But Saṃkarṣaṇa, seeing him fallen and struck upon the head, became enraged at the sight; the Lord cried out, "Stay! Stay! and seizing his club, the hero slew the enemy in battle.
Struck on the head with a club, the ball, its faculties impaired, fell down with its skull shattered and died. || 18 ||
Seeing the fallen Golaka and the weeping Brāhmaṇa, as well as Kūrmapṛṣṭha, the Blessed Viṣṇu set his mind upon killing them; he struck the enemy in the heart with a very sharp iron arrow.

Struck by Viṣṇu’s arrow, he abandoned his weapon and fled. When that exceedingly powerful one had been pierced and had departed on the back of the tortoise, the entire army was shattered and scattered in the ten directions.
Standing at the gate, he reported to Kuśa, the king of the Daityas, that the entire army led by Tatprabhagra and Golaka had been slain.
Hearing that Golaka had been slain, as well as the other Daityas, the king of the Daityas commanded his warriors and the troops of his own army to prepare for battle.
Having received Kuśa’s command, all the Daityas, Pañcajana and the others, set out for battle on chariots and elephants, facing him directly. || 23 ||
An army of ten thousand set out from Kūrmapṛṣṭha; likewise, there were twenty thousand chariots and ten thousand elephants.
Ten times ten thousand horses and likewise camels [were there]; and the Daitya Baka went forth accompanied by a vast army.

Likewise, the Daitya Dīrghanakha, surrounded by his own army, and the son of the minister of Kuśa, the king of the Daityas, who was a great master of illusion, as well as the Daitya Vighasa and the very powerful Praghasa, went forth. || 26 ||
With upraised arms and a crooked head, clad in a tunic and accompanied by jackals, he was the Daitya Rāhu, the slayer of Brahmins, the destroyer of sacrifices, and likewise Barbaraka.
Sunāman and Vasunāman were his two ministers, supreme in intelligence; Ugradaṃṣṭra was his commander-in-chief, and Mahāhanu was his brother.
These and many other Daityas, filled with wrath and desiring battle, went forth with the great roar of chariots.

Having bathed, wearing white garments and adorned with white garlands, Kuśa worshipped Śambhu, the Great God, the imperishable Lord of Bhavānī, the Sovereign of all beings, with supreme meditative concentration.
Having bathed him with the five nectars (pañcāmṛta) and likewise anointed him with perfumes, the lord of the Daityas worshipped him with heaps of many kinds of flowers.
Having worshipped Mahādeva with the sounds of songs and musical instruments as well as auspicious recitations, and having had the Brāhmaṇas pronounce blessings, [he should proceed].
Having adorned her with ornaments, including decorations of jewels and diamonds, and with a crown the color of the sun, blazing with the radiance of the sun; || 33 ||
The king of the Daityas, shining and exceedingly adorned with a necklace, having equipped himself, the mighty-armed one looked toward his charioteer.
He spoke these words to his two ministers, Sunāmā and Vasu: "Who is this that slays the asuras, and for what purpose? Let it be found out. (35)
Having heard those words of his, Ruru spoke these words: "Indeed, on the day after tomorrow, a brahmin is to go to bathe at the confluence of the Gomatī. (36)
O Lord of the Earth, having arrived there, he was obstructed by the Daityas; then Viṣṇu, accompanied by Saṃkarṣaṇa, was summoned by him.
O great king, that Lord of the Universe, who is devoted to Brahmanas, slays us; by him many Daityas have been killed and some have fled. || 38 ||
Sunāman said: "O King, let this brahmin go after he has bathed, accompanied by Vāsudeva. What is the use of a futile conflict? Tell us. (39)
Having heard those words of his, Kuśa was filled with rage and said, "How shall I not slay Keśava, the killer of Golaka? (40)
Having spoken thus, the enraged lord of the Daityas then departed, accompanied by the sounds of musical instruments and the beating of kettledrums.
There he beheld the Lord of Gods, the thousand-headed Sovereign, as well as Viṣṇu, who holds the discus in his hand, and the sinless Durvāsas.
Seeing that he was a portion of Īśvara, [the sage] thought, "This lord must not be slain. Then, with Viṣṇu in mind, he incited all those Dānavas.
They surrounded him on all sides with elephants resembling mountains, with chariots like clouds, and with horses of great speed.
Then a battle took place between the two gods and the dānavas; at that time, the hosts of gods saw those two covered by the daityas.
Then, seizing his mace and plow, the powerful wielder of the plow struck down the foremost of the Daityas, who were like the fire of cosmic destruction or Yama himself.
Being struck by that powerful Bala, those Daityas fled in all directions; broken and shattered, they then sought refuge with Kuśa alone.
Baka, Yajñakopa, Brahmaghna, Vedadūṣaka, Mahāmakhaghna, Jambha, Rāhu, and likewise Vakraśiras; || 48 ||
These and many other eminent and supreme Dānavas, their eyes bloodshot with rage, pierced Janārdana.
Then Saṃkarṣaṇa and Janārdana, filled with wrath, struck down the foremost of the Dānavas with blows from their discus and plow.
With his discus, he swiftly severed Baka’s head from his body, and with his mace, he crushed the destroyer of the sacrifice to pieces.
He struck Rāhu with his discus and others with his mace; thus slain and being struck down, they fled broken in the ten directions.
Seeing his own army thus routed and slaughtered, Kuśa, his eyes bloodshot with rage, said to his charioteer, "Go! (53)
Having approached them and announced his own name, he said: "O wielder of the mace, who are you that slays the sons of Diti before me?"
Śrī Vāsudeva said: "Because this meritorious confluence of the Gomatī and the ocean, which bestows liberation, has been obstructed by wicked evildoers, therefore they have been slain by me."
Kuśa said: "Do you not know me standing here? How will you depart while still alive? Stand firm and fight; then you shall give up your life."

Having spoken thus, he struck Keśava with twenty-five arrows and Ananta with eight; then, having observed Atri’s son and seeing that he was a portion of the Lord (Īśvara), he said, "Go, do not delay! (57)
With all his limbs pierced by arrows, he drew the Śārṅga, the best of bows, and struck down the four horses with four shafts.
With a crescent-shaped arrow he severed the head of the charioteer from his body; with one [arrow] he cut his bow, and with another he cut down his banner.
With his bow broken, deprived of his chariot, his horses slain, and his charioteer killed, he then seized a great sword and spoke these words.
If I were to strike you down, my fame would indeed be incomparable; but if I am struck down by you, O hero, I shall go to the supreme destination.
"Stay, stay, O Hari! Sadāśiva is my refuge in this place. Seeing him running toward him, exceedingly enraged and with a sword in hand, he effortlessly severed his head with a sharp-edged discus.
Then, seeing that Dānava fallen on the ground with his head severed, the Daitya Khañjanaka likewise spoke from his chariot in the battle.
When the Daitya Kuśa had fled, Viṣṇu and Saṃkarṣaṇa, accompanied by Durvāsas, then returned filled with joy.
Having cast the kuśa grass that had fallen into the temple of Śiva, the Dānava gratified him with baths, perfumes, worship, incense, songs, and instrumental music.
And by the grace of Śaṅkara, he immediately regained his life; then that Daitya rose up, crying out, "Śiva! Śiva! (66).
Then, seeing that Daitya restored to life, the host of Daityas spoke these words with joyful minds: "O Lord, may you prosper for a very long time! (67)
If, after having caused him to bathe, you then turn back the Brahmin, let him go as he pleases; what is the use of this futile conflict of yours?
Having heard those words of his, Kuśa spoke these words: "Go, send those two quickly, for they are both protectors of the Brahmins. (69)
And having been thus commanded by the king, O best of sages, Sumanas bowed down to Viṣṇu and paid homage to Halāyudha, and then spoke.
"I have been sent to your presence by Kuśa, O Janārdana. What offense has been committed against you, O Lord, that you wish to slay the Daityas? (71)
"Having bathed Durvāsas, go; you are liberated, O giver of honor! Know that immortality has indeed been obtained from Mahādeva by Kuśa. (72)
Śrī Viṣṇu said: "This holy place of liberation has been obstructed by you, evildoers; therefore, I shall slay all the Dānavas—of this there is no doubt. (73)
"Furthermore, bring back those darbha grasses, sesame seeds, and unbroken grains belonging to Durvāsas which were cast into the abode of Varuṇa. (74)
Together with your vehicles, retinues, kinsmen, families, and relatives, leave this holy pilgrimage site and enter into the depths of the earth. (75)
Having heard those words, Sumanas, his eyes bloodshot with rage, said to him, "Fight! This shall not be so. (76)
He related to Kuśa what had been said by the wielder of the Śārṅga bow; and having heard those words uttered by the minister, he became enraged. (77)
Mounting his chariot, the subduer of enemies went with speed to fight, while mentally recollecting the god who wields the Pināka bow and has the bull as his emblem.
Then there commenced a most great battle, hair-raising, between the other Dānavas and Keśava and Kuśa.
Yajñaghna struck Saṃkarṣaṇa with a heavy mace; struck on the head by Saṃkarṣaṇa with a club, he fell down.
The Blessed Lord Hari swiftly struck down Kañcuka with his discus; then Ulmuka was slain and Brahmaghna was felled.
"These and many others have indeed been slain by Keśava. Seeing the Dānavas fallen, Kuśa was filled with supreme rage.
Enraged in battle, he struck Keśava with a supreme weapon; the Blessed Lord, filled with wrath, severed his head with his discus.
Seeing him with his head severed and fallen upon the ground, Keśava likewise cut his arms and feet into pieces as small as sesame seeds with his sword.
Then, seeing Kuśa slain in pieces by Keśava, all those demons gathered him up and carried him to the abode of Śiva.
By the grace of the Wielder of the Trident, the Dānava immediately regained his life; rising up suddenly in a rage, he cried out, "Where is Viṣṇu? (86)
Raising his mace in great rage, he came to fight Janārdana; seeing him with mace uplifted, [Janārdana] considered his life as already slain and restored once more.
He then said to Durvāsas: "Why does this not die, even though its head has been cut off by me repeatedly and reduced to pieces like sesame seeds?"
"Tell us, for what reason and by what means does this man live?"—having been addressed thus, that best of sages reflected through meditation.
Having understood the entire cause of that matter, he said to Madhusūdana: "By the gratified Mahādeva, this Kuśa has been made immortal."
Even though he was cut into pieces, he was not deprived of his life; thereupon, overcome with wonder, [the king thought], "How is it that he must be slain by me? (91)
"I shall employ a means by which he shall not come to be. Then, having regained his life through the grace of Śaṃkara, he took up his shield and sword and cried out, "Stay! Stay! (92).
Then, seeing Kuśa—who was protected by Śiva—approaching, he struck Kuśa, who held a mace in his hand, with a heavy mace.
Struck by Keśava, he fell with his head shattered; seizing Kuśa as he lay prostrate on the ground with force, Hari [acted]. 94.
Having cast that body into a pit, Janārdana indeed filled it up once more; he then installed a Liṅga upon its site.
Having regained consciousness, that demon saw the Śiva-linga situated upon him, and he then became lost in thought.

Thus ends the twentieth chapter, titled "The Description of Viṣṇu’s Installation of a Śiva Liṅga upon the Rākṣasa Kuśa during the Battle between the Rākṣasa Kuśa and Viṣṇu at Cakratīrtha," in the Dvārakāmāhātmya, the fourth section of the Prabhāsakhaṇḍa, within the Skanda Mahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses. || 20 ||
Śrī Prahlāda said: "The Śiva-liṅga is indeed inviolable; I have been slain intentionally. O sinless one, the demon said to Kṛṣṇa, 'I have been deceived by you.'"
Śrī Viṣṇu said: "I am well-pleased with you, O Daitya, because of your heroism and your refuge in Śiva. Choose a boon—blessings be upon you—if there is anything you desire, O high-minded one."
Kuśa said: "O Hari, just as Mahādeva is worthy of my worship, so are you; you are one and the same being in two forms. Therefore, I choose you. (3)
O Lord, this Śivaliṅga which has been installed by you upon me—let it be known as Kuśeśvara, after my name. || 4 ||
"If I am to be favored by you, let this fame be mine. Having been told, "It shall be so," the asura remained right there.
Then, on another occasion, Mādhava dispatched all the Dānavas; some had gone to the subterranean realm (rasātala), while others had approached Viṣṇu.
Ananta is established there, and Viṣṇu is situated immediately thereafter; having recognized that this holy ford (tīrtha) bestows liberation, Durvāsas, the foremost among sages, [arrived].
At Gomati and at Cakratīrtha resides the Lord Trivikrama; considering it to be a bestower of liberation because of that, Durvāsas has established himself there.
Thus the Lord Trivikrama remained established from that time forward; however, in the Kali age, the Lord again attained the state of Kṛṣṇa through the manifestation of his portions.

Prahlāda said: O brāhmaṇas, listen with well-concentrated minds to the procedure for the worship of Hari; it is declared that when worshipped specifically during the months of Madhu and Mādhava, He bestows special fruits.
The man who, in Dvāravatī, makes an image of Madhusūdanī and worships Lord Kṛṣṇa, having bathed and anointed him; || 11 ||
Having covered it with perfumes and garments, and with various kinds of incense and lamps, as well as with food offerings, ornaments, betel-leaf, and fruit. || 12 ||

Having worshipped with the *ārārtika* ritual and prostrated like a staff, one should offer a lamp fed with ghee and likewise perform a night vigil with songs, musical instruments, and readers of sacred texts.
And having performed this rite with devotion, one shall obtain all desires. || 14 ||

Likewise, by worshipping [the deity] in the sky and performing the offering of the sacred thread (pavitrāropaṇa), there shall be inexhaustible satisfaction for the ancestors, and their desires shall be fulfilled.
O best of the twice-born, when the day of awakening arrives in the month of Kārtika, one who worships Kṛṣṇa, the Lord of Gods, shall attain the supreme goal.
Likewise, by worshipping in the month of Nabhasya with the offering of the sacred thread (pavitrāropaṇa), one attains all desires and goes to the world of Viṣṇu. || 17 ||

And having worshipped [the Lord] at the beginnings of the Yugas, during the southern and northern solstices, in the months of Āṣāḍha, Jyeṣṭha, and Māgha, and on the twelfth days (dvādaśīs) beginning with Pauṣa; || 18 ||
In the Kali age, by worshipping Kṛṣṇa at the confluence of the Gomatī and the ocean, one attains the stainless world, having gone to which one does not grieve.

Thus ends the twenty-first chapter, titled "Description of the Majesty of the Worship of the Blessed Lord in the Sacred Field Situated on the Banks of the Gomatī," within the Dvārakā-māhātmya, the fourth section of the Prabhāsa-khaṇḍa, in the seventh part of the Śrī Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a compendium of eighty-one thousand verses.

Śrī Prahlāda said: Listen, O tigers among the twice-born, as I relate it to you exactly as it is. Having bathed the Lord of the World, having likewise anointed him with fragrant pastes, having worshipped him with Tulasī, and having adorned him with ornaments— || 1 ||
Having gratified [the deity] with food offerings and likewise with the waving of lights (nīrājana) and other rites, one should worship Durvāsas as well as the lotus-eyed Lord (Puṇḍarīkākṣa).
Having worshipped Ananta, Vainateya, and the others with devotion, a person should give gifts according to his own capacity, free from any stinginess regarding wealth.
And there he should satisfy those who have sought his protection—the wretched, the blind, and the miserable.
Then a man should go to Rukmiṇī, the daughter of Vidarbha, having presented offerings along with oblations, perfumes, and lamps.
Planets continue to afflict and diseases continue to overcome men as long as they do not behold the beloved of Kṛṣṇa with devotion in the Kali age.
In the Kali age, a person does not perceive the fear of calamities nor the suffering born of living beings, as long as they possess devotion to the beloved of Kṛṣṇa.
A man shall remain poor, miserable, and indeed a constant beggar for as long as he does not behold the beloved of Kṛṣṇa with devotion during the Kali age.
As long as a woman does not behold the beloved of Kṛṣṇa with devotion, she remains unfortunate, joined with suffering, and her offspring will die.
As long as a man in the Kali age does not behold the beloved of Kṛṣṇa with devotion, he shall experience fear of enemies, the ruin of his home, and folly.
Having worshipped Kṛṣṇa according to the prescribed rites, one should then worship Rukmiṇī; one should bathe her with curd and milk, as well as with honey and sugar.
Having bathed [the deity] with ghee, various perfumes, as well as sugarcane juice and water from sacred fords (tīrtha), one shall obtain all desires.
Thus, for whoever bathes the goddess Rukmiṇī, the beloved of Kṛṣṇa, nothing whatsoever is difficult to attain in this world or in the next.
One who is childless should likewise anoint [the image] with sandalwood paste, saffron, and musk; he will certainly obtain a son. (14)
He shall always be an enjoyer of pleasures, handsome, and honored by people; he should worship with *mālatī* flowers and fragrant *śatapatra* blossoms. (15)
With *karavīra* flowers, with *mallikā*s, and especially with *campaka*s; with water-born lotuses, with *ketakī*s, and with *pāṭala*s. (16)
One should worship with agallochum incense and indeed with guggulu resin, as well as with very soft, pure garments originating from various lands. (17)
Having respectfully covered Vaidarbhī Rukmiṇī, the beloved of Kṛṣṇa, he should adorn the goddess with ornaments endowed with precious gems.

In that family there shall be no one who is unhappy, nor unrighteous, nor likewise destitute; nor shall there be anyone childless, nor engaged in forbidden acts, nor a gambler, nor a servant of the lowly.

Those men who, in the Kali age, worship Rukmiṇī, the Mother of the World, with offerings of food—both solid and soft—and with the thought, "May the Goddess be pleased with me," should devoutly offer her betel-leaf mixed with camphor.
And having taken a bright fruit together with unbroken grains (akṣata), O brahmins, one should indeed offer the arghya according to the rule with this mantra: || 21 ||
O beloved of Kṛṣṇa, salutations to you, daughter of the lord of Vidarbha; O Goddess who grants all desires, accept this arghya, obeisance be to you.
Then, filled with meditative visualization, one should perform the *ārārtika* rite, and the *nīrājana* ceremony should be performed, especially with camphor. (23)
Having placed water in a conch shell, one should whirl it about with a devout mind; having whirled it, it should be held over the head for the sake of purification.
O twice-born ones, one should prostrate on the ground like a staff, saying, "Salutation to Kṛṣṇa’s beloved," and should worship the wives and the brahmins according to one's ability.
Having worshipped with necklaces, threads, vermilion, garments, and bodices, as well as with fragrant flowers, and having anointed [the image] with saffron; || 26 ||
One should satisfy [the deity] with saffron-dyed garments, collyrium, and betel-leaf; and with various kinds of foods to chew and eat, sweetmeats, sugarcane, honey, and clarified butter.
Keśava, the lord of the gods, becomes pleased together with Rukmiṇī; O best of the twice-born, fruits should especially be offered here.
Then one should worship the gatekeeper deity Unmattaka, having bathed him with fragrant water and anointed him with saffron.

Having fumigated [the deity] with incense, one should worship thoroughly with flowers and other offerings, as well as with food offerings consisting of various kinds of eatables and drinks, meat, and liquor.
And with abundant offerings and various kinds of flour-based sweets, one should worship the sixty-four Yoginīs at that sacred seat (pīṭha). || 31 ||
One should worship Hara-siddhi and Kṣetrapāla in every way, as well as Virūpasvāminī there and likewise the Seven Mothers.
One should worship the eight forms of Kṛṣṇa’s wives upon that pedestal: Rukmiṇī, Satyabhāmā, the auspicious Jāmbavatī, and likewise [Nāgnajitī, Mitravindā, Lakṣmaṇā, and Kālindī].
And there one should worship Mitravindā, Kālindī, Bhadrā Nāgnajitī, and Lakṣmaṇā as the eighth—these beloved wives of Kṛṣṇa. (34)

Having worshipped these according to the prescribed rite and having gratified them with curd and milk-rice, one should do so amidst the sound of singing and musical instruments, with lamps, and by keeping a vigil.
Endowed with sons and grandsons, and possessed of wealth and grain, he attains all his desires; Viṣṇu is pleased with him. (36)
What is the use of his many gifts, or likewise what use are vows and restraints, for him by whom Rukmiṇī, the Mother of the World and beloved of Kṛṣṇa, has been seen?
What need has he for many sacrifices accompanied by abundant sacrificial fees, by whom Rukmiṇī, the mother of the world and beloved of Kṛṣṇa, has been seen? (38)
By him has been given, by him has been offered in sacrifice, and by him has been recited the eternal mantra, by whom Rukmiṇī, the Mother of the World and beloved of Kṛṣṇa, has been seen. (39)
By him the eight supernatural powers (siddhis) were attained with ease, of this there is no doubt; for he went to Dvāravatī and beheld the beloved of Keśava.
His life is fruitful and his desires are fulfilled by one who, in the Kali age, goes to Kṛṣṇa’s city and beholds the beloved of Mādhava. (41)
O King, what is the use of sovereignty or even the state of liberation for one who has not beheld Rukmiṇī, the Mother of the World and beloved of Kṛṣṇa? 42.
Therefore, with every effort, Rukmiṇī, the beloved of Kṛṣṇa, who grants all desires, should always be worshipped and beheld by human beings. (43)
Especially during the Navarātra in the month of Āśvina, she should always be worshipped; for those men by whom the beloved of Hari is worshipped on the ninth day, [they attain their desires]. (41)

When she is gratified with baths, perfumes, and the like, with garments, abundant offerings, the sound of singing and instrumental music, and with lamps and keeping vigil, the daughter of Bhīṣmaka grants all desires.
Likewise, on the fourteenth day of the festival of lamps, one who worships with a concentrated mind according to the scriptures obtains the desired fruit. (46)

Those by whom the mother of Kandarpa is worshipped on the eighth day of the bright fortnight of the month of Māgha with perfumes, flowers, and various offerings—their life has become fruitful and their desires have been fulfilled. (47)
Those men who, during the month of Madhava (Caitra), behold the goddess Rukmiṇī on the twelfth day of the dark fortnight going together with Kṛṣṇa—they are the blessed ones on earth.
Endowed with sons and grandsons, possessed of wealth and grain, and free from disease during their lives, they go to the state that is beyond all ailment.
Those men by whom the beloved of Kṛṣṇa is worshipped on the eighth day of the month of Jyeṣṭha shall attain the fulfillment of their desires; of this there is no doubt.
Likewise, those men by whom the worship of the Mother is performed in the month of Bhādrapada go to the abode of Viṣṇu, completely liberated from all sins.
Those men who behold Rukmiṇī together with Kṛṣṇa on the twelfth day of the month of Kārttika—for them, no fear exists anywhere.

He who beholds Rukmiṇī joined with Kṛṣṇa as they stand together in one place—his life is truly fruitful, his lineage of sons is imperishable, his wealth and grain are inexhaustible, and he shall never know poverty. (53)
Whoever should thus behold Rukmiṇī, the beloved of Kṛṣṇa, and worship her, being liberated from all sins, goes to the world of Viṣṇu.

O twice-born ones, whatever merit and fruit arises in this world for one who bathes in all the holy fords and gives gifts according to his capacity—all that has been explained in its entirety regarding the Kali age during the presence of Kṛṣṇa.

"O Brahmins, in the Kali age, liberation cannot be attained except through Dvārāvatī. He who bound Bali composed this Purāṇa-saṃhitā; O best of the twice-born, he formerly gave it to me out of his grace. (56)
And on this matter, O best of the twice-born, an ancient history was previously told in a conversation between Pradyumna and the high-souled Mārkaṇḍeya.
Mārkaṇḍeya said: O Indradyumna, learn from me the greatness of Dvārakā, where the Lord of Rukmiṇī, the destroyer of afflictions, dwells during the Kali age. || 1 ||
In this Kali age, those who hear or recite the majesty of Kṛṣṇa shall not dwell in the world of Yama for eight yugas.
O King, for him whose discourse concerning Kṛṣṇa is always dearer than his own life, nothing whatsoever in this world or the next is difficult to attain.
The fruit that is obtained by residing in Kāśī for thousands of Manvantaras is attained by those dwelling in Dvārakā for five days.
"Whoever, even if he be an outcaste (śvapaca), dwells in Dvārakā during the Kali age, attains the goal of ascetics; so indeed has Prajāpati declared. (5)
The man who daily performs [this rite] for one desiring to go to Dvārakā obtains the fruit arising from Kurukṣetra.
Whatever fruit has been declared for the eclipse of the moon and whatever fruit for the Lord of the Moon (Somanāyaka), one obtains that same fruit by beholding Janārdana at Dvāravatī.
The fruit that is obtained by performing the Kārttikī festival at Puṣkara over ten million years is produced by residing in Dvārakā for a single day.
When the Son of Devakī is beheld in Dvārakā in a single day, the fruit should be known as ten millionfold; here, it arises from a hundred lakhs.
O King, for those dwelling in the Kali age, their desires are blessed: the constant longing for a vision of Kṛṣṇa and the resolve to go to Dvārakā. (10)
O best of kings, O ruler of the earth, listen to the fruit obtained by one who observes even a single Dvādaśī in the presence of Kṛṣṇa at Dvārakā. || 11 ||
Blessed are they, fulfilled are they, and those people are purifiers of the world, by whom the face of Kṛṣṇa has been seen—that which destroys tens of millions upon tens of millions of sins.
Whatever fruit is obtained through days joined with vows and associated with Kṛṣṇa, or through great sacrifices and gifts, that same fruit is gained by staying for even a single day in Dvārakā.
For those men who perform a milk-bath upon the head of Kṛṣṇa, it is remembered that for every single drop, the merit born of a hundred horse-sacrifices is attained.
Curd is ten times [the value] of milk; ghee is ten times more than curd; honey is ten times the value of ghee; and that which follows honey is ten times its value. (15)
O best of kings, there is water with flowers, water with gems, and the Vardhana water; likewise, there is water with mantras and water with perfumes. || 16 ||
O King, bathing with sugarcane juice is equal to performing a hundred horse-sacrifices; likewise, the water of a sacred ford yields that same fruit.
If one wipes with a cloth Kṛṣṇa, whose body is wet from bathing, there shall be the wiping away of even that sin acquired through hundreds of thousands [of births]. || 18 ||
Having bathed the Lord of the World, one who performs the descent of the flower garland obtains the fruit of ten thousand gold niṣkas for every single flower.
If one sounds the conch and other instruments at the time of the deity's bath, he dwells in the world of Brahmā for the duration of a day of Brahmā.
At the time of bathing, he should recite the Thousand Names of Kṛṣṇa; for every syllable, he shall obtain the merit arising from a hundred beloved tawny cows.
O protector of the earth, this fruit of the Gītā has been proclaimed; it is likewise celebrated through the liberation of Gajendra by means of this King of Hymns.
O lord of men, by means of other hymns composed by sages that are recited, the Lord of Gods attains satisfaction and grants all desires. (23)
Furthermore, O Leader of Men, the merit that one who recites the Vedas at the time of his ceremonial bath obtains is not known [to us]. (24)
