And when the time for bathing has arrived, there shall be dancing before Kṛṣṇa, as well as singing and the recitation of hymns of praise with the mouth. (25)
At the time of Kṛṣṇa’s bath, whoever utters the cry of "Victory! and performs song and dance accompanied by the clapping of hands— || 26 ||
If, while performing movements therein, one laughs or even speaks, he has escaped from that supreme confinement of the mother’s womb. (27)
O Lord of Men, he who recites the virtues of Kṛṣṇa at the time of his ritual bathing does not sleep on his back in his mother’s lap.
He who anoints Kṛṣṇa with fragrant saffron mixed with sandalwood and aguru, along with camphor and musk, shall dwell for a kalpa in the abode of Viṣṇu together with his ancestors.
O Indradyumna, each of these, beginning with sandalwood, is not otherwise; they are produced in various regions and consist of very soft, excellent cloths.
The person who, having first offered fragrant incense, then offers incense [to Hari], dwells in the abode of Hari for as many Manvantaras as there are incense sticks. || 31 ||
And according to their own capacity, they adorn the Lord of the Gods with ornaments made of incomparable gold and beautiful, radiant jewels.
O Great King, Rudra and Vāsava and the others are the fruit of those [deeds]. || 33 ||

The sages know this, with the sole exception of Mādhava: those who worship Kṛṣṇa, the Lord of the Universe and the remover of the impurities of the Kali age, with ketakī and tulasī leaves, or with flowers produced from jasmine.
O King, tiger among men, each single flower from those various abundant blossoms produced in that region is considered equal to the Rājasūya sacrifice. (35)
Those men who perform worship of the Lord of Rukmiṇī according to their ability, those men sport in the world of Viṣṇu for a hundred Manvantaras.
Furthermore, whoever worships Kṛṣṇa, the son of Devakī, with faith using tulasī leaves together with tender flower-clusters; || 37 ||

That destination which belongs to those disciplined in yoga, that destination which belongs to those adorned with yoga, that destination which belongs to those of generous character, and that destination which belongs to those who frequent sacred fords; || 38 ||
Whatever goal is attained by those devoted to their mothers who observe the twelfth day free from transgression, keeping a vigil for Viṣṇu while dancing and singing—that is the fruit [of this]. (39)
Whatever fruit belongs to the devotees of Viṣṇu who are exponents of the Vedas, that same fruit belongs to those who read the Vaiṣṇava scripture and to those who bestow it upon other Vaiṣṇavas.
O protector of the earth, Kṛṣṇa, the husband of Rukmiṇī, when worshipped with a garland of Tulasī, bestows this fruit; of this there is no doubt.
Just as Lakṣmī is dear to Viṣṇu, Tulasī is even more so; born specifically in Dvārakā, she is especially rich in fruit.
Wherever Viṣṇu is situated, when worshipped with a garland of tulasī leaves, he bestows in the Kali age a merit equal to that of Dvārakā.
O King, whoever worships Kṛṣṇa, the remover of the impurities of the Kali age, with ketakī leaves, he receives the fruit of an Aśvamedha sacrifice for every single leaf.
Whoever worships Kṛṣṇa, the Lord of the three worlds, with mālatī flowers—there is no doubt that he has obtained that fruit which is difficult even for Hari to attain. (45)
He who worships the Lord of Rukmiṇī with flowers blooming during their proper seasons attains all desires that are difficult for both gods and humans to obtain.
In the Kali age, O King of kings, those who burn black agallochum along with camphor for Kṛṣṇa become equal to Kṛṣṇa himself.
Having incensed Janārdana with fragrant guggulu resin mixed with clarified butter, a person goes to the state of eternal Śiva.
O protector of the earth, he who offers a lamp before Kṛṣṇa casts off all sin and attains a station that is of the nature of light.
Indeed, he who constantly offers a garland of lamps at the gate of Kṛṣṇa shall obtain the fruit of sovereignty over the seven islands in each and every island. || 50 ||
One should present delightful food offerings to Kṛṣṇa; indeed, for that reason, the satisfaction of one's ancestors remains eternal until the end of the kalpa.
O Lord of Men, for him who bestows agreeable fruits upon a friend, his desires shall indeed bear fruit until the end of the eon. || 52 ||
O leader of men, he who indeed offers betel-leaf with camphor and areca nut to Kṛṣṇa attains the world whose deity is Agni.
One should place a water-pot filled with water and containing a pomegranate in front of Kṛṣṇa; even at the end of the kalpa, the ancestors have no need for water.
Then, O king of kings, with great devotion he provides a protective barrier against the wind for the God of gods by means of a fan, a cloth, or the breeze itself. (59)
In that family there is no one more sinful, nor in the world of Yama; O protector of the earth, from the world of Vāyu there is no further destination.
He who creates a pavilion of flowers with incense in the abode of Kṛṣṇa sports in heaven with ten million Puṣpaka celestial chariots.
The Lord of Gods indeed kisses upon his own mouth the head of that man who pleases Kṛṣṇa with the wind from a moving chowrie.
He who constructs a temple for Kṛṣṇa adorned with plantain pillars dwells in the world of the Sun for as long as the earth endures.
He who offers incense and garlands of sandalwood in the abode of Kṛṣṇa is served by hundreds of thousands of celestial maidens and the leaders of the gods.
Whoever, out of devotion, raises a banner atop a temple shall dwell in the abode of Brahmā and sport together with Brahmā.
He adorns the courtyard of the God of gods with decorative patterns and auspicious svastikas; thus he sports within the three worlds.
He who offers a heap of flowers to the Lord of Rukmiṇī within the pavilion sports in all the divine gardens with the leaders of men.
He who performs the work of painting in the palace of the God of gods dwells in the world of Rudra for as long as the oceans endure.
O lord of men, he who gives a moon made of silver upon the black [cloth] dwells in the world of Soma for as long as Dvārakā exists. || 65 ||
The parasol, however, has many ribs, is draped with strings of tinkling bells and garlands, is adorned with divine jewels, and is provided with a golden handle. || 66 ||
He offers an umbrella adorned with hundreds of thousands and millions [of jewels] to Kṛṣṇa; accompanied by all the immortals, he sports together with his ancestors.
O leader of men, one should give a celestial chariot to Kṛṣṇa; thus honored by the Giver of Wealth (Dhanada), he dwells there for the duration of a day of Brahmā.
O King, having performed worship and other rites, one who offers the waving of lights (ārārtika) before the blazing form upon the head of Kṛṣṇa rejoices in the presence of Kṛṣṇa. (69)
O King, that man who performs the *ārārtika* rite for Kṛṣṇa with camphor and radiant lamps dwells in the world [of Viṣṇu] for seven kalpas.
He who, having taken water from a conch shell, whirls it over Keśava, dwells in the presence of Viṣṇu in the Ocean of Milk until the end of the kalpa.

Having done this, O King, whoever performs a circumambulation of Kṛṣṇa while reciting the Thousand Names, or reciting another hymn, gains at every step the merit of [giving away] the earth consisting of seven continents.

One who performs a prostration with a staff [before Kṛṣṇa] obtains a merit equal to ten thousand horse-sacrifices. He who pleases Kṛṣṇa with well-sung songs in sweet tones attains the fruit of the Sāmaveda; of this there is no doubt.
He who dances with a joyful soul, manifesting many emotions with great devotion, burns away even those sins committed during an entire Manvantara.
Whoever performs the recitation of a book before Kṛṣṇa with great devotion shall obtain for every single syllable the merit born from the gift of a hundred tawny cows.
Those best of the twice-born who satisfy Kṛṣṇa with the words of the Ṛg, Yajur, and Sāma Vedas dwell in the world of Brahmā until the end of the kalpa.
Those who recite the Yoga-śāstras, Vedāntas, and Purāṇas in the presence of Kṛṣṇa pierce the solar disc and attain absorption into Hari.
The Gītā, the Thousand Names, the King of Hymns (Stavarāja), the Anusmṛti, and the Liberation of Gajendra—these are exceedingly dear to Kṛṣṇa. (78)
He who recites the glorious Bhāgavata in the presence of Kṛṣṇa sports eternally with the yogis, accompanied by hundreds of millions of his ancestors.
O protector of the earth, whoever should read the life of Rāma spoken by Vyāsa, as well as the Purāṇas, shall attain liberation; of this there is no doubt. (80)
On the twelfth day, when it has arrived, those men who act in this manner—by means of songs and other such offerings—Keśava bestows upon them a hundred thousandfold merit.
O Lord of the Earth, for those staying at Dvārakāvāsa, the merit becomes ten-millionfold through keeping vigil; they obtain this fruit every single day. (82)
By the sight of those whose mouths are blackened after being purified by the waters of the Gomatī, the sins they have accumulated over a hundred years depart.
Blessed are those in the world of men who, having gone to Dvāravatī in the Kali age, satisfy the ancestors and the gods with the water of the ocean at Gomati. 84.
At Gaṅgādvāra, Prayāga, and on the Gaṅgā in Kurujāṅgala; at Prabhāsa, Śuklatīrtha, Śrīsthala, and also at Puṣkara—|| 85 ||
O King, when the propitiation of the ancestors is performed through bathing, the offering of funeral cakes (piṇḍa), and libations, such satisfaction is attained through the sight of the Gomatī.
He who says, "The Gomati stands for many yojanas," diligently obtains the fruit of a thousand Cāndrāyaṇa fasts.
Blessed is Dvāravatī in this world, where the Gomatī flows and where the beloved of Rukmiṇī himself dwells eternally.
In the Kali age, those deluded by sin will not bathe on the banks of the Gomatī; how then can there be an exhaustion of their bondage of sin? (89)
O best of men, in the Kali age, Kṛṣṇa has fashioned the Gomatī as a ladder to heaven, which generates joy in the minds of all living beings.
The visible staircase to heaven, which is equal to the Gomatī, is not seen; it grants happiness to sinful men and bestows liberation merely by bathing in it. 91.
O tiger among men, one should go to that place where the ocean roars, joined with the waters of the Gomatī, for it is there indeed that Kṛṣṇa resides.
Who would not serve that city where stones marked with the discus, emerging from the ocean at the Gomati, grant liberation when worshipped? (93)
O King, who would not serve that city where pure clay marked with the discus remains for the sake of destroying sins in the Kali age? (94)
Who would not serve that city, which was formerly invisible in the world to Daityas, Dānavas, and Rākṣasas, yet served as a refuge for the gods and others? 95.
Who would not serve that city which Kṛṣṇa, the son of Devakī, does not abandon in the Kali age, whether by deed, mind, or speech? (96)
Mārkaṇḍeya said: Listen, O King, I shall relate a story that destroys all sins; by hearing which one is surely liberated from the bondage of this miserable cycle of existence. 97.
O King, formerly in the region of Avantī there was a Brāhmaṇa who had mastered the Vedas, renowned as Candraśarman, and who was always a devotee of Śiva.
In thought, deed, or word, he meditated on no one other than Sadāśiva; nor, O lord of men, did he perform any vow other than that of the Śaivas. 99.
O King, one does not observe a fast on the day of Hari, nor perform a vow dedicated to Hari, except on the fourteenth day; nor does one perform a vow arising from any other deity.
O King of kings, wherever there is a sacred field of Śiva or a holy site of Śaṅkara, there he goes; he never goes to a Vaiṣṇava site.
Every year he visits Somanātha for an audience; O lord of men, he especially does not miss the lunar festival (somaparvan). 102.
O king of kings, as he performed this practice while cultivating devotion to Śiva, seventy-nine years passed away.
Once, O protector of the earth, when the Soma festival had arrived, innumerable men from various lands came to bring the Soma. 104.
Having all seen the Lord Someśvara, they went to the city of Kṛṣṇa; though summoned by them, Candraśarman did not go to the city of Dvārakā.
I do not consider there to be any holy place superior to the field of Śiva in the three worlds; nor have I known any other god than Īśvara, the leader of the gods. (106)
Except for Candraśarman, they all went to the city of Dvārakā. O King, on another day, as they were returning toward their own homes, the grandfathers of Candraśarman appeared to them in a dream.
Having seen a most terrible dream of hungry ghosts—huge-bodied, emaciated by hunger, and fearsome—he became terrified and trembled. (109)
Candraśarman said: "Who are you, with such deformed appearances and so terrifying to living beings? Such creatures born of the earth have never been seen or heard of by me. (110)
The pretas said: "O best of brahmins, do not fear; your ancestors have come into your presence, tormented by great suffering. (111)
Candraśarman said: "Sacrifices have been performed, gifts given, and austerities practiced by your ancestors; that there should be a cause for your state as ghosts is a source of wonder to me. (112)
The pretas said: Listen, my son, we shall explain the cause of this state of existence as a preta. In former times, the day of Vāsudeva was always desecated by you. (113)
"Listen, my son, we have attained this state of being a preta because a vigil for Hari was specifically performed by us at night while pierced [by obstacles]. (114)
There will be a fall into a terrible hell, of this there is no doubt; together with you, without a shadow of doubt, until the dissolution of all beings.
Candraśarman said: For those devoid of devotion to Hari and who have neglected the vow of Dvādaśī, the state of being a ghost does not cease even if Śaṅkara and other deities are worshipped. (116)
If the Lord, the destroyer of Tripura, has not been propitiated with devotion, he will surely grant him a destination; he shall not go to the state of a ghost.
The pretas said: "O son, without an expiation for the violation of the Dvādaśī vow, one who has fallen [into this state] certainly goes to the state of a preta; he never escapes it. (118)
O son, even one who is always performing penance and worshipping Śaṅkara incurs the sin of cow-slaughter if he lacks the worship of Keśava. (119)
First Keśava is to be worshipped, and afterwards the god Maheśvara; likewise, whatever other deities there may be, they too are indeed to be worshipped with devotion.
From that root, branches and sub-branches arise in great numbers; from Vāsudeva, this entire world of moving and non-moving beings has emerged.
Therefore, a wise person should not worship the branch while abandoning the root—especially Hari, the Lord of the Universe and Sovereign of the three worlds.
Those who perform [the rites] on that day, though properly adorned with the piercing (vedha), do so with a thorn; there is no doubt that because of this, they go to the state of a preta.
The gods do not accept the *havya* offering, nor do the ancestors accept the *kavya*; likewise, neither the Sun nor the Grandfathers accept the worship. (124)
Those who pass the day of Hari with a thorn in their hearts are pretas when the two full-moon days (paurṇamāsī) arrive, specifically the one devoid of fire (rākā).
The Vaiśākhī day is especially praised for rites such as the Śrāddha; however, he who observes the third lunar day of Vaiśākha joined with the preceding [second] day [is at fault]. (126)

The gods do not accept the *havya* offering, nor do the ancestors accept the *kavya* offering, where the gods do not accept it, how can the ancestors accept it there? Therefore, the third lunar day (*tṛtīyā*) joined with the preceding [second] day should be observed by wise men.
If, out of delusion, they act [in such a way], then that state of being a preta becomes eternal; it does not depart even through many performed meritorious deeds or visits to sacred fords.
One who observes the tenth lunar day and the anniversary of one's parents' death on a day overlapping with the preceding tithi falls into hell.

The Darśa and Paurṇamāsa sacrifices, when joined with the preceding [lunar day], must be performed by those who maintain the sacred fires; they are not to be performed by those devoid of fire—so Prajāpati has declared once again. (130)

On the anniversary of the death, however, it is declared that the lunar day (tithi) which extends through its own [specific] time is the one to be used; the śrāddha should be performed on that day, and neither the waning nor the waxing of the moon is a cause for concern.

Regarding this, it was stated by Manu, by the sons [of the sages], and by the authors of the Vedānta commentaries: "That alone must be accepted as authoritative; otherwise, you will fall into the state of a ghost. (132)
In these ways, the state of being a preta arises for living beings on earth; having examined the treatises on dharma, one should perform what is ordained for oneself. (133)
If one has bowed to Somanātha and undertaken the pilgrimage, yet does not proceed for the sake of seeing Kṛṣṇa, what fruit accrues to him? (134)
The supreme form is said to be Hari, who is established as the Lord; no distinction should be made here, for as is Śambhu, so is Hari. (135)
No difference whatsoever is seen between Kṛṣṇa and Somanātha; the pilgrimage to Śrī Somanātha is complete through the sight of Kṛṣṇa. (136)
Therefore, O son, you must go from both sides; there is no doubt about this. Having beheld the god Someśvara, you should proceed toward Dvārakā.
At Prabhāsa, the meritorious Keśava himself remains stationed within the center of the Liṅga of Somanātha; he stays there and accepts the offerings.
If a man has not gone to Dvārakā after seeing the god Someśvara, there will be a fall into a terrible hell for his ancestors as well. (139)

"Especially by you, my child, the Dvādaśī vow was not performed; whereas the vow that was performed by us was joined with the Vedhas [the Creator]. Indeed, our departure from the world of Yama is no longer to be seen. (140)
Candraśarman said: "O father, if the Dvādaśī vow was not performed by me out of ignorance, why has the Dvādaśī vow been performed by you all in such a flawed manner?"
The pretas said: "We have entered this state of existence as pretas because of wicked Brahmins and false astrologers who were deluded by the illusion of Śukra, and because of our own harshness. (142)
Our giving, asceticism, fire-offerings, and recitations have gone to waste; we have entered the womb of a preta because of the thorn-like observance of the Dvādaśī vow.
O Keśava, O son, those who make the day dear [to the Lord] thornless, their ancestors fall from heaven into the state of ghosts.
Candraśarman said: "O grandfathers, how does this state of being a ghost come to an end? By what action does that occur? Tell me all of that, and whatever it is that I must perform. (145)
The pretas said: "Neither at Gayā nor Prayāga, nor at Puṣkara or Kurujāṅgala; nor at Ayodhyā, Avantī, Mathurā, or Arbuda. (146)
And there is no other holy site (tīrtha) equal to Gomati, setting aside the Ganges, the Sarasvati, the Narmada, and Pushkara. || 147 ||

Just as there is a destruction of the state of being a ghost on the banks of the Gomatī during the Kali age—through the gift of Gomatī water and by beholding the face of Kṛṣṇa—[so too is there liberation]. || 148 ||
Even sins committed over ten million lifetimes go to dissolution; however, the merit of those who have falsely renounced is in vain, and that of forest-dwellers is likewise in vain. (149)
"O son, if they spend the day of Viṣṇu with a thorn in their hearts, then go and behold that face which is like the full moon. (150)
"Having gone to Dvārakā for Kṛṣṇa, let there be a way for us; otherwise, your journey has become fruitless, and that which was earned by you will not be realized. (151)
All of that has become useless without the worship of Keśava. Since Śaṅkara was worshipped by you without the worship of Keśava, that merit has become fruitless; you shall go to the womb of a ghost.
Your merit will become complete by the sight of Kṛṣṇa at Dvārakā, near the ocean at the Gomatī; of this there is no doubt. (153)
"Having seen the god Someśvara, if one does not see Kṛṣṇa, one does not obtain the fruit of the pilgrimage; thus Śiva himself declares. (154)
I have been seen by them without a doubt—those who have beheld Kṛṣṇa; for there is no doubt that my single form is not different from that of Kṛṣṇa. (155)
"Having seen me, you should go to Dvārakā and behold Kṛṣṇa; indeed, having seen Kṛṣṇa, he will see me, and thus he shall attain great fruit. (156)
The man whose soul is purified by the sight of Kṛṣṇa, who beholds me, shall have no return from my Vaiṣṇava world.
Thus spoke the Lord of the Gods himself, the Lord of Soma, in ancient times; this was heard by us from the virtuous Brahmins as they were speaking at Puṣkara. (158)
Therefore, go for the sake of departure; have an audience with Kṛṣṇa. Otherwise, you will go to the womb of a Piśāca, which bestows sin.
Even one who has committed an offense, when he beholds Kṛṣṇa, is liberated from the sins committed throughout his life; of this there is no doubt. (160)
When Kṛṣṇa, the son of Devakī and Lord of the gods of gods, is worshipped, all the deities, including Brahmā, Rudra, Bhaga, and the others, are worshipped.
O son, without the worship of Kṛṣṇa, even the gods beginning with Rudra, nor the Grandfathers (Pitāmahas), do not grant satisfaction when they are worshipped. || 162 ||
Therefore, go to Dvāravatī and behold Kṛṣṇa; liberated from the state of a ghost, we shall attain the supreme goal.
O son, in the Kali age, the sages have not seen anyone whose limbs are washed by the waters of the Gomatī who must undergo rebirth.
Struck by the pair of her feet, the waves of the sound of the Gomatī provide a path indeed for those who speak of Brahman, who otherwise have no way to go.
Furthermore, whoever performs a śrāddha at the confluence of the Gomatī and the ocean, satisfaction for the ancestors arises that lasts until the dissolution of all beings.
Whatever merit is obtained by visiting all the holy fords on the earth including the oceans, that same merit is gained in a single day in the presence of Kṛṣṇa at Dvārakā.
Whatever fruit is seen by the gods as arising from all sacred fords (tīrthas), one obtains all that fruit day after day in Dvārakā.

Whatever fruit is said to result from performing Śrāddha rites at thousands of millions of sacred fords (tīrthas), that same fruit for the ancestors is obtained from the libation of sesame seeds in the Gomatī. || 169 ||
Whoever provides food for ascetics in the temple of Kṛṣṇa, there shall be satisfaction for the ancestors at every mouthful for as many ages as there are grains of rice.
By giving a loincloth, a covering garment, an umbrella, sandals, and a water-pot to renunciants, one attains that fruit for seven kalpas. (171)
Blessed are those men, my son, even the outcastes and others, who dwell in Dvārakā; for those yogis residing there attain the supreme goal. || 172 ||
Those who behold the face of Hari three times every day shall not undergo rebirth even in hundreds of millions of kalpas.
Any woman who, having become a widow, takes refuge in Dvārakā, leads ten thousand members of her lineage to the supreme state. || 174 ||
What purpose is served here even by a son if he has not gone to Dvārakā? A woman is superior to a hundred sons; having gone, she should dwell in the city of Kṛṣṇa.
Having gone to Kṛṣṇa’s city, he who worships Kṛṣṇa with tulasī leaves has obtained the fruit of his birth; his great-grandfathers have been delivered.
Whoever wears a garland of Tulasī leaves that has been removed from Kṛṣṇa obtains the fruit of ten horse-sacrifices for every single leaf.
The enemy of the Daityas bestows daily the fruit arising from Dvārakā upon that man who wears a garland made from Tulasī wood.
Having offered a garland made of *tulasī* wood to Viṣṇu, the man who wears it with devotion incurs no sin at all; Kṛṣṇa, the son of Devakī, is always pleased in mind with him. (179)
In the body of that mortal who possesses ornaments made from Tulasī wood for the head, arms, and other parts, Hari is ever present. (180)
Whoever performs any rite for the ancestors or the deities while adorned with a garland of Tulasī, that act becomes ten millionfold effective in the Kali age. || 181 ||
But upon seeing a garland made of Tulasī wood, the messengers of the King of the Dead flee from afar, like nests driven away by the wind. (182)
When that [merit] is grasped, no transference of sin occurs at all; for we have heard this ancient lore (purāṇa) recounted by those who discourse upon Brahman. || 183 ||
Therefore, you should wear a garland made from the wood of the Tulasī plant; it removes all sin pertaining to this world and the next—of this there is no doubt. (184)
If one wanders about adorned with a garland of Tulasī, there shall be no bad dreams, no ill omens, and no fear from enemies anywhere. (185)

Having indeed performed the renunciation of sacred fords (tīrthasaṃnyāsa), ascetics and widowed women are to be known as liberated while living (jīvanmukta) in the Kali age, together with ten million members of their lineage.
Those rationalists who, deluded by sin, do not wear the garland, do not return from hell, having been consumed by the fire of Hari’s wrath.
O son, you must observe Unmīlinī, Vañjulī, Trispṛśā, Pakṣavardhinī, Jayantī, Vijayā, and Jayā. (188)
The eighth lunar day is declared to be the destroyer of sins and is exceedingly dear to Kṛṣṇa; when observed in the Kali age, O son, Dvārakā bestows liberation.

Thus ends the twenty-third chapter, titled "The Description of the Greatness of Wearing Tulasī," within the "Greatness of Going to Dvārakā," in the "Greatness of Dvārakā," in the fourth section of the Prabhāsa-khaṇḍa, in the seventh part of the Śrī Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a compendium of eighty-one thousand verses. || 23 ||
Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya said: O lord of the earth, having fulfilled the request of the ancestors who had appeared in the form of spirits, Candraśarman, the best of the twice-born, arrived at Dvārakā.
Where Kṛṣṇa dwells daily together with Rukmiṇī, and where the sacred fords reside—there the best of the twice-born went.
Where the sacrifices abide, where the deities abide, and where the sages and seers, the foremost knowers of yoga, abide.
That city of Dvārakā, which grants all desires, is frequented by Siddhas, Gandharvas, Kinnaras, men, hosts of Apsarases, and Yakṣas.
That city, where the Gomatī flows as a ladder for ascending to heaven, was indeed seen by the best of Brahmins to be the giver of liberation to men.
Who would not serve that city, upon entering whose boundary even such sins as the killing of a Brahmin perish by the mere sight of it?
Having gone to Kṛṣṇapura and having beheld both the Gomatī and the ocean, I consider myself to have achieved my life's purpose—my life, my youth, and my wealth.
Having beheld the beautiful city of Kṛṣṇa and the lotus-face of Kṛṣṇa, I am blessed, I have fulfilled my purpose, and I am fortunate upon this earth.
Having beheld the beautiful Kṛṣṇamukha, Rukmiṇī, and the city of Dvārakā, what need is there for thousands of crores of visited holy places?
Through hundreds of thousands of merits, the auspicious Dvāravatī was attained; indeed, Madhusūdanī was reached during the month of Vaiśākha when it is bright.
The twelfth lunar day named Trispṛśā destroys hundreds of millions of sins; blessed are all those humans who observe Madhusūdanī in the month of Vaiśākha.

For those by whom the Trispṛśā, conjoined with a Wednesday, has been attained, that fruit which is not obtained through sacrifices, nor through the Vedas, nor even by visiting ten million holy places, is indeed obtained by men in Dvārakā.

Having spoken thus, the best of the twice-born resorted to the bank of the Gomatī and, having performed the ritual ablution according to rule through the rites prescribed in the scriptures, [he remained there].

Having performed the bath as prescribed and having satiated the ancestors and the deities, O King, one should take auspicious stones marked with the discus from Cakratīrtha, worshipping them according to the stated ritual with the Puruṣasūkta.

Afterwards, having performed the worship of Śiva and recollecting the words spoken by his father, he duly offered the funeral cakes (piṇḍa) and water to the ancestors according to the prescribed rites.
Ointments, garments, flowers, incense, lamps, pleasing food offerings, and roots and fruits; || 16 ||

Having offered betel-leaf with camphor and performed the lustration ceremony (nīrājana) and other rites, he should perform circumambulations and prostrations again and again, preceded by hymns of praise.
Having asked the Lord of Gods for forgiveness, he then performed a vigil; when three watches of the night had passed, Candrāśarman indeed spoke.
O Kṛṣṇa, hear my words as one who is afflicted and wretched; O Keśava, deliver me, for I am terrified by the fear of saṃsāra. (19)
For those devoted to your lotus feet, there is no suffering even for sinners; how much less so for men who observe the Dvādaśī vow and are free from sin? (20)
The sin born from the piercing of the tenth lunar day has been described by my ancestors; may that evil deed be destroyed through your grace, O Janārdana. (21)
O Kṛṣṇa, O Hari, may the sin of this day, which was rendered fruitless because the vigil (jāgara) was not performed, go to destruction like salt in water. || 22 ||
"Since the day was made turbid by my grandfathers, they have consequently attained the state of a ghost (preta), which brings about great suffering. (23)
O Lord of Gods, O Master of the World, act in such a way that my ancestors, who have been liberated from the state of being a preta, may attain final liberation. (24)
O best of the Yadus, you ought once again to show me favor; for though deluded by ignorance, I failed to perform your worship. (25)
O Lord of Gods, though I am a sinner, I have taken refuge in devotion to Śiva; yet I have never practiced devotion to you, nor have I observed your sacred day.
O Kṛṣṇa, I have not seen Dvārakā, nor have I bathed in the waters of the Gomatī; nor have I beheld your lotus feet, which bestow liberation.
"I have not made a pilgrimage to Dvārakā after seeing the Lord Someśvara; thus, the merit that I have accumulated has become fruitless. (28)
O Lord of the Gods, everything has been told to me by my ancestors; O Keśava, by your grace, let that merit not go to waste. (29)
But your face, so difficult to behold even in the three worlds, has been seen by me; O Son of Devakī, I have never heard of such a thing in the Purāṇas.
Furthermore, those who are remembered as offenders, such as Śiśupāla and others, having been slain by your hand in anger, those best of men attained liberation. (31)
From this day forward, that worship must be performed by you every single day; even if it is deficient by half a *pala*, food must be eaten on your day. (32)
I must perform the Dvādaśī vow together with you, and I must cultivate devotion to the Bhāgavatas even at the cost of my life and wealth. (33)
The thousand names should always be recited, for they are dear to you; indeed, the worship must always be performed by me with tulasī leaves. (34)
"A garland made from Tulasī wood must always be worn by me; and when your vigil has arrived, dancing and singing must be performed. (35)
I must go to Dvārakā every day, and for the sake of hearing your stories, I shall constantly read from the book.
I shall always bear the water from [Your] feet upon my head with great devotion, and I shall partake of the food offering with great devotion. (37)
I shall reverently bear upon my head your floral remains (nirmālya); and having offered it to you, that which is desired by you must always be consumed by me. (38)
In such and such a manner you must act that satisfaction may arise for you; this truth has been proclaimed by me before you, O Kṛṣṇa. (39)
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: "Excellent, excellent, O illustrious Candraśarman, best of the twice-born! Your grandfathers shall come to my world along with you."
Behold, O best of the twice-born, your ancestors, released from the state of a preta through my grace, mounted upon Garuḍa in the sky. (41)
The grandfathers said: "O son, by your grace we have attained liberation, there is no doubt; we have been released from the state of the departed through the sight of Kṛṣṇa’s face. (42)
Blessed are those sons, grandsons, and great-grandsons in the world of men who, having beheld Śrī Somanātha, go on to behold Kṛṣṇa at Dvārakā. (43)
Blessed is that widow who performs the pilgrimage to Kṛṣṇa; she shall deliver a hundred generations of her lineage from hell in this world.
Even an outcaste who performs such a pilgrimage to Hari and Śaṅkara attains supreme liberation, surrounded by his ancestors.
Furthermore, for one who remains there after having performed renunciation at a sacred ford (tīrtha), there is no return from the world of Viṣṇu even in hundreds of millions of kalpas.
They have been deceived, there is no doubt, even after seeing the Lord Someśvara; they have not seen the face of Kṛṣṇa, nor have they bathed in the waters of the Gomatī.

"What is the use of abundant meritorious waters arising from ten million holy fords (tīrthas) for one who, having seen Someśvara, does not go to Dvārakā? His ancestors dwelling in heaven reproach that sinner. (48)
Having seen the god Someśvara and having seen Kṛṣṇa again as Śiva, the merit arising from a hundred pilgrimages was recounted in the Sauparṇa [Purāṇa]. (49)
Having seen the god Someśvara, one does not see Kṛṣṇa at all; due to delusion, all his worldly activity has indeed become utterly futile.
The man who, having arrived at Prabhāsa, beholds Kṛṣṇa, obtains with effort the fruit equivalent to ten thousand visits to Prabhāsa.
Because all holy places, all the gods, as well as all sacrifices, come to Dvārakā three times a day into the presence of Kṛṣṇa. (52)
O son, what is the use of various other holy places and their locations? By merely beholding Dvāravatī, one obtains the fruit of all sacred fords. || 53 ||
When Kaṃsa, Jarāsandha, and Naraka had been struck down, and the burden of the earth had been removed, Kṛṣṇa, the son of Devakī, established the beautiful city of Dvāravatī near the ocean.
Remaining there with a joyful mind, Kṛṣṇa shall obtain the pleasure of amorous union.
Brahmā, Agni, Vāyu, and Sūrya; the inhabitants of heaven beginning with Vāsava; mortals, Brahmins, and kings; and from the netherworld, the lords of serpents. || 56 ||
Rivers and streams, mountains and forests, groves and cities, villages, wildernesses, oceans, and lakes. (57)

The Yakṣas, Asuras, Gandharvas, Siddhas, and Vidyādharas; Rambhā and the other Apsarases; the sons of Diti beginning with Prahlāda; the Rākṣasas beginning with Vibhīṣaṇa; and Dhanada, the leader of the Rākṣasas. || 58 ||
The ṛṣis, the munis, the siddhas, and the yogins beginning with Sanaka; the planets, the constellations, and the yogas; and Dhruva, the supreme Vaiṣṇava. (59)
Whatever exists in the three worlds, whether stationary or moving, always remains eternally in the presence of Śrī Kṛṣṇa every single day.

They do not abandon the holy city of Dvārakā, which is served by Kṛṣṇa; for you, O son, have now served it through the vision of Kṛṣṇa. Released from the womb of a Piśāca, we shall go to the supreme goal.
O son, the sin born from the overlapping of the twelfth lunar day has been destroyed by the power of Dvārakā; there is no doubt that you have attained the supreme state.
Whatever sin you have accumulated arising from the transgression of the twelfth day (dvādaśī) has been destroyed by the sight of Kṛṣṇa; do not abandon the vow of dvādaśī.
O son, this piercing born of the tenth day must be guarded with great effort; otherwise, without a doubt, you will fall into the womb of a preta. (64)
The sin arising from the three worlds falls upon those on this earth who pass the day known as Kṛṣṇa with a sense of grievance.
There is no atonement for him who spends a single day of Hari pierced by a thorn; such people do not go to heaven even in hundreds of Manvantaras.
The state of being a preta is unbearable, my son, as are the torments of Yama; therefore, my son, one should not perform the Śalya-dvādaśī vow.

For those ignorant ones who cause [the rites] to be performed through fraudulent means and as mere rationalizers shall go to the realm of hungry ghosts (preta-yoni), together with all their ancestors.
The twelfth day (dvādaśī) pierced by the tenth (daśamī) utterly destroys one's lineage; it annihilates former merits and destroys devotion to Kṛṣṇa.
"May it be well with you; we shall depart by the grace of the Lord of Rukmiṇī. O son, the station of Viṣṇu, known as 'no more rebirth,' has been attained."
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: "O Candraśarman, O best of the twice-born, I am pleased with your devotion; for although you have entered into the state of a devotee of Śiva, you have indeed become a Vaiṣṇava."
For seventy-nine years, you did not perform [the rites] during my day; by my grace, it has been completed for you—of this there is no doubt.
Indeed, by a single fast alone—since the Trispṛśā [fast] was impossible—through the grace of Dvārakā and through the sight of my vision, [this was achieved]. || 73 ||
"Though deluded by ignorance, you did not perform my worship out of devotion to Śiva; yet, by my grace, it shall indeed be accomplished. (74)
O best of the twice-born, those by whom I was seen in Dvārakā during the month of Vaiśākha, specifically on the Trispṛśā day and likewise on the Vañjulī day—[they have attained my state]. (75)
When the day of Unmīlinī arrives, or when the Pakṣavardhinī arrives, there is no fault in these [acts], even if they were committed by slayers of Brahmins.
O Brahmin, even a man who has not performed any merit since birth shall become a partaker of its fruit merely by beholding my city. (77)
Having visited all the sacred fords on earth, such as Prabhāsa and others, the same fruit may be obtained here simply by seeing my city, even after having inquired about them.
Whoever reads this greatness of Dvārakā on my day, or anywhere at all, shall obtain my holy city through my grace. (79)
He who recites this in the Kali age obtains that same merit which belongs to those dwelling in my city who behold me at the three times of day.
O best of the twice-born, in the Kali age, Kāśī, Mathurā, Avantī, Ayodhyā, as well as Māyā, Kāñcī, and my own city [shall flourish]. (81)
Likewise, that which originates from Śāligrāma, as well as Badarī, Kurukṣetra, Bhṛgukṣetra, and Puṣkara known as auspicious; || 82 ||
Prayāga, Prabhāsa, and the sacred field of Hāṭakeśvara; Gaṅgādvāra, Śaukara, and the confluence of the Gaṅgā with the ocean. || 83 ||
O twice-born one, Naimiṣa, the Daṇḍaka forest, as well as Vṛndāvana, Saindhava, and the place called Arbuda—all these sacred abodes—84.
O best of the twice-born, there are forests such as Māgadha and others, lotus-lakes, and mountains such as Śailarāja and others, headed by the Himālaya. (85)
Whatever rivers such as the Gaṅgā exist upon the earth, those sacred fords (tīrthas) are equal to the city of Dvārakā at all three times of day.
O Brahmin, having avoided everything seized by Kali, when a hundred years have passed, there shall be a vision of me in my city.
"O god on earth, by my grace, your death shall come when the day known as Trispṛśā has arrived during the bright fortnight of the month of Vaiśākha. (88)

O Brahmin, on the day of the conjunction with Wednesday, during the daytime, while standing before me on the ground, the departure of your life-breath shall occur upon reaching the tenth door; of this there is no doubt, by my grace.
"Go to your own abode, O best of Brahmins; you shall obtain all your desires. For those devoted to me, even at the end of an eon, no destruction occurs. (90)
For men who carry devotion to me, whether in this world or in the next, no inauspiciousness exists; it shall lead ten million members of their lineage to heaven.
Mārkaṇḍeya said: Then, when a hundred years had passed, having gone to the city of Dvāravatī and relinquishing his life-breaths through the instruction of Kṛṣṇa, he indeed attained liberation.
O Indradyumna, that greatness arising from Dvārakā has been narrated; I shall now speak further of whatever else dwells in your mind. (93)
Those who hear or indeed read the greatness arising from Dvārakā obtain all the fruit that was described by Kṛṣṇa. (94)
In whosever house this is written and spread throughout this world, the manifest merit of Dvārakā arising from Kṛṣṇa is obtained.

Thus ends the twenty-fourth chapter, titled "The Description of the Excellence and Greatness of the City of Dvārakā, Beginning with Candraśarman’s Arrival at Dvārakā and His Receiving the Boon Granted by Kṛṣṇa," within the Legend of Candraśarman in the Dvārakā Section, the Fourth, of the Prabhāsa Section, the Seventh, in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a compendium of eighty-one thousand verses. || 24 ||
Indradyumna said: O best of sages, tell me something; I have a great curiosity. Speak at length about a sacred, purifying, and sin-destroying holy place (tīrtha). || 1 ||
Mārkaṇḍeya said: O King, in the Kali age, these three cities—Mathurā, Dvārakā, and Ayodhyā—are the beloved of Hari; they bestow virtue, wealth, and desire, and grant liberation.
In Madhurā, the Kālindī is present; near Kṛṣṇa is the Gomatī; and in Ayodhyā, the Sarayū, which always bestows liberation when served, is ever-present.
By remembering Kṛṣṇa and Rāma, the bestowers of auspiciousness, in Dvārāvatī and Ayodhyā, and Hari and Viṣṇu in Mathurā, one shall attain liberation.
Blessed is that Mathurā in the world where Hari himself was born; blessed is Dvārakā in the world where Viṣṇu sported.
That Ayodhyā, which grants all desires, is worthy of worship even by the fortunate; for it was personally protected by the god-like Rāma, whose mind is fixed on righteousness.
The fruit that is bestowed by serving Kāśī for the duration of a kalpa, Mathurā bestows that same fruit in even a single day.
Whatever fruit may be obtained at Prayāga during a thousand Manvantaras, that same fruit is attained by those residing in Dvārakā for even half a moment.
Whatever fruit is obtained by those dwelling at Prabhāsa and Kurukṣetra for hundreds of years, that same fruit shall be attained in Ayodhyā in half a moment.
Rāma, the lord of Ayodhyā; Keśava in Mathurā; Kṛṣṇa, the resident of Dvārakā; and even the chanting [of their names], which is difficult to obtain.
By glorifying Mathurā, by hearing about the city of Dvārakā, and even by beholding Ayodhyā, one shall go to the state that is pure in its three aspects.
The city of Dvārakā, which resembles the third heaven, brings about the destruction of rebirth for anyone who hears of or beholds the self-existent god Kṛṣṇa.
Indeed, Ayodhyā, when heard of, written down, or seen, removes the sins accumulated over an eon; and Dvārakā is the third [city] that does so.
In the Kali age, Lord Kṛṣṇa, Viṣṇu, Hari, is remembered as being at rest; by keeping a vigil at night on the twelfth lunar day (dvādaśī), one obtains the fruit of ten thousand horse-sacrifices.
O best of kings, for those men who remember that place of childhood play day after day, the state of being on the Golden Mountain (Meru) arises.
Blessed are those men in this world during the Kali age, O best of men, by whom the ritual immersion in the waters of the Gomatī river has been performed. (16)
Having bathed in the western direction and joined his palms in reverence, those men who remember Dvārakā shall obtain ten million times the fruit [of their merit].
Indeed, that man who even mentally contemplates the city of Dvāravatī in the Kali age effortlessly obtains the merit of ten thousand tawny cows.
O lord of men, by going to Dvāravatī in the Kali age, one obtains the merit born of the Gaṅgā and the ocean, as well as that produced at Gaṅgādvāra.
O King, I am Mārkaṇḍeya, who remembers seven kalpas; I recall that there is no city equal to or even superior to Dvāravatī.
O King, there is no one more fortunate than Durvāsas, nor anyone superior to him, for by him Hari was detained at Dvārakā through the binding of a verbal agreement.
Do not go to Kāśī, nor Kurukṣetra, nor Prabhāsa, nor Puṣkara; O royal sage, go to Dvārakā and behold the auspicious face of Kṛṣṇa.
A man who goes to Dvārakā obtains the merit of a thousand horse-sacrifices and a hundred Rājasūya sacrifices at every step during the Kali age. (23)
O best among the foremost of kings, their life is fruitful in this Kali age—those whose minds did not falter as they journeyed toward Dvārakā. (24)
By him who has offered the pinda-oblation at the Gomatī in the presence of Kṛṣṇa, his mother becomes possessed of sons, as do his father and his ancestors. (25)
Having made a mark with Gopīcandana, even that place upon which he wanders on the earth becomes purified; how much more so the place where he remains? (26)
He who constantly wears upon his head the Tulasī that has grown in Dvārakā and was served by Kṛṣṇa shall become the lord of the gods.
The lunar day of the Lord, the enemy of the Daityas, is Vijayā; likewise, water born from the clouds, the city of Kāśī, Tulasī, and the fruit of the Dhātrī tree are eternally dear to Him. (28)
Likewise, the Bhāgavata scripture, the beloved Rāmāyaṇa, the meritorious Dvārakā, the highly cherished Mālatī, and the composed Gīta-jāgara were performed. (29)
In whose house the clay of Gopīcandana always remains, there Dvārakā dwells together with Kṛṣṇa in the Kali age.
Whether one is ungrateful, a killer of cows, a sophist, or a perpetrator of every sin, one becomes purified at that very moment through contact with Gopīcandana.
Whoever gives a piece of Gopīcandana here to a Vaiṣṇava has indeed delivered one hundred and one generations of his lineage.
O King, Yama, along with his servants, is perpetually afraid of him in whose house there is Tulasī originating from Dvārakā.
Clay originating from Dvārakā and the chanting of the glories of Kṛṣṇa as Tulasī are said by the son of Vyāsa to possess the merit of a hundred million sacrifices.
"O protector of the earth, having churned through all the scriptures and Purāṇas again and again, I have seen no city equal to Dvārakā. (35)
By him who has performed the glorification of Kṛṣṇa’s arrival at Dvārakā, it is as if he has bathed in thousands of sacred fords and performed ten million sacrifices.
But what will the subduing of the senses avail embodied beings, nor even the study of Sāṃkhya, if they do not go to Dvārakā? (37)
Those people who have not gone to the city of Dvāravatī and seen Kṛṣṇa’s face are undoubtedly beasts, equal to donkeys. (38)
But those who have fulfilled their duty are blessed; having performed the vigil for Hari on the twelfth day with devotion, they dance again and again. (39)
But he who, having gone to Kṛṣṇālaya, performs the offering of funeral cakes (piṇḍa) at the Gomatī and gives gifts according to his ability, his ancestors are liberated.
O King of kings, that embodied being who has gone to the city of Dvārakā shall not become a preta or a piśāca in birth after birth. (41)
Whatever merit is gained by one who abandons the body at Prayāga through fasting, that fruit is obtained in the presence of Kṛṣṇa in half a moment on the twelfth lunar day.
Whatever fruit one might obtain by giving ten million cows during a solar eclipse, that same fruit is obtained day after day in Dvāravatī during the Kali age.
The fruit that one obtains by giving ten million loads of gold during an eclipse of the moon or sun, that same fruit is obtained upon the sight of Kṛṣṇa.
And those who behold Kṛṣṇa seated upon the swing during the months of Madhu and Mādhava—their sons, grandsons, maternal grandfathers, and paternal grandfathers [attain liberation]. || 45 ||
O best of men, their fathers-in-law and others, along with their servants and animals, sport together with Viṣṇu until the dissolution of all beings.
O King, whatever twelfth day occurs in the presence of Kṛṣṇa, I perceive no difference whatsoever between them, especially in the Kali age. (47)
In the presence of Kṛṣṇa, all days are eternally equal to the twelfth day (Dvādaśī); in the eternal presence of Kṛṣṇa, they are all equal to the beginnings of the Yugas.
In the Kali age, Dvāravatī should be resorted to, having recognized its particular merit; for while the six cities are easily accessible, Dvārakā is difficult to attain in the Kali age.
Because through remembering and chanting [her name], humans always attain both worldly enjoyment and liberation, this city remains protected by the sage Durvāsas.
In the Kali age, it is not possible to go there or to obtain a vision of Kṛṣṇa without the grace of Kṛṣṇa; even the gods, beginning with Rudra, must go [to seek that grace].
O Lord of the World, the speech of that person who utters "Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa" three times a day for the sake of beholding Rukmiṇī becomes fruitful.
Seeing him traveling toward Dvārakā, those situated in heaven sing; the ancestors, liberated from hell, move about and laugh.
The Gomati removes whatever sin men may have that is to be concealed; this occurs through mere remembrance or recitation, so what need be said when one has actually bathed?
Having seen the Lord accompanied by Rukmiṇī at Śaṅkhoddhāra, the conch-bearing one at [Śrī] Śaṅkha, and the four-armed one at Piṇḍāraka, what will he do with others?
Rukmiṇī, the son of Devakī, Cakratīrtha, and the Gomatī; the sandalwood of the gopīs and Tulasī are difficult to obtain in the Kali age.

Those sons who, when the Kali age has arrived, go to Gayā and offer the funeral cake (piṇḍa), visit Dvārakā for the vision of Kṛṣṇa, and observe the fast at Vañjulī—those sons should be known as rare destroyers of the sins of the earth.
The fruit of their merit is equal; Vañjulī is equal to Dvārakā. That it is neither less nor more has been declared by Viṣṇu himself. 58.
O King, listen further; I shall explain the reason for Vañjulī. By fasting on the twelfth day and breaking the fast on the twelfth day, that supreme abode of Viṣṇu is attained with ease. (59)

For those dwelling in their homes, there is a sacred pilgrimage site; for those dwelling in their homes, there is austerity; for those dwelling in their homes, there is liberation through the fast of Vañjulī.
Vaṃjulī, Dvārakā, Gaṅgā, Gayā, the chanting of Govinda’s names, the Gomatī, Gokula, the Gītā, and gopīcandana are difficult to obtain. (61)
The person who hears this with devotion, having placed Keśava in their mind, obtains the fruit of a thousand horse-sacrifices.
Those who indeed hear the greatness of Keśava during the vigil shall be liberated from all sins and go to the abode of Viṣṇu.
Those men who indeed shall constantly recite it or listen to it with devotion, they truly obtain the fruit of the gift of one's weight in gold (tulāpuruṣadāna).
O King, the sages have declared that whatever gift is given during the Kṛṣṇajāgaraṇa vigil, even if it be small, should be known to become ten millionfold.
Fraud with weights, fraud with measures, and the buying of girls, horses, or cattle—all that goes to destruction when the vigil on the twelfth day is performed.

Thus ends the twenty-fifth chapter, titled "Description of the Greatness of Vañjulī, Dvārakā, Gaṅgā, Gayā, Govinda, Gomatī, Gokula, Gītā, and Gopīcandana," in the fourth section, the Dvārakāmāhātmya, of the seventh book, the Prabhāsakhaṇḍa, within the Śrī Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a compendium of eighty-one thousand verses. 25.

Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya said: [He spoke to] Prahlāda, who knew all dharmas, who had reached the further shore of the meaning of the Vedas and Śāstras, who knew the truth of the Vaiṣṇava Āgamas, and who was devoted solely to the worship of the Lord.
The sages, who knew the true essence of the meaning of all scriptures and were the upholders of their own dharma, came to see the highly wise one as he sat at ease.
The sages said: "Without knowledge, without meditation, and without the restraint of the senses—by what means can this supreme state be attained without effort? (3)
O tiger among men, out of affection, speak briefly; tell me, without exception, all the dharmas that result in both seen and unseen fruits.
Thus addressed, that illustrious one, who was devoted to Nārāyaṇa and intent on the welfare of all the worlds, spoke in brief.
Śrī Prahlāda said: Listen, for I shall declare that which is the greatest secret among secrets; by the mere hearing of which the destruction of all sins occurs.
I shall relate that which is the most essential of the essences of the eighteen Purāṇas, and which bestows the fruits of both worldly enjoyment and liberation.
To Mahādeva, the supreme cause of the universe, who was seated comfortably, the six-faced one (Kārttikeya), intent on the welfare of all the worlds, inquired with devotion.
Skanda said: O Blessed One, please graciously describe the easy means for liberation, which is the medicine for the suffering of saṃsāra for all the worlds.
Īśvara said: Whatever fourfold sin has been accumulated over ten million births in the Kali age, one dispels it by reciting the Vaiṣṇava scripture during a vigil.
One who proclaims the Vaiṣṇava scripture during the vigil for Hari should be known as my devotee; otherwise, he shall perish.
A wakeful vigil for Hari must be performed by my discerning devotee; otherwise, those who hate Janārdana should be known as sinners.
O Six-faced One, those who keep vigil and sing on the day of Hari obtain the fruit of the Agniṣṭoma sacrifice in half a moment.

For those who, during the night vigil, behold the face of Viṣṇu again and again, and whose body hairs stand on end during the night vigil of Hari, their families dwell for that long in heaven in the presence of Hari.
People who are enveloped by hundreds of sins are liberated on the path of Yama if they keep a vigil on the twelfth day, accompanied by the diversion of singing and sacred scriptures. || 15 ||
Happy is the dawn for those men who are blessed and virtuous, by whom the vigil for Hari has been performed; they do not lose their senses even at the loss of life. (16)
Those men in the world who have sons born of their lineage who perform the vigil for Hari are truly possessed of children, wealth, and renowned prowess. (17)
By those who have performed sacrifices with desired oblations, given gifts, offered funeral cakes at Gayāśiras, bathed daily at Prayāga, and kept vigil for Hari; || 18 ||
O Six-faced One, my beloved devotees of Viṣṇu always perform the beneficial vigil on the day of Viṣṇu. (19)
He who, upon hearing this, feels no joy nor keeps a vigil, surely reveals his mother’s wicked conduct.
For those who, having reached the day of Viṣṇu, do not keep a vigil for Hari, the religious merit arising from a hundred years of their lives has gone in vain.
Whether it be a son, a grandson, a daughter, or even a daughter’s son, someone in our family will perform the vigil for Hari during the Kali age.
Being cast down by the servants of Yama, the ancestors lament: "Liberation from hell will be ours once the jāgaraṇa has been performed. (23)

Liberation does not arise for us otherwise, even through hundreds of sacrifices, nor by any means from the world of men without the vigil (jāgaraṇa). Therefore, one who desires the welfare of the ancestors should perform the vigil.
Through devotion to the devotees of the Lord and through the chanting of Govinda’s names, there shall be no further assumption of a body in this world for him.
And he who keeps a vigil at the confluence on the day of victory has himself, by his own self, burnt away the rebirth of the body.
He who has spent the day of Trispṛśā engaged in a vigil at the body of Keśava becomes absorbed within Him; of this there is no doubt.
For him by whom this [night] was made to bloom while keeping vigil at night, neither gross nor subtle sins prevail.
He who causes a vigil for Hari to be held on the twelfth day, accompanied by music with cymbals and joined with gifts to the deity, [attains great merit].

I shall now declare the merit of that great devotee of the Lord: the fruit which one obtains by giving a thousand *prasthas* of sesame seeds along with gold to a twice-born man during the solstice or the sun’s transit (*saṃkrānti*). (30)
In the Kali age, one shall obtain through the gift of a spectacle that same fruit which is gained by the constant giving of a hundred loads of gold and ten thousand tawny cows with their calves.
Furthermore, O son, he who on that day satisfies Padmanābha with divine hymns composed by sages, or with Vedic Viṣṇu-sāmans; || 32 ||
O son, [he should worship] with Vaiṣṇava hymns derived from the Ṛg, Yajur, and Sāma Vedas, as well as with refined (saṃskṛta), vernacular (prākṛta), and various other praises.
The Lord of the Gods, remaining awake on the twelfth day, bestows joy; hear in brief the merit that was sung to me by Brahmā.
O Six-faced One, whatever fruit a person obtains by giving away the earth twenty-one times, having multiplied it threefold—that same fruit he shall attain. || 35 ||
Whatever fruit is obtained by [giving] a hundred thousand cows along with their calves, a mortal shall obtain that same fruit if he satisfies Hari with hymns of praise. (36)
The pleasure derived from Vedic recitation is tenfold for every single watch of a night spent in vigil; thus, a vigil for Hari should be performed in accordance with such results.
Furthermore, he who recites the Gītā and the Thousand Names at night on the twelfth lunar day, in the presence of Viṣṇu and in the company of Vaiṣṇavas, [attains the supreme goal]. || 38 ||
The meritorious Bhāgavata and the Skanda Purāṇa, which are dear to Hari; the account of Mādhava’s childhood, as well as the deeds of the gopīs. (39)
O child, I do not know the fruit for him who recites these at night after having worshipped Keśava; perhaps Keśava himself will know it.
He who lights a lamp with hymns during the vigil for Hari at night—his merit does not diminish even in hundreds of kalpas.
One who worships Hari with devotion during the vigil using Tulasī leaves together with their flower-clusters shall not undergo rebirth.
Bathing, anointing with unguents, worship, incense, lamps, hymns of praise, and offerings of food along with betel—whatever is given during the vigil becomes inexhaustible.
Whoever, being devoted to me, desires to meditate upon my six-faced form, let him perform the vigil for Hari with great devotion on the twelfth lunar day.
On the day of Vāsudeva, all the gods, including Indra, abide having taken recourse to his body for those who perform the vigil (jāgara).
Those who, while awake, perform the glorification of Vāsudeva through the Mahābhārata, attain the same goal as yogis; of this there is no doubt. (46)
Those who recite the life-story of Lord Rāma and the slaying of Rāvaṇa during a vigil for Viṣṇu attain the supreme goal.
Having studied the four Vedas, performed the worship of Hari, and bathed in all the sacred fords (tīrthas), one obtains that same fruit as from keeping a vigil for Hari.
The fruit that is obtained by means of ten thousand chariots, thousands of excellent elephants, and a hundred thousand choice horses is attained through the vigil (jāgara) dedicated to Hari. || 49 ||
Whatever fruit is proclaimed by the sages for thousands of grain-mountains and tens of millions of Tulāpuruṣa gifts, that same fruit is obtained from a vigil in honor of Hari.
Those by whom the vigil for Hari was performed have given away ten million maidens, as well as hundreds of loads of gold and hundreds of tens of thousands of jewels. (51)
Whatever fruit may arise from reciting the eighteen Purāṇas, that same fruit is obtained a hundred thousandfold by performing a vigil for Hari.
Whatever fruit belongs to the twice-born who study the scriptures beginning with the works of Manu, one who performs the vigil for Hari obtains a fruit even greater than that.
Whatever fruit belongs to men who give food during a famine, or whatever fruit comes from feeding thousands of renunciants in the Kali age—that same fruit one obtains by performing a vigil for Hari.

Thus ends the twenty-sixth chapter, titled "Description of the Majesty of the Dvādaśī Vigil," in the Fourth Section on the Majesty of Dvārakā, within the Seventh Book, the Prabhāsa-khaṇḍa, of the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a compendium of eighty-one thousand verses.

The Lord said: Having remained awake for the night of the twelfth day—a rite equal to a sacrifice that removes suffering and bestows merit—and having performed the worship of Hari, the person who listens to the beautiful Bhāgavata attains merit multiplied ten million times over that of the Vājimedha sacrifice. That supreme devotee, having severed the multitude of bonds and the mass of his wings [of karma], reaches the abode of Kṛṣṇa. || 1 ||

O King, although one may be completely surrounded by millions of heaps of the sins of killing, by millions of violations of the preceptor’s wife, by thefts multiplied a hundred thousandfold, and by those who have committed the murder of a guru—nevertheless, upon hearing the *Bhāgavata* and performing a vigil for Hari, he cuts through all that, attains liberation with a stainless body, and pierces the orb of the sun.

The eleventh day (Ekādaśī) that has entered into the twelfth day (Dvādaśī) in the month of Nabhasya, when conjoined with the Śravaṇa asterism—especially when meeting with a Monday—effects the liberation of one's great-grandfathers.

Whatever is given on the auspicious twelfth day, dedicated to Viṣṇu as well as to the ancestors, is indeed equal to Mount Meru when offered with devotion; it is truly sufficient, surpassing sacrifices, pilgrimages, and other gifts. || 4 ||

Whoever reaches the Mahānadī on the day of Viṣṇu and offers handfuls of water to the ancestors, by him a Śrāddha has been performed for a thousand years; thus fully satisfied, the ancestors grant all desired objects.

Listen, my son: the merit gained by protecting those who have come for refuge and by providing food, as well as that gained by discharging debts to the twice-born and the gods—that very same fruit is obtained through keeping a vigil for Viṣṇu.

He who gives a golden cow, a honey-ocean cow, a black antelope skin, a silver and golden Meru mountain, or the gift of the Brahmāṇḍa—verily he attains the same fruit as one who performs the vigil for Viṣṇu.

O Six-faced One, whatever fruit is obtained through truth, purity, self-restraint, forbearance, compassion, and the power of charity, that fruit is attained by those through keeping a vigil for Viṣṇu, as well as by ten horse-sacrifices accompanied by abundant sacrificial fees.

Whatever fruit is obtained by bathing in the most excellent river, by offering funeral cakes (piṇḍa) for one's father at Gayā, or by the gift of gold in Kurujāṅgala—that same fruit is attained through the vigil (jāgaraṇa) dedicated to Viṣṇu.
If those who recite this song during the Śrījāgara destroy many previously committed sins—even if they have accumulated ten thousand killings or immeasurable thefts of gold—[they are purified]. (10)
O Six-faced One, those messengers of yours do not see even the slightest path to Saurapura within the forest; nor do those men see it even in a dream whose sleep has been dispelled by wakefulness.

What is the use of saffron robes, matted locks, sacrificial fires, or other mantras? Worship the one auspicious Goddess who grants the boons of dharma, artha, kāma, and mokṣa, and who destroys the age of Kali.

Thus, it is said, Nārada formerly spoke with the intent of seeking the highest good for the son of Vinatā: "There is no other deity here superior to Kṛṣṇa; there is no vow whatsoever greater than that day. (13)

"O gods, listen! O hosts of sages, Siddhas, and lords of Munis, including the king of birds and Nārada! Having thus spoken, he raised his arm, and it was said by the devotees: "There is no vow whatsoever equal to the Ekādaśī vow. (14)

O Lord of Birds, in the Kali age, sinful men do not worship Hari, nor do they become devoted to the scriptures concerning His devotion. Those of deluded minds observe the Ekādaśī mixed with the tenth day and abandon auspicious days. || 15 ||
He who resorts to even a single day of Murāri shall always be afflicted, always diseased, always sinful, always miserable, always a destroyer of his lineage, and always a denizen of hell. (16)

Thus ends the twenty-seventh chapter, titled "The Description of the Universal Excellence of the Dvādaśī Vigil," in the fourth section on the Greatness of Dvārakā, within the seventh book, the Prabhāsa-khaṇḍa, of the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a compendium of eighty-one thousand verses. || 27 ||
Mārkaṇḍeya said: O lord of men, after one has performed the vigil for Viṣṇu according to the prescribed rule, what does Yama do thereafter with the merit that is offered to the ancestors?
Whether one has eaten or not eaten, whether one is pure or indeed impure—liberation is said there for men through the vigil for Hari.
Whether a man has not bathed or has already bathed when the vigil has arrived, he should be known as one who has immersed himself in all sacred fords; by beholding him, one shall go to heaven.
Even outcaste dog-cookers (śvapacas), having kept vigil, have attained the state of Nirvāṇa; how much more so those born of the [four] castes who are devoted to virtuous conduct? || 4 ||
Just as sleep does not arise upon hearing the cry of young women, so too shall it be during the recitation of those stories while one remains awake.
The vigil for Viṣṇu purifies the sins of killing a Brahmin, drinking liquor, theft, violating the teacher’s wife, verbal abuse, and mental wickedness.
Liberation is said to be for the lustful person; how much more so, then, for those who behold Hari?
Whatever verbal or mental sin has been accumulated through the various means of action, he undoubtedly dispels it all in a mere moment by other [means]. (8)

But for those who have gathered together in a social assembly, from where is sin traditionally said to arise? O King, the wise know that the worship of one's mother, the ancestral rites at Gayā, and likewise the pilgrimage to a sacred ford, are equal to the merit of keeping a vigil for men.
O King, the worship of one's mother is equal to ten thousand horse-sacrifices. O King, even water drawn up by the tip of a blade of kusha grass [is meritorious] for a full hundred years.
Even drinking properly from a vessel at the sacred ford known as Puṣkara, these do not equal even a sixteenth part of the merit of keeping a vigil.
O Lord of the Earth, the fruit that one obtains by giving away the entire earth filled with gold is the same fruit obtained from the vigil for Hari.

Indeed, he who performs the vigil (jāgaraṇa) undoubtedly removes the evil deeds committed by himself, as well as the cutting away of his past karma; O Lord of the Earth, I shall again speak briefly of that fruit which the wise know to belong to the vigil of Padmanābha.

Having pierced this solar orb during the waking state of Hari, that yogi goes to the supreme abode, stainless and accessible only to yogis—that state of Hari which is attained with great difficulty through Sāṃkhya and Yoga. || 15 ||
Just as rivers and streams gradually reach their final resting place in the ocean, so too do all beings, through the practice of vigilance, attain a state of stable rest in that supreme state.
Whether a person has committed sins equal in measure to Mount Meru or Mount Mandara, he undoubtedly dispels them all by keeping a vigil for Hari.
Established in the vigil, the Blessed Lord Kṛṣṇa bestows through his own songs kingship, heaven, as well as liberation and whatever else is desired by men. (18)
O Lord of the Earth, even for sinful outcasts, that state is declared by the wise through vigilance alone; how much more so, then, for the twice-born? (19)
O King, even for a singer devoid of recitation and meditation, and for one fallen from his religious duties, liberation is said to be attained through the vigil for Hari.
O King, there is no merit in the three worlds for meritorious men that equals what one who is fully engaged in the vigil accomplishes. (21)
Furthermore, you must remember this duty: the one whose banner is Garuḍa (Viṣṇu) should be remembered; one should never eat on the eleventh day, and a vigil should always be observed.

Even for an outcaste who remains awake [in this manner], such a goal shall be attained; how much more so, O Lord of the Earth, for those of the various castes and lineages who are devotees of Viṣṇu? (23)
O best of kings, for those who do not succumb to sleep while staying awake, their mother does not suffer the exhaustion of carrying them in the womb.
Therefore, wakefulness should be maintained by mortals who have avoided the mother’s womb, who seek liberation from fear, and who have turned away from the pursuit of worldly pleasures. (25)
O King, he who keeps a vigil at night endowed with devotion shall obtain the fruit of a horse sacrifice at every single moment.
O King, it has been declared by Viṣṇu in the past that the merit derived from establishing a bed and from raising one up is equal; there is no distinction between them.
Brahmins, Kshatriyas, Vaishyas, and Shudras remained awake; birds, worms, insects, and indeed many other living beings—they all went to the supreme abode, stainless and accessible only to yogis. (28)
Whatever sins there may be, even those equal to the killing of a Brahmin, they all go to destruction during the vigil for Kṛṣṇa; of this there is no doubt. (29)

On one side are all sacrifices together with all sacred fords; on the other side is the vigil for the God of gods, which is dear to Kṛṣṇa. Indeed, the vigil for Kṛṣṇa has been declared by the wise to be superior and not equal [to them].
The gods, such as Sūrya and Śakra, and the hosts, such as Brahmā and Rudra, always come to the vigil for the beloved of Kṛṣṇa.
The Gaṅgā, Sarasvatī, Revā, Yamunā, Śatahradā, Candrabhāgā, Vitastā, and indeed all rivers are truly present there.
O King, best of monarchs, on the eleventh day, all the lakes, ponds, and oceans go entirely to the vigil for Hari.
Those men who perform dance, song, and likewise the playing of the lute during the vigil for Kṛṣṇa are indeed more desirable than even the gods. || 34 ||
Whether with devotion or without devotion, whether pure or impure, by performing a vigil for Viṣṇu, one is liberated from millions of sins.
As many particles of dust from his feet as remain upon the ground, for that many thousands of years does he dwell in heaven as one who has kept vigil.
Therefore, one should go home after the vigil for Mādhava, and likewise on each of the twelve Dvādaśīs during the Kali age, for the destruction of impurity.
Even after committing many sins, the vigil for Hari shall burn away [the consequences] equal to Mount Meru, even those accumulated over hundreds of millions of eons.
O protector of the earth, listen as I describe the fruit obtained by those who, filled with devotion, have performed the Unmīlinī rite accompanied by a night vigil during the Kali age. (39)
A man obtains that same fruit by standing on one foot upon the earth for a thousand yugas on the banks of the Jāhnavī in Kāśī. || 40 ||
Whatever fruit is obtained by being without food for a thousand yugas, that same fruit is attained by performing a vigil for Hari after reaching the Unmīlinī festival.

The station of Viṣṇu, which is indeed difficult to attain even through the performance of hundreds of millions of sacrifices, is certainly reached with ease when a vigil is observed on the twelfth day.
Those who do not observe the vow of Viṣṇu accompanied by a night vigil—the sin of misappropriating others' property and adultery falls upon them. (43)
Even men devoid of spiritual cultivation, by means of a single fast alone, having all their sins utterly consumed, go to the forest of heaven.
Wherever there is the scripture of the Bhāgavata, wherever there is the vigil for Hari, and wherever there is the Śāligrāma stone—there Hari himself goes.
In the Kali age, the seven purifying cities do not exist, nor does the word of the Vedas; for the day of Viṣṇu, accompanied by a night vigil, is as purifying as they are.
Those men and women who do not perform the vigil on the day of Viṣṇu that has arrived, undoubtedly sink into a terrible hell. (47)

Thus ends the twenty-eighth chapter, titled "Description of the Greatness of the Twelve-Day Vigil," in the Fourth Section on the Greatness of Dvārakā, within the Seventh Book (Prabhāsa-khaṇḍa) of the Śrī Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a compendium of eighty-one thousand verses. || 28 ||
Prahlāda said: Now I shall further proclaim another great matter, more secret than the secret, the supreme merit and the most excellent majesty of Dvārakā. || 1 ||
I shall describe a captivating history of past events, which dispels the doubts of the sages and the deities of sacred fords, holy fields, and other such places.
O best of the twice-born, having seen his incomparable beauty when Jupiter was situated in the zodiac sign of Leo, Nārada, the beloved of the Blessed One, went to the Godāvarī. || 3 ||
Having beheld on all sides of Gautama’s hermitage the holy fords and all the rivers originating from the three worlds, he was filled with the utmost wonder.
Therein are Kāśī, Kurukṣetra, Ayodhyā, the city of Mathurā, Māyā, Kāñcī, and Avantī, together with forests and hermitages.
Harikṣetra, Gayā, Miśrakṣetra, Puruṣottama, Prabhāsa, and all other sacred sites of liberation without exception.
The Jāhnavī, Yamunā, Revā, and the meritorious Sarasvatī are there, as well as the Sarayū, Gaṇḍakī, Tāpī, and Payoṣṇī—the best among rivers.
The Kṛṣṇā, Bhīmarathī, and the holy Kāverī—these and other excellent rivers, existing in heaven, on earth, and in the netherworld, are all sacred pilgrimage sites.
She remained on the bank of the Godāvarī while Jupiter had entered the zodiac sign of Leo; likewise, there were the Puṣkara lakes and the seven great oceans.
The Meru and other mountains are meritorious, destroying sins through the mere sight of them; and Prayāga, the king of holy places, is accompanied by all sacred fords.
The Vedas and Upavedas, the Śāstras and Purāṇas in their entirety; all the Siddhas, the hosts of Munis, and the celestial Ṛṣis, Pitṛs, and deities. || 11 ||
While Jupiter was situated in Leo, the moon, the sun, and the hosts of gods remained on the banks of the Godāvarī for one year, filled with great joy.
Whatever holy places and sacred fields exist throughout the three worlds, they were all seen within the Gautamī, and [the sages] were struck with wonder.
There the celestial sage Nārada dwelt joyfully with the sages; and at the conclusion of the lion’s [penance], they all indeed departed for their own respective abodes.

Having addressed Queen Gautamī, they then stood before her; while all were listening, O brahmins, Gautamī, distressed in mind and tormented by association with wicked people, spoke sorrowfully to Nārada. (15)
Gautamī said: Behold these excellent holy places, the pure rivers beginning with the Gaṅgā, the oceans, the sacred mountains, and the triad of Gayās. (16)
O Nārada, all the fields born within the three worlds grant liberation, O dear one; so too do the gods, the ancestors, the Siddhas, the Ṛṣis, humans, and others. (17)

And Prayāga, the king of holy places, accompanied by all other sacred sites—O great sage, through my association with all of these, which have become purified, the three worlds shine with their radiance. (18)
O Lord, they all go back to their respective places; now I am exhausted, being scorched day and night. (19)
O Lord Nārada, through close association with wicked people, this evil-minded one had fallen into great sin; but now, by contact with the virtuous, he has attained auspiciousness.
All these, being joyful, go to their own respective abodes.
These meritorious accounts have been told by my grace; speak for the sake of pacifying your fatigue—being distressed, what shall I do? (22)
Prahlāda said: O twice-born ones, having heard the words of Godāvarī, the blessed Nārada, pained by grief and with a mind full of doubt, meditated for a moment and spoke.
Nārada said: "Oh, how truly wonderful is this great calamity of Gautamī! Let the gods, the foremost among sacred fords, holy fields, and rivers behold it without doubt. (24)
Reflect upon how the fire of sin in that city—where a constant store of true merit was surely established by you all—might be extinguished. (25)
Śrī Prahlāda said: O lords of sages, while all those of purified souls were thus reflecting, the venerable Gautama arrived there.
Having seen him, the sages and the gods worshipped him as was fitting; so too did the Jāhnavī, the Yamunā, the holy Narmadā, and the Sarasvatī.

And all other rivers that flow through the three worlds, as well as Vārāṇasī, Kurukṣetra, and the foremost sacred hermitages—all these together, having simultaneously paid homage to the sage, spoke to him.
O great sage, by your grace we have indeed been protected and thoroughly purified, now that you have brought the Gaṅgā, known as Gautamī, down to the surface of the earth.
All men have achieved their purpose and are freed from all sins; however, due to contact with the wicked, Gautamī is greatly distressed.
O Gautama, consider this: how is it that the goddess Suprabhā, liberated from all evils and overflowing with supreme bliss, was born? (31)
Prahlāda said: Having been addressed thus by them, the sage Gautama, his mind agitated with anxiety, looked at the face of Nārada and spoke while smiling. (32)
Gautama said: "The illustrious Gautamī, which destroys the great misfortunes of all sacred fields and holy fords—where can its heat be quenched? (33)

When Jupiter enters Leo, there is no sacred ford in the three worlds for bathing, nor any holy field that does not come to the Gautamī for purification, by whose grace even Kāśī, Prayāga, and other such sites shine with splendor. (34)
"Let all the sages dwelling in sacred fields and holy fords speak; having reflected upon what is pure, that which must be done by me in this time of crisis. (35)
Prahlāda said: Having spoken thus, all the sages, being utterly bewildered, said nothing; not knowing the remedy for that situation, Gautama spoke to Gautamī. (36)
Gautama said: "O Goddess, you have been brought here by me after propitiating Śaṅkara through ascetic penance; he will tell you the means. Having spoken thus, he then reflected.
Then Gautama, whose intellect was unimpaired, with faith and devotion [beheld] the Lord whose crest is the Gaṅgā; O stainless sages, listen to that great marvel which occurred. 38.
While the high-souled Gautama was meditating upon Mahādeva, a voice suddenly arose, gladdening the three worlds. (39)
O twice-born ones, that auspicious sound, which has no perceptible form, characteristic, or shape, filled all the directions up to the realm of Brahmā and dispelled all despondency.
The divine voice said: "Oh, what a great marvel! In this auspicious context, which bestows happiness upon all, even the wise are submerged in an ocean of suffering within this great sacred field."
Oho! O Teacher Gautama, O sages such as Nārada and others, please listen; out of compassion, I shall describe the holy places and sacred fields. 42.
