It is situated along the shore of the western ocean; and from here, in the northwestern direction, lies the supreme sacred field of Dvārakā.
There the holy Gomatī flows, joined by the ocean; there Mahāviṣṇu is eternally stationed, facing westward.
It is always declared to be the place of burning for heaps of many fierce evils, just as fire is for pieces of fuel. (45)
Where, having burnt away the wondrous sin born from the slaughter of the three worlds—the universal deceiver—the [flame] shines forever like the sun. (46)
Therefore, O highly fortunate ones, proceed toward the Gomatī, the burner of sins, keeping the Godāvarī—endowed with sacred fields and holy fords—in front of you. (47)
O best of the twice-born, having reached the holy Dvāravatī through my grace and by the power of Dvārakā, truth shall manifest itself.
Prahlāda said: When this had been spoken, they all, their minds overflowing with joy upon hearing of that most excellent sacred field, roared with the names of Hari.
"Victory! Victory has been won by us! We are blessed, most blessed! By good fortune, delusion has departed; the supreme among holy places has been discovered. (50)
Then all the sacred fords (tīrthas), together with the holy sites, forests, and hermitages—Vārāṇasī, Prayāga, and the rest—as well as the lakes, rivers, and mountains [all came there]. (51)
And having heard these words, the ancestors—both divine and human—who had come to the sacred pools at Gayā, were greatly delighted and cried out, "Victory! Victory! (52).
Oh, what a most excellent field for all of us, the destroyer of our sins! Salutation with my head to Dvārakā, the king of kings and the sovereign of sacred pilgrimage sites.

Śrī Prahlāda said: Having heard of the field that is the most excellent of all, the sacred ford that is the most excellent among the most excellent, and the God who is the most excellent of gods—Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the destroyer of afflictions—(he went there). 54.
Indeed, an unsurpassed longing for the sacred fords and other such sites arose within them; then, all of them simultaneously spoke these words to one another.
The sages, holy fords, and gods said: "When shall we behold the meritorious Dvārakā protected by Kṛṣṇa, and the divine form of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, his most beautiful face? (56)
"When indeed will our bath in the Gomatī take place? Having bathed at Cakratīrtha, when shall we behold the temple of Lord Kṛṣṇa—that most meritorious, open gateway to liberation? (57)

O twice-born ones, residence in Dvārakā is difficult to attain; the sight of Kṛṣṇa is difficult to attain; bathing in the Gomatī is difficult to attain; and the sight of Rukmiṇī is difficult to attain. (58)

Thus ends the twenty-ninth chapter, titled "The Description of the Gomatī River," preceded by the eagerness to go to Dvārakā after hearing the power of Dvārakā from the divine speech regarding all the holy fords, sacred sites, and other locations situated on the banks of the Gautamī, within the fourth section, the Dvārakā-māhātmya, of the seventh book, the Prabhāsa-khaṇḍa, of the Śrī Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a compendium of eighty-one thousand verses. || 29 ||
Śrī Prahlāda said: Then, all those holy pilgrimage sites and sacred fields experienced great joy in every way, desiring to go to the meritorious city of Dvāravatī.
Upon seeing Nārada and Gautama arrive at Dvārakā, a great and enchanting festival will take place there.
They declared, "One must go on a pilgrimage to Kṛṣṇa among the sacred fords. Then those sages and gods, accompanied by all the holy sites, [set out]. || 3 ||

Placing Gautamī at their head, they went joyfully to Dvāravatī; then all the holy fords, sacred fields, and forests in their entirety, as well as the sages and gods, arrived at Dvārakā with great delight.
With supreme faith and devotion, longing for a vision of Kṛṣṇa, they spoke on the road to Nārada, who was an expert in the true essence of the lute’s sound.
The sages said: "Indeed, these are heaps of masses of merit, as well as of austerities, sacrifices, gifts, vows, and great sacred fords upon the earth."
This grace has been obtained by us, that we shall behold Kuśasthalī; we now indeed question you, the supreme teacher of yogins.
O Sage, what ritual procedure is proclaimed for the pilgrimage to Dvārakā? What rule should be observed here, and what is to be avoided? (8)

What is to be heard, what is to be glorified, and what indeed is to be remembered along the way? What festivals are proclaimed there on the road to Dvārakā? O highly fortunate one, please describe all of this in detail, for each [festival] increases the joy of the devotees. (10)
Śrī Nārada said: Having performed an oil massage on the previous day and having worshipped Hari with faith, one should, being well-pleased, feed Vaiṣṇava brāhmaṇas according to one's own capacity.
Permitted by Mahāviṣṇu and having indeed enjoyed his grace, he should lie down upon the ground, well-pleased, with his mind fixed on Kṛṣṇa and Dvārakā.

On the following day, having bathed and become pure, he worshipped the Lord of the Universe; having circumambulated and prostrated before Mahāviṣṇu with his permission, and having consulted the family elders as well as dear Vaiṣṇava Brāhmaṇas.
Then, permitted by him, he, filled with great joy, should undertake the commencement of the procession in Dvārakā amidst the praises of songs and instrumental music.
Going toward Dvārakā, he should always remain peaceful, self-controlled, and pure; with his senses restrained, he should observe celibacy and sleep on the ground.
The recitation of the Thousand Names, as well as the recitation of the Purāṇas, should be performed; likewise, one’s mind should be compassionate, and one should attend upon the virtuous. (16)
When one possesses wealth, every act such as the giving of food—even if performed to a small extent according to one's own capacity—becomes multiplied ten millionfold.
Whoever offers even a single morsel of food with devotion on the path of Kṛṣṇa has, by that act, given away the earth unto its furthest islands; there is no end to his merit.

How much more so in the sacred field of Dvārakā, in the presence of Kṛṣṇa! In the Kali age, for every single grain [of rice offered], one obtains the fruit of ten thousand Rājasūya sacrifices. || 19 ||
Those men who have performed thousands upon hundreds of *śrāddha* rites at Gayā, and who have given gifts of food on the path to Dvārakā—[for them, the merit is complete]. (20)

Medicine, food and drink, sandals, as well as a blanket, garments, shoes, and wealth—provided it is available—he who is wise should avoid mixing these with others, and likewise avoid idle chatter with the crowds.
A wise person, even when possessing wealth, should abandon reviling others, backbiting, deceiving others, eating the food of others, and enjoying the cooked meals of others. (22)
There is no fault for one of meager means to possess only that much; he should listen to the true discourse on Viṣṇu, which is the nectar of the chanting of His names. 23.
By those traveling on the road to Dvārakā, Vedic prayers, hymns, and likewise scriptural praises that increase mutual devotion should be recited.
The fruit that is proclaimed for the pilgrimage to Śrī Kṛṣṇa in the Kali age cannot be told by me even with mouths as numerous as the number of Yugas.
O best of the twice-born, all that was asked has now been told; therefore, strive with diligence for the swift attainment of Viṣṇu.
Śrī Prahlāda said: Thus addressed by Nārada, those sages, their minds filled with joy, all together performed that path for the sake of Lord Kṛṣṇa.
Some hear those virtuous stories of Viṣṇu, world-renowned, by the mere hearing of which the Blessed One enters the heart. (28)
These names, when being recited, indeed bestow great merit; they are always purifying in the world, O Brahmins, especially in the Kali age.
The divine Purāṇa-saṃhitās proclaimed by the sages reveal the most auspicious majesty of Viṣṇu. (30)
The six qualities and the heroic deeds performed by Viṣṇu in the past through the forms of his playful incarnations, they listen to with supreme joy.
Others, filled with supreme devotion, recount the most auspicious deeds of Vāsudeva with joy and eyes brimming with tears. || 32 ||
Others remember the Lord of Gods, the omnipresent one who is without beginning or end; some sages recite hymns with supreme joy.
Some sages chant the hundred names on the road, others the thousand names, and still others the hundred-thousand names.
Some, filled with joy, sang worldly songs about the names of Hari; others went forth in processions adorned with banners and other ornaments. || 35 ||
With the sound of singing and instrumental music, and with the resonance of hand-clapping, there is no one more blessed than him in all the three worlds. (36)
He for whom the unsurpassed vision of the Vaiṣṇavas has arisen, as well as the meritorious Jāhnavī, Yamunā, and Sarasvatī [have likewise appeared]. (37)
The Revā and all other rivers performed songs and dances, as did the holy sites such as Prayāga, the oceans, and the foremost mountains.

Vārāṇasī, Kurukṣetra, and all other sacred places in their entirety—whatever holy fords and fields exist in the three worlds, O leaders of the gods—they performed songs and dances upon the auspicious path of Dvārakā. (39)
For those walking on the path to Dvārakā, with every single step taken, there is the merit of thousands of sacrifices equal to the number of those footprints.
Then all those sages, including Nārada and others, accompanied by pilgrims and those visiting sacred sites, beheld from afar the glorious abode of Kṛṣṇa.

Thus ends the thirtieth chapter, titled "The Description of the Festive Procession for the Departure of the Tīrthas, Sacred Sites, Deities, and Great Sages toward Dvārakā," in the fourth section, the *Dvārakāmāhātmya*, of the seventh book, the *Prabhāsakhaṇḍa*, of the *Śrī Skanda Mahāpurāṇa*, a compendium of eighty-one thousand verses.
Prahlāda said:
Constantly destroying the darkness of living beings with his divine radiance, he generates supreme bliss for his devotees and removes their fear.
With banners fixed upon its flags, increasing the victory of Dvārakā, it shines like the king of mountains with the manifestation of divine merit. || 2 ||
Then, having beheld the abode of Viṣṇu adorned with his weapons, she left her sandals and parasol and fell prostrate upon the ground like a staff.
O tigers among brahmins, there occurred a great and wonderful upheaval of the ground for those holy places, as well as for the sacred fields and all other sites, in every respect.
Vārāṇasī, Kurukṣetra, Prayāga, and likewise the Jāhnavī; the holy Yamunā, the holy Narmadā, and the holy eastern Sarasvatī.
The Godāvarī is greatly meritorious; Gayā, Śāligrāma, and the great sacred field (Mahākṣetra) are the three auspicious ones; and the holy Cakranadī is auspicious.
The Payoṣṇī, Tapatī, Kṛṣṇā, Kāverī, and other rivers that bestow great merit; the holy sites such as Puṣkara; the oceans; and the most excellent mountains—[all these are present here]. || 7 ||
Ayodhyā, Mathurā, Māyā, Avantī, and others grant liberation; and especially Śrīraṅga, known as Ananta, and Prabhāsa.
Puruṣottama, Mahākṣetra, Araṇyānī, and other auspicious places—all the sacred fords (tīrthas) existing everywhere throughout the three worlds—[are present here]. || 9 ||
Having beheld the meritorious abode of Kṛṣṇa, they were repeatedly filled with great joy; they roared with shouts of "Victory!", cries of "Obeisance!", and the names of Hari.
Shedding tears of joy and with voices faltering from love, all the sages and all the sacred fords (tīrthas) and other entities praised him from every side.
Then, as they were praising one another with joyful hearts, the great seer Nārada, beholding the faces of them all, spoke: (12)
Śrī Nārada said: "O you who have created these excellent heaps of merit, that temple of Kṛṣṇa which was seen by you is such that it could not be seen even through thousands of births."
The vision of Lord Kṛṣṇa and the resolve to go to Dvārakā—this firm devotion to Mahāviṣṇu is not the fruit of meager austerity. (14)
Blessed indeed are those ancestors whose lineage members go to Dvārakā with great festivity to behold Kṛṣṇa and see the beloved of Hari. (19)
Blessed is this Gautamī Gaṅgā, and blessed is this Gautama of great asceticism, by whose grace the welfare of all has been established. (16)
O you who are like all sacred fords, we have obtained the full fruit of sacrifices, Vedic study, charity, austerities, vows, and meditative concentrations through you. (17)
By the command of Kṛṣṇa, you all, together with all the deities, must remain at all times in all the holy fords and sacred fields in their entirety. (18)
Blessed are those who dwell here, even for a single day, for they are sanctified; O highly fortunate ones, behold the Godāvarī and the Jāhnavī meeting here.
And let these illustrious ones behold this auspicious Dvārakā, beloved of Kṛṣṇa, as well as the beautiful Vārāṇasī. || 20 ||
Let them behold the foremost fields of the Lord, such as Dvārakā; likewise Mathurā, Kāśī, Māyā, and Ayodhyā shine forth. (21)
Neither Avantī nor Kāñcī, nor Puruṣottama-kṣetra, nor even Kurukṣetra shines at the time of a solar eclipse. || 22 ||
There is no sacred site like Gayā-tīrtha as this one appears.
Just as the sun shines resplendent among the planets, lunar mansions, and stars, so does the sun of Dvārakā shine resplendent among the sacred fields and the kings of holy fords.
Prahlāda said: Having heard what was spoken by Nārada, the twice-born ones were likewise delighted; and placing all the sacred fields and holy fords before them, they honored Gautama. (25)
Leaving Gautamī there, they proceeded forward, each one before the other; Gautamī, being delighted, bowed there and departed in haste.
Accompanied by songs, instrumental music, dances, and banners on all sides, as well as with the recitation of hymns, they all proceeded toward their refuge in Dvārakā.
Placing the sacred fords before him and keeping the beautiful Prayāga, the king of holy places, in the middle, he was filled with joy at the sight of that field.
Thereafter, that best of sages performed his ritual bath in the rivers: the Jāhnavī, Gautamī, Revā, Yamunā, and the eastern Sarasvatī.
The Sarayū, Gaṇḍakī, Tāpī, Payoṣṇī, Yamunā, as well as the Kṛṣṇā, Bhīmarathī, Gaṅgā, and Kāverī, which destroy all sins; || 30 ||
The highly meritorious Mandākinī and the holy river Bhogavatī—all of them proceed together, beholding the city of Dvārakā. || 31 ||
Then those seven oceans, accompanied by their respective sacred bathing places (tīrthas), followed, and after them came the forests joined with holy hermitages.
Then the beautiful and most splendid mountains, such as Meru and others, began to dance and sing praises with great sages.
Then the sages and the gods, their minds filled with joy on all sides, sang, danced, and roared the names of Hari.

Gladdened by the loud sounds of musical instruments and shouts of victory, they reached the bank of the Gomatī accompanied by all the sacrificial materials; all those highly meritorious ones, with joyful hearts, offered their salutations.
Śrī Nārada said: O Bhāgīrathī, O Revā, O Yamunā, listen, O Gautamī! The most excellent Goddess Śrī Gomatī is renowned throughout the three worlds. (36)

A single bath in her rivals even the knowledge of Brahman; therefore, this Gomatī is indeed the most excellent among all sacred fords (tīrthas). People are liberated by the knowledge of Brahman or by death at Prayāga, but one is liberated along with one's ancestors merely by bathing in the Gomatī. (37)
Prahlāda said: Having heard of those holy places and the great, wonderful majesty of the Gomatī, they bathed with faith and proceeded ahead amidst festive celebrations.
Then the sacred fields, holy fords, rivers, oceans, and other such places beheld the beautiful Dvārakā as they arrived at the gateway pavilion.
She was seated upon a divine lion-throne adorned with jewels and gold; she was beautiful, white in complexion, and possessed a radiance equal to that of Rudra and the Ādityas.
She was clad in divine garments, rich with fragrance, adorned with jeweled ornaments, and beautified by divine crowns, earrings, bracelets, and other finery.

Her hands display the gestures of granting boons and fearlessness, and she holds the conch, discus, and mace as weapons; she is enriched by the splendor of a white parasol and attended by chowries, fans, and other such items.

Seeing the city of Dvāravatī situated upon a great lion-throne, being praised with hymns and delighted by songs, instrumental music, and other festivities, they all simultaneously bowed down with perfect devotion. (43)

Thus ends the thirty-first chapter, titled "The Description of the Vision of Embodied Dvāravatī," in the fourth section on the Greatness of Dvārakā, within the seventh book, the Prabhāsa-khaṇḍa, of the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a compendium of eighty-one thousand verses. || 31 ||
Prahlāda said: Nārada, having gone ahead and bowed to the beloved of Hari, spoke these charming words, gladdening the city of Dvārakā.
Śrī Nārada said: Behold, behold, O highly fortunate and beautiful lady! All the sacred fords and holy sites, as well as the gods and sages, have arrived here in their entirety.
Behold this Prayāga arrived before you along with holy pilgrims; they roll about in devotion at your lotus feet in Dvārakā in a most wonderful manner.
But this auspicious Puṣkara tīrtha bows with faith; and this meritorious Gautamī is the refuge of all tīrthas. (4)
When Jupiter was situated in Leo, O auspicious one, she attained great good fortune; however, through association with the wicked, she was severely scorched by the fire of sin.
Having understood the means there while the sages were listening, and having heard a great sound in her ear, she has now arrived in your presence.
"O Goddess, the auspicious Gautamī in Dvārakā bows to you. Behold, behold this most meritorious and auspicious Bhāgīrathī! (7)
With great joy, she bows her head again and again at your feet; behold this lovely Narmadā, prostrate at your feet.
The Yamunā, the Candrabhāgā, this Prācī Sarasvatī, the Sarayū, the Gaṇḍakī have arrived, as has the Gomatī flowing toward the east.
The Śoṇa, the Sindhu river, and these other excellent rivers—the Kṛṣṇā, the Bhīmarathī, the holy Kāverī, and other such preeminent streams—[are likewise sacred]. || 10 ||
The Sītā, Cakṣu, and Bhadrā rivers bow to his lotus feet; these highly meritorious ones in Dvārakā, as well as other supreme rivers arising from the seven continents, do the same.
Behold this wonder, O blessed lady: Vārāṇasī, the bestower of liberation, is joined by the highly meritorious Mandākinī, Bhogavatī, and others. 12.
And with devotion, placing your lotus feet upon his head, he dwells there; he bows to you day and night at Kurukṣetra, which is greatly meritorious. (13)
"Behold Mathurā from Dvārakā, prostrating at your feet; Ayodhyā and Avantikā have arrived and bow to your lotus feet. (14)
Kāñcī, Gayā, and Viśālā roll upon the earth; the great sacred field of Śāligrāma has fallen at your feet; and the fields of Prabhāsa and Puruṣottama shine forth. (15)
O beautiful one, all other sacred fields, beginning with Bhārgava, bow down to you in Dvārakā, rising up again and again with devotion.
Behold these seven oceans fallen at your feet; behold all the forests, and Naimiṣa bowing before you.
Behold Dhanuṣka, Daśāraṇya, Daṇḍakāraṇya, Arbuda, Nārāyaṇāśrama, and likewise that which is bowed down at Dvārakā.

This Mount Meru, Kailāsa, Mandara, and thousands of others; the Himālaya, the Vindhya mountain, Śrīśaila, and the rest—were all filled with great joy. Indeed, all these hosts of sages bowed down again and again. (19)
The Gaṅgā and other rivers, the oceans, and the mountains dance before you; all the hosts of sages and gods roar with your names. (20)

Śrī Prahlāda said: While he was speaking thus, Dvārakā, her mind delighted, seeing everyone dancing with joy and greeting them with affection, touched Gautamī with her hand and spoke these charming words.
Then, with sweet words, she delighted all the sacred sites and others everywhere, such as Bhāgīrathī and Prayāga, as well as Dvārakā.
Then a wonder occurred there, increasing the joy of all; at that very moment, sounds of singing, instrumental music, and cries of "Victory! arose in the sky.
Then all the leaders of the gods, beginning with Brahmā, beheld the most meritorious roars, each distinct with the sounds of "Hari."
Maheśa was seen together with his own attendants and Bhavānī; Indra, meanwhile, was seen together with the thirty gods, as well as the yakṣas, gandharvas, and kinnaras.
Dancing with great joy along with the Maruts and the world-protectors, all the Siddhas and Vidyādharas, as well as the Vasus, Ādityas, and the planets, [were present]. (26)
Bhṛgu and the others, as well as Sanaka and the others, being greatly delighted, danced; and the gods residing in the seven heavens, having paid homage to Brahmā, [did likewise].
Then, having beheld Dvārakā, Brahmā, Īśāna, and the others spoke, their souls overwhelmed with joy and filled with wonder as they looked at one another.
The gods said: "This very city of Dvārakā flows where the Gomatī river runs; where the Blessed Lord Kṛṣṇa resides, this holy city shines forth."
This Dvārakā shines upon the earth as the most excellent of all sacred fields and the highest of all holy fords; it is even superior to heaven itself.
This indeed is Cakratīrtha, which is the stone marked with the discus; it grants liberation to sinners in this world and is worshipped even in the land of the Mlecchas.

Prahlāda said: Having seen Brahmā and the others arrive, Nārada and the rest were struck with wonder; the sacred fields, the foremost holy fords, and the best of rivers were all filled with amazement. Then everyone—every one of them, all of them, in every way—simultaneously offered their salutations.
O best of Brahmins, having witnessed the enchanting procession of Brahmā and the other holy ones toward Dvārakā, the inhabitants of Dvārakā were filled with wonder.
Seeing [this], all the hosts of gods in their palaces toward Dvārakā were filled with great joy, dancing to the sounds of songs, musical instruments, and the like. || 34 ||
Uttering cries of "Victory! and saying, "This is the beloved of Kṛṣṇa," Brahmā and Maheśvara, their minds filled with joy upon seeing Dvārakā, [departed]. (35)
Having abandoned their excellent vehicles, they fell prostrate upon the ground like staffs, and then, filled with joy, the two gods spoke toward Dvārakā.
O Mother, you are the most excellent of all, even compared to ourselves and others, because the imperishable Lord Viṣṇu himself never abandons you.
Therefore, show us the Lord of Gods, Kṛṣṇa, the destroyer of Kaṃsa, by whose sight great perfection shall come to all. (38)
Prahlāda said: Having spoken thus, the Goddess departed, accompanied by the holy fords and sacred fields, placing Brahmā and Īśāna at her head, as she joyfully beheld the great festivals.
Then Dvārakā, overwhelmed with joy, approached the gods accompanied by songs, instrumental music, and banners, with divine offerings in their hands, and spoke to them.
O gods, behold, behold! This very one is the Lord of Dvārakā. The fruit that belongs to those who have attained his vision does not exist even among thousands of Brahmāṇḍas. || 41 ||

Then all the hosts of gods, accompanied by sacred fields, holy fords, and other sanctuaries, beheld Kṛṣṇa, the destroyer of afflictions, facing the west; having approached him, they all bowed down simultaneously, filled with great joy.
Accompanied on all sides by the sounds of singing and instrumental music, they danced while shouting cries of "Victory! and "Homage!", chanting the names of Hari.
Brahmā, Bhava, Bhavānī, and the hosts of gods including Indra, having seen Kṛṣṇa on earth, bowed down to him again and again, rising up with devotion.

The holy places such as Prayāga, the pure rivers such as the Gaṅgā, the sages, the gods and gandharvas, Śuka and others, and Sanaka and others—having beheld the face of Mahāviṣṇu, they bowed down again and again. || 45 ||

Crying out "Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa! O Kṛṣṇa! Victory to Kṛṣṇa!", Brahmā, seated upon his lotus throne, bathed in the waters of the Gomatī on the shore of the great ocean and joyfully worshipped the glorious Kṛṣṇa.
Having bathed [the deity] with the milk of the celestial cow and with the five divine nectars (amṛtas), Bhava and Bhavānī then worshipped [him] with devotion.
Indra, all the hosts of gods, the yogis beginning with Sanaka, the sages beginning with Nārada, and the best of rivers beginning with the Gaṅgā—[all these were there]. || 48 ||
With priceless ornaments fashioned from great jewels, offered with devotion, and with many divine garlands produced in the Nandana grove and other celestial realms; || 49 ||
Together with their beloved Śrītulasī, they indeed worshipped the glorious Kṛṣṇa with divine incenses, lustration rites (nīrājana), and camphor, each offered separately.
With various kinds of food offerings, divine flowers scented with camphor, betel leaves mixed with camphor, and likewise with other beloved presents; || 51 ||

Having thus worshipped Mahāviṣṇu Kṛṣṇa, the destroyer of afflictions, with all kinds of highly auspicious and divine hymns of praise, they all danced with great joy, delighted by songs and musical instruments.
In the presence of Lord Kṛṣṇa were the Apsarases; then Brahmā, the sons of Brahmā, and the hosts of Maruts together with Indra.
Seeing Brahmā and the others dancing, the lotus-eyed Lord, the all-pervading one, being pleased, restrained them with his hand and spoke to the gods.

The Blessed Lord said: "O Brahmā, O Maheśāna, O Bhavānī, O Maheśvarī! [You have summoned] the sacred fields, all the holy fords (tīrthas), Nārada, Sanaka and the others. I am well-pleased with you; you shall obtain all your desires."
Prahlāda said: Then, having obtained all those desired boons that grant every wish, they, filled with supreme joy, spoke to the glorious Kṛṣṇa with the highest devotion.
The gods said: O All-pervading Lord, by Your grace we have obtained our desired boon from every aspect: auspicious and unfailing devotion, full of love, toward Your lotus feet. (57)
Prahlāda said: In that same manner, they worshipped Rukmiṇī, the beloved of Kṛṣṇa; then Brahmā and Maheśāna—listen to this from me, O all of you. (58)
Endowed with supreme faith, they replied toward Dvārakā: "O Goddess, you are the most excellent of all sacred fords and holy fields. (59)
Just as Meru is among mountains, as the ocean is among rivers, as the vital breath is among bodies, and as the mind is indeed among the senses; || 60 ||

Just as fire is worshipped among luminous things, as the Caitya is worshipped among the principles (tattvas), as the moon is indeed the fixed point among the planets, constellations, and stars, and as the sun shines among these masses of light; || 61 ||
Just as this great Mahāviṣṇu is the greatest among all the gods, so too is this auspicious Dvārakā worthy of worship among all sacred fords (tīrthas). 62.
Prahlāda said: Having spoken thus, O best of beings, the two lords of the gods consecrated Dvārakā in the sovereignty over all the deities, sacred fields, and other such places. (63)
Brahmā and Īśāna, as well as the gods, the lords of progeny, and the stainless sages, are the cause of its status as the great king among holy fords and royal sacred sites.
Greatly rejoicing, they performed the great consecration ceremony for Dvārakā during the grand festival, sounding various musical instruments.

With divine five nectars (pañcāmṛta), with waters originating from all sacred fords (tīrtha), and with the meritorious waters of the celestial Gaṅgā lifted by the trunks of the elephants of the quarters; || 66 ||
Then, having given divine garments and likewise water for sipping, she was anointed with divine sandalwood pastes and adorned with divine ornaments.
And they performed worship with flowers produced from sandalwood and other substances; then those great divine beings became the attendants (pārṣadas) of Hari.
Viṣvaksena, Sunanda, and others, illuminating the ten directions, uttered shouts of "Victory! and "Salutations!", raining down flowers.
Dancing to the sound of singing and instrumental music, they were filled with great joy; they were adorned with crowns, earrings, necklaces, and the Vaijayantī garland.
Seeing Brahmā and Maheśvara, who were dark-complexioned, four-armed, adorned with yellow garments and garlands, and blazing with their own radiance, [the gods spoke]. (71)
[They saw] Nārada and the sages Sanaka and others, who were great devotees of the Lord; they too, being greatly delighted, were overcome with excitement born of joy. (72)
Then, filled with joy, they honored one another with embraces and other gestures; the other sages and gods also bowed down to the attendants of Viṣṇu.
Then those attendants of Viṣṇu, having arrived at Dvārakā, bowed to the Lord of Dvārakā as well as to the city of Dvārakā itself.
Having worshipped with faith and devotion using various divine flowers produced in that forest of supreme bliss, as well as with Tulasī grown in that same forest; || 75 ||
Having offered divine fruits produced from that [tree], incense, lustration rites (nīrājana), and various kinds of food and betel-leaves, they gratified the Lord Kṛṣṇa.
"O Sovereign Lady, you are the Great Queen of all kings of sacred fields, holy fords, and the like"—saying this, they all paid homage to Dvārakā. (77)
In the meantime, O brahmins, the sounds of celestial drums were heard as great noises, and showers of flowers fell. (78)
Now, O best of sages, listen to this great marvel: Kurukṣetra and Prayāga were on the left and right sides [respectively]. (79)
Standing there, they took up two divine, beautiful white umbrellas, as well as two auspicious, bright yak-tail fans at the gates of Dvārakā.
Ayodhyā, Mathurā, Māyā, Vārāṇasī, and Jayasvana—these and all other sacred sites praise him in every way. (81)
As he gazed upon the sacred fords, all the rivers, and the lotus-face of Dvārakā, gods and men attained supreme bliss.
And the attendants of Viṣṇu said: "Blessed indeed are all these people everywhere, having beheld the holy Dvārakā, the sole ornament of all the worlds. (83)

When Hari is properly propitiated by one through the Vedas, sacrifices, austerities, and the chanting of prayers, He becomes gracious toward that person; for such a person, the inclination to go to Dvārakā shall arise. (84)

Thus ends the thirty-second chapter, titled "The Description of the Greatness of Dvārakā as Narrated by Viṣṇu’s Attendants," in the fourth section (Dvārakāmāhātmya) of the seventh book (Prabhāsakhaṇḍa) of the Śrī Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a compendium of eighty-one thousand verses. || 32 ||
Śrī Prahlāda said: Having heard what had been spoken by the attendants of Viṣṇu regarding the greatness of Dvārakā, Brahmā and Maheśāna spoke in order to describe it.
The illustrious Brahmā and Īśāna said: "O holy fields, sacred fords, lakes, oceans, and so forth; the pilgrimage sites such as Prayāga, and Kāśī and others which bestow liberation! || 2 ||
O you kings of holy fords, this auspicious Dvārakā is indeed to be served by you, the great king; therefore, remain outside at your own pleasure.

Śrī Prahlāda said: Upon hearing the words of Maheśa, there was a festival for everyone. Then, having performed circumambulation and prostrated before Dvārakā, the sacred sites and holy places (kṣetra-tīrthas) joyfully made their residence there.
The Bhāgīrathī, Prayāga, the Yamunā, and the Sarasvatī; the meritorious Sarayū and Gaṇḍakī, and the Gomatī flowing toward the east.

Furthermore, all other rivers as well as the Sindhu and Śoṇa rivers, situated in the northern quarter along with fifty crores of holy pilgrimage sites, were intent on the service of Kṛṣṇa as they gazed repeatedly upon Dvārakā.
Likewise, the meritorious Mandākinī, the river Bhāgīrathī, the great river Narmadā, the Śiprā, and the Prācī Sarasvatī; || 7 ||
The Cakṣurbhadrā, the Sītā, and other rivers that destroy sins are situated in the eastern quarter along with sixty crores of sacred fords (tīrthas).
The Payoṣṇī, the holy Tapatī, and the water-rich Vidarbhā; the highly meritorious Godāvarī, as well as the Bhīmā and the Kṛṣṇā river.
The holy rivers, headed by the Kāverī, along with others that destroy sins, accompanied by their own sacred bathing places, arrived with devotion in nine hundred and ninety million.
Situated in the southern region, eager to serve Dvārakā, they sport in the waters of the Gomatī and on its banks in the presence of Kṛṣṇa.
Whatever excellent rivers exist in the seven continents, as well as other such great rivers, and likewise the seven oceans situated in the western direction—[all these were brought there]. || 12 ||
They indeed sport at Cakratīrtha along with hundreds of millions of other holy sites, and they constantly behold Kṛṣṇa, who always faces the west.
And in all the intermediate directions, there is no counting of sacred fords (tīrthas): Puṣkara and other holy sites, Viśālā, Virajā, and Gayā.
O best of the twice-born, one hundred times ten million sacred fords exist at the confluence of the Gomatī and the ocean, where they remain engaged in the service of Kṛṣṇa amidst great festivities.
Vārāṇasī is situated in the northeast; Avantī is located in the eastern direction; Kāntī is in the southeast, and Mathurā is situated in the south. (16)
Likewise, Māyā is in the southwest, and Ayodhyā is situated in the west; Kurukṣetra is in the northwest, and Harikṣetra is in the north.
Śivakṣetra is in the northeast, Puruṣottama in the east, Bhṛgukṣetra in the southeast, and Prabhāsa is situated in the south.
Śrīraṅga is in the south-western quarter, Lohadaṇḍa in the west, the Nārasiṃha temples in the north-west, and likewise Kokāmukhya in the north.
Kāmākhyā, Reṇukā, and all other Śākteya sites, as well as all the kings of sacred fields (kṣetrarāja), indeed dwell in their respective locations. || 20 ||
Furthermore, O twice-born ones, there are entirely solar and Gāṇapatya sacred sites (kṣetras) to the north, situated in the vicinity of Rukmiṇī.
Dhenuka, Naimiṣa forest, Daṇḍaka, and likewise Saindhava; Daśāraṇya, Arbuda, and the hermitage of Nara and Nārāyaṇa. || 22 ||
Just as directed, the mountains beginning with Meru dwelt on all sides around Dvārakā; eager to serve Dvārakā, they resided in the northern quarter.
Kailāsa and other mountains are in the northeast; Himavat and others are in the east; Śrīśaila and others are in the southeast; and Siṃhādri and others are likewise in the south.

In the southwest are Vāmamārgī and others, Mahendra, Ṛṣabha, and the rest; there are also other meritorious mountains, along with Lokāloka and Mānasa. They are situated all around Dvārakā and attend upon it every day.
In this way, the gods beginning with Brahmā and the sages beginning with Sanaka were endowed with sacred fields, holy fords, and other such most meritorious things.
With supreme faith and devotion, while Jupiter is situated in the sign of Virgo, Brahmā and the other gods arrive at Dvārakā to behold it, filled with great joy. (27)

Thus ends the thirty-third chapter, titled "The Description of the Residence of All Tīrthas, Kṣetras, and Other Sites in Dvārakā, Preceded by the Description of the Majesty of Dvārakā," in the fourth section (Dvārakāmāhātmya) of the seventh book (Prabhāsakhaṇḍa) of the Śrī Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a compendium of eighty-one thousand verses. || 33 ||
Śrī Prahlāda said: O lords of sages, such is the wonderful majesty of Dvārakā, which shatters all great sins among all sacred fields and pilgrimage sites.
It is declared to be the remover of great sins for those of all castes and stages of life, and especially for those who have fallen; it increases great merit.
O Brahmins, it is traditionally held that Dvārakā is a place of burning for heaps of most terrible sins; how much more so, then, is residing in Dvārakā?
Especially, O best of Brahmins, when Jupiter is situated in the sign of Virgo, even Brahmā and the other gods are seen there together with sacred fords (tīrthas). || 4 ||
Those men who make the journey to Dvārakā every year—even sinners—attain heaven by touching the dust of their feet.
For those purified by the waters of the Gomatī who gaze upon the face of Kṛṣṇa, the sins accumulated over hundreds of births depart simply from that sight.
O best of sages, listen to this ancient history previously mentioned in the dialogue between Dilīpa and Vasiṣṭha, which increases the greatest wonder.
In Kāśī, however, even an adamantine coating perishes in a single field; having heard this from the traveler’s account, Dilīpa spoke these words. (8)
Dilīpa said: "Is there that which exists where even the terrible adamantine cement (vajralepa) in Kāśī is destroyed entirely, and where great merit is thereby obtained?"
O best of the twice-born, tell me of that meritorious field where sins do not sprout, and where sin is utterly destroyed.

Vasiṣṭha said: Formerly, in Kāśī, there was a certain ascetic carrying three staffs who was a knower of the dharma of liberation; he remained concentrated, chanting the Gāyatrī mantra ten times for every Aśvamedha sacrifice.
There, a certain young woman with the gait of an elephant arrived; having placed her garments on the bank to relieve her fatigue, she entered the water naked and engaged in water-sports.
Seeing her naked as she played, the ascetic was filled with passion; by fate, he was cast from the path of righteousness and suddenly became utterly deluded.
She too desired that young ascetic in her mind; thus, a union occurred there between those two of sinful deeds.
Deluded by her, he immediately followed after her alone; and for her sake, he then acquired wealth through unjust means.
For in Vārāṇasī, even the acceptance of gifts from a Caṇḍāla was not abandoned; though always sinful and devoid of ritual bathing, he lived by means of theft at night. || 16 ||
At one time, a wicked man seeking meat went to the forest; there he beheld a woman, a Mātaṅgī with intoxicating eyes.
Seeing her first youth, he was overcome by pride and sin; then, in that desolate forest, he approached the meeting place of the Mātaṅgī river.
Deluded by sin, he engaged in eating food, drink, and other things with her; that man, greedy for vice, ate mud and cow-flesh along with liquor. || 19 ||
Having met his death in that house, that sinful soul who was a devourer of all things did not then fall into hell due to the power of Vārāṇasī.
However, the extremely terrible sin committed there was like an adamantine coating; through the sin of contact with a Śūdra woman, he was born into these cruel wombs.
He became a wolf, a tiger, a serpent, a dog, a jackal, and a boar; having undergone these endless torments, he finds not even a trace of peace.
Thus, even after thousands of births and ten thousand yugas, the sin born of his union with the Mātaṅgī woman was not destroyed for that man of evil deeds.
Then, in his seventh birth, he was born as a hare; thereafter, that evil-souled one was born as a Rākṣasa who devoured everything.
Having devoured all living beings, he arrived at the Vindhya mountain; immediately after this, he was to become a wondrous lizard.
Through the sin born of union with a Śūdra woman, one must be reborn in the womb of a worm; indeed, the fruit declared for sexual union with a Mātaṅgī woman is utterly loathsome.
O Dilīpa, listen to this great and most wonderful event that occurred there—a terrible thing destined to be experienced for ten thousand times ten thousand ages. (27)
And on the Vindhya mountain, everyone beheld a sight that was a source of wonder: someone who, having seen Dvārāvatī, beheld the most beautiful face of Kṛṣṇa. (28)
Purified by the waters of the Gomatī, that traveler reached the Vindhya mountains, filled with great joy as he carried a portion of Kṛṣṇa’s grace upon his shoulder.
While proceeding on his way home, he saw there on the path a Rākṣasa of cruel deeds who had come swiftly to devour him. || 30 ||
By the mere sight of him, the most terrible adamantine paste (vajralepa) arising from Vārāṇasī was reduced to ashes in an instant. || 31 ||
That mountain of sin which could not be removed even in a hundred million lifetimes was liberated by the sight of the traveler Kṛṣṇa.
Then, when the cruel state was consumed, he shone with the light of merit like the moon released from the clouds upon seeing the traveler Kṛṣṇa.
Then, approaching him with joy as he traveled on the road toward Dvārakā, he prostrated himself on the ground with devotion, for the sight of him was a great festival.
Having bowed down, he then spoke in amazement: "Aha! By the sight of you today, my most terrible state has vanished and the highest perfection has been attained."
"O noble one, why have you come? What is the nature of your power? For your adamantine coating was indeed burnt away in Kāśī immediately upon [your] being seen."
Vasiṣṭha said: Having heard these words spoken by the Rākṣasa, Kṛṣṇa’s traveler was struck with great wonder and, his heart filled with joy, spoke to him. || 37 ||
The traveler said: "O Rākṣasa, having seen the glorious Dvāravatī, I have indeed come here; our power, which was like an adamantine glue, has been destroyed by the sight of Kṛṣṇa. (38)
Whoever bathes but once in the Gomatī and beholds the lotus-face of Kṛṣṇa, is delivered from all sins, even those that burn the three worlds.
Vasiṣṭha said: Having been addressed thus, the Rākṣasa, delighted, pure in soul, and filled with devotion, bowed down, performed a circumambulation, and then arrived at Dvārakā.
Having cast off his body in the Gomatī, he attained the station of Viṣṇu, being praised by the lords of the gods and the Gandharvas with showers of flowers. (41)
Thus has the great power of Dvārakā been proclaimed; even sins do not sprout upon seeing its travelers. What more need be said of Dvārakā itself? Therein, no sin whatsoever can take root.
O sinless King, that which I was asked by you has thus been told: the field that is the best of all fields, which destroys even the most adamantine taints.
Śrī Prahlāda said: Having heard what was spoken by Vasiṣṭha, Dilīpa, with a joyful mind, recognized Dvārakā as that king of sacred fields and was filled with wonder. (44)
He went joyfully to Dvāravatī with reverence for the God of gods; having seen Kṛṣṇa in the temple of the deity, he attained supreme perfection. (45)

Thus ends the thirty-fourth chapter, titled "The Description of Dilīpa’s Pilgrimage to Dvārakā, Preceded by the Account of the Ascetic," within the *Dvārakāmāhātmya*, the fourth section of the *Prabhāsakhaṇḍa*, the seventh part of the *Śrī Skanda Mahāpurāṇa* consisting of eighty-one thousand verses, concerning the destruction of the adamantine coating of sins committed at Kāśī merely by seeing a traveler from Dvārakā.
Prahlāda said: Oh, how great is the majesty of this sacred field extending ten yojanas in every direction, where even those dwelling in heaven behold everyone as four-armed!
Oh, how great is the majesty of this field! Having seen the four-armed deities who dwell eternally there, all the inhabitants of heaven pay homage to every resident of Dvārakā.
Oh, how great is the majesty of this sacred field, renowned in all the scriptures! Oh, how great is the majesty of this sacred field—listen, O stainless sages! (3)
Those who dwell there never desire liberation, being always eager for the service of Kṛṣṇa; even the stones found there grant liberation wherever one may be.
Even insects, moths, and the like, as well as beasts and reptiles—all sinners—become liberated by the grace of Dvārakā; how much more so those humans who dwell in Dvārakā eternally? || 5 ||
That destination which belongs to all living beings dwelling in the city of Dvārakā is surely difficult to attain even for sages whose vital energy is drawn upward (celibates).
The fruit that is obtained by those dwelling in all sacred fields and holy fords for ten million years is attained in Dvārakā day by day in less than a moment.

All the men and women residing in Dvārakā possess four arms; whoever beholds all these inhabitants of Dvārakā, who destroy all impurities, shall become exceedingly dear to Kṛṣṇa—truly, truly so, O best of the twice-born. (8)
Those lowest of men who, residing in Dvārakā, revile [Kṛṣṇa] and are devoid of love for Kṛṣṇa, fall into an ocean of misery.
Greatly terrified by Jayanta, they were impaled upon the tips of spears for a long time; indeed, they were dragged, beaten, fainted, and then rose up again.
"Save us! Save us, O Jayanta!"—thus cried those overcome by fear, as they remembered their former sins while being struck down by Jayanta.
Jayanta said: What evil and most dreadful deed have you, unfortunate ones, committed, that after obtaining all the fruits of merit, you have attained this supreme residence in Dvārakā? || 12 ||
The censure of the inhabitants of Dvārakā is certainly a great sin; that sin shall not be averted, and she [who endures it] is to be known as the Supreme Goddess. 13.
Therefore, by the command of Kṛṣṇa, I punish all sinners after they have experienced the most terrible fruit of reviling the Vaiṣṇavas.
Then, a meritorious birth shall take place in Dvārakā; by pleasing Kṛṣṇa, a perfection that is very difficult to attain shall be achieved.
Therefore, let that sin arising from the reviling of a Vaiṣṇava be consumed; for Maheśvara alone is the lord there, and Yama has no power over those people. (16)
Śrī Prahlāda said: Therefore, having gone to Dvāravatī, one should worship the Lord of Devas.
O Brahmins, listen to the arising of the fruit of whatever wealth one bestows at Dvārakā while residing on the banks of the Gomatī. || 18 ||
Whatever merit one obtains at Kurukṣetra on a Sunday during a solar eclipse by the gift of elephants, horses, and chariots, along with thousands of loads of gold—[that is obtained here]. (19)
Therefore, I have declared the truth, the absolute truth: that by the act of bringing [the image] from Dvārakā, even a gift measured at half a māṣa of gold is multiplied a thousandfold.
O twice-born ones, in the worship of Lord Kṛṣṇa, the merit becomes infinite according to the number of grains of rice in the food offering, as well as the number of leaves and flowers. (21)
But as for the fruit of one who should give food at Dvārakā, I am not able to describe it, nor are Brahmā, Śeṣa, and Maheśvara.
Whether he be a Brāhmaṇa, a Kṣatriya, a Vaiśya, or even a Śūdra, or even an outcaste, or a woman, whoever indeed dwells in Dvārakā with devotion; || 23 ||
Having uplifted ten million members of his lineage, he is glorified in the world of Viṣṇu; this is the truth, the absolute truth, O best of the twice-born—my speech is not false. (24)
Having seen and especially having touched a resident of Dvārakā, they are liberated from great sins and dwell in the heavenly world. || 25 ||
Even the dust of Dvārakā, when raised by the wind, is said to grant liberation to sinners; how much more so, then, the city of Dvārakā itself upon the earth? (26)
Śrī Prahlāda said: O tigers among the twice-born, listen to the greatness of Dvārakā, which destroys great delusion, situated in the presence of the Gomatī and Kṛṣṇa. (27)
Starting from Kuśāvarta and extending as far as the ocean, on whichever lunar day the priest of the gods arrives there during the month of Siṃha; || 28 ||
For in that [place], a bath in the Gomatī yields the fruit of two Gaṅgās and Godāvarīs; having diligently immersed oneself even once in the Gautamī at the end of a lion’s [era].
O twice-born ones, one obtains that same merit which would accrue from dwelling for a number of years on the Godāvarī by serving the Gomatī.
A bath taken with faith in the Gomatī when Jupiter is fully situated in Leo yields a thousandfold merit; that same merit is obtained day after day at Dvāravatī.
"Go, go, O fortunate one, to Dvārakā"—for whoever should say this, by the mere sight of him, one is liberated from all sins. (32)
And that man who, facing toward Dvārakā, utters the name "Dvārakā," shall certainly partake in liberation through the grace of Lord Kṛṣṇa. (33)
Those who daily remember Dvārakā, the holy Gomatī, Rukmiṇī, and Kṛṣṇa themselves with devotion, partake in the fruit of Dvārakā.
"Those whose minds were set upon this—that they would go to Dvāravatī and behold the Lord of Dvārakā—though they stood a thousand yojanas away," (35)

They are liberated from all sins; blessed are they, the purifiers of the world! What more need be said of those men who undertake a pilgrimage to Dvārakā? How much more so for those men who behold Kṛṣṇa, the Lord of Dvārakā? (36)
One who betrays a friend, a slayer of a Brahmin, a killer of a cow, a stealer of another's wife, as well as a matricide, a patricide, and likewise a thief of a Brahmin’s property—|| 37 ||
These and others who are most wicked and possessed of great sins are all liberated from every sin by the sight of Lord Kṛṣṇa.
What is the use of the Vedas devoid of faith, or even of complete commentaries? What is the use of thousands of loads of gold at Kurukṣetra during a solar eclipse? 39.
What is the use of gifts of elephants, horses, and chariots, or of the consecration of temples? What is the use of their proper worship, or of meritorious works such as *iṣṭa* and *pūrta*? (40)
What would be the use of all sacrifices, such as the Rājasūya and Aśvamedha, or what use of visiting sacred fields and pilgrimage sites, or of various kinds of austerities? (41)
What is the use of the hardships of the means to liberation, such as meditation, yoga, and samādhi, for one who obtains a vision of Kṛṣṇa, the Lord of Dvārakā? (42)
Or whoever hears the greatness of Dvārakā, especially on the full moon day of Vaiśākha or during the vigil on the Jayantī; || 43 ||
Especially on the full moon days of Māgha, Phālguna, Caitra, and Jyeṣṭha, Dvārakā remains meritorious even today, and particularly so during the Kali age.
On whose bank he established a sacrificial session, a water-shed, a palace, and even a couch; and having provided a refuge for ascetics, he constructed a pavilion on the shore. || 45 ||
Or else, by restoring ruined step-wells, wells, and tanks, or by consecrating an image of Viṣṇu, or by giving an object for his enjoyment; || 46 ||
O Brahmins, listen; I shall describe its fruit, which is the most excellent of all: having attained one's desired objects, one becomes a recipient of Kṛṣṇa’s grace. (47)
Having enjoyed pleasures in succession within the worlds consisting of light, that man indeed attains the world of Viṣṇu, which is saluted by the gods.
One should indeed install an image made of wood or stone in Dvārakā; by him the three worlds are established, and he shall attain union with Viṣṇu.

"There is no growth of sin, and there is the highest increase of merit. O Lord, how has this distinction arisen in Dvārakā? They say it is more wonderful than all other sacred fields and pilgrimage sites; please tell us how. (50)

Thus ends the twenty-fifth chapter, titled "Description of the Majesty of the Name Dvārakā," in the fourth section, the Dvārakā-māhātmya, within the seventh part, the Prabhāsa-khaṇḍa, of the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a compendium of eighty-one thousand verses.
Sūta said: Having heard the words of Prahlāda, Bali remained there in the assembly hall and, with a mind full of great eagerness, inquired about the majesty of that sacred field.
Having heard those words, which were preceded by a spirit of devotion, Prahlāda greeted him with love and began to speak.
Prahlāda said: For every single step taken toward the city of Dvāravatī, embodied beings obtain the merit that is the fruit of thousands of sacrifices. || 3 ||
Even those who desire to go toward Dvārakā through a mental resolve—their sins accumulated over ten thousand previous births are dissolved.
Even the most terrible sins remain in the body only so long as a living being does not go toward Dvāravatī in the Kali age.
Whether out of greed, or through compulsion, or by means of hypocrisy or deceit, he who goes to Cakratīrtha shall not enter the earth again.

Even a man of low birth or a sinful soul, upon dying in the city of Kṛṣṇa, is never tainted by the most fierce defects produced by the Kali age and the power of Time, provided he beholds the face of Kṛṣṇa with devotion.
Indeed, Kāśī, Avantī, and the city of Mathurā shine forth only so long as a living being does not behold the city protected by Kṛṣṇa.
O leader of the Dānavas, for those whose lives have departed in the abode of Kṛṣṇa, there is no return even in hundreds of millions of kalpas.
Residence in Dvārakā is difficult to attain; the sight of Kṛṣṇa is difficult to attain; bathing in the Gomatī and the sight of Rukmiṇī are difficult to attain in the Kali age.
For those who, while remaining at home, constantly remember the beautiful city of Kṛṣṇa, no sin whatsoever remains attached to their bodies.
O Lord of the Earth, the food of one in whose house an image of Keśava does not reside must not be eaten; it is declared to be equal to forbidden food.
O King of the twice-born, there is indeed no heat in fire, nor is there coldness in the sacrificial flame; likewise, there is no sin for Vaiṣṇavas who observe the fast on Ekādaśī.
O fortunate ones, there is no age equal to the Kali age; by the remembrance and glorification of Viṣṇu, the supreme, imperishable state is attained.
Wherever Satyabhāmā’s husband [Kṛṣṇa] is present and wherever the meritorious Gomatī flows, men shall attain liberation by bathing there in the Kali age.
If one obtains the Trispṛśā Dvādaśī in the bright fortnight of the month of Mādhava at Dvārakā, there is no one more fortunate than that person. (16)
Having reached the Trispṛśā-Dvādaśī and gone to Kṛṣṇapurī, the man who performs [the rites] with devotion to Hari shall obtain the fruit of an Aśvamedha sacrifice.
If Naṇdā, Jayā, and Bhadrā should indeed coincide, fasting, worship, and singing are difficult to achieve for the sake of Kṛṣṇa’s presence.
When the Ekādaśī at sunrise is very short, and the Trayodaśī at the end [of the month] is likewise short, while the Dvādaśī in between is complete, it is called Trispṛśā, and it is dear to Hari.
By a single fast, one obtains the fruit of ten thousand fasts; by keeping a vigil, a hundred thousandfold; and in the Kali age, by dancing, a crore-fold reward.
A mortal obtains that fruit day after day in Dvārakā; how much more so for those dwelling in houses in the very presence of Kṛṣṇa? (21)
Those of sinful intellect who have been struck down by defects born of speech, mind, and body are liberated in Dvāravatī upon beholding the auspicious face of Kṛṣṇa.
O Lord of the Daityas, those men who have gone to Dvāravatī are worthy of praise.
Holy fords are difficult to find here in this world, as are the best of mountains; Vaiṣṇavas are indeed rare in the world, and residence in Dvārakā is rare in the Kali age.
Whatever fruit one obtains by giving away thousands of crores of cows and hundreds of crores of jewels, that same fruit is obtained in the presence of Kṛṣṇa.
Who would not serve that city, upon entering whose boundary even such sins as the killing of a Brahmin perish by the mere sight of it? (26)
Who would not serve that city where, at the confluence of the Gomatī and the ocean, a stone marked with a discus grants liberation when worshipped? (27)
O Brahmins, whatever fruit is obtained at the Godāvarī when Jupiter is situated in Leo, that same fruit is gained merely by bathing in the Gomatī in the presence of Kṛṣṇa.
If a man drinks the water situated at Dvārakā for six months, his body becomes marked with the discus; of this there is no doubt.
The fruit that is obtained by residing in Kāśī for thousands of Manvantaras is attained by one dwelling in Dvārakā for five days.
O best of Daityas, a woman whose children have died remains unfortunate only so long as she does not behold with devotion, in the Kali age, that city beloved of Kṛṣṇa.
Rukmiṇī, Satyabhāmā, and Queen Jāmbavatī, as well as Mitravindā, Kālindī, Bhadrā, and Nāgnajitī.
Having worshipped Lakṣmaṇā there, as well as the Vaiṣṇavī forms beloved by Kṛṣṇa—by worshipping these according to the prescribed rites, an excellent son is obtained.
Men shall experience fear of worldly existence, the ruin of their homes, and folly only so long as they do not behold the City of Kṛṣṇa with devotion in the Kali age. (34)

Not everywhere does great merit reside at the confluence of the lord of rivers; yet from the confluence with the Jāhnavī comes liberation, and from the confluence with the waters of the Gomatī. Purified by the contact of the Gomatī's waters, I am now in the presence of Kṛṣṇa.
"The Lord of Rivers has declared that those men who behold me while I am joined with the waters of the Gomatī shall not return [to this world] again. (36)
If misfortune should befall one who is going to Dvārakā, there shall be no return for him even in hundreds of crores of kalpas.

Thus ends the thirty-sixth chapter, titled "Description of the Majesty of Beholding Dvārakā and the Ritual for Bathing in the Gomatī River," in the fourth section (Dvārakāmāhātmya) of the seventh book (Prabhāsakhaṇḍa) of the Śrī Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a compendium of eighty-one thousand verses.
Śrī Prahlāda said: Even a dog-eater who, while awake at night, constantly chants "Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa" during the Kali age, shall indeed become one whose very form is Kṛṣṇa. || 1 ||
In the Kali age, he who constantly utters "Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa" day and night obtains the merit of ten thousand sacrifices and that arising from ten million sacred fords.
If, having become a full Ekādaśī, it increases on the Dvādaśī, that most excellent of lunar days is renowned as Unmīlinī. || 3 ||
Those who indeed keep a vigil at night on the day of Vaṃjulī obtain the merit of ten million times ten million sacrifices in even half a Muhūrta. || 4 ||
O best of sages, when the twelfth day (dvādaśī) becomes complete and increases on the following day, such a Vañjulī occurring on the thirteenth day (trayodaśī) is difficult to obtain in the Kali age.
Those who keep a vigil after reaching Unmīlinī obtain that merit which yields the fruit of ten million cows in half a moment.
If, having become a full Ekādaśī, it increases day by day, then both the new moon (darśa) and the full moon (paurṇamāsī) are likewise called "increase of the fortnight" (pakṣavṛddhi).
Those who perform a vigil after obtaining [this rite] which increases one's merit for a fortnight obtain the fruit of ten million cows in a mere half of a half-moment (1/4th of a second).
Śrī Prahlāda said: Having bathed at Cakratīrtha, a man is liberated from all sins; he goes to the supreme abode, which is free from burning and dissolution.
Where Kṛṣṇa himself indeed washed the discus, that is the sacred Cakratīrtha of Hari, which is supremely meritorious; there, even the stones are marked with the discus and bestow liberation.
If they are found in that very place together with twelve wheels, he is to be known as the "Twelve-Souled One" (Dvādaśātmā), who is proclaimed as the bestower of liberation. || 11 ||
In Dvāravatī, there is a most beautiful stone known as Sudarśana, which possesses a single disc and bestows the singular fruit of liberation. || 12 ||
Those two, Lakṣmī and Nārāyaṇa, bestow the fruits of both worldly enjoyment and liberation; and by three [names], one worships the god Acyuta, who eternally grants the station of Indra.
Bhūtida is the destroyer of obstacles and possesses four wheels; Janārdana possesses five, while Vāsudeva removes the fear of birth and death.
Pradyumna, with exactly six [syllables], bestows fortune and splendor; Baladeva, however, with seven [syllables], increases one's lineage and fame.
Puruṣottama grants whatever is desired through devotion with his eight [forms]; Navavyūha grants everything—he who is difficult even for the best of gods to attain.
With ten [verses], however, Daśāvatāra bestows sovereignty; with eleven, Aniruddha grants lordship.
Nirvāṇa, however, consists of twelvefold [nature] and is remembered as being composed of twelve wheels; beyond that, it is infinite, bestowing both bliss and liberation. || 18 ||
Whatever stones there are there that are marked with the black discus, by the mere touch of them one is liberated from all sins. || 19 ||
Sins such as the killing of a Brahmin, born of the actions of mind, speech, and body—all these go to dissolution through the worship of the one marked with the discus.
Whether in a barbarian land or even a beautiful one, wherever the mark of the discus remains, O beautiful lady, that area for twelve yojanas is my sacred field.
And when the time of death has arrived, whoever holds the discus-mark in their heart, which destroys all sins, shall go to the supreme goal. || 22 ||
Having bathed at the confluence of the Gomatī as well as at Bhṛgutīrtha, one does not dwell within a mother’s womb again, even if he were a sinner.
Whatever worship of Viṣṇu is performed, whether it be of a tamasic or rajasic nature, it attains a state of sattva, just as the water of a river reaches the ocean.

Thus ends the thirty-seventh chapter, titled "The Description of the Greatness of the Stones Marked with the Signs of the Discus, Beginning with Sudarśana and Ending with Ananta, Located in the Sacred Field of Dvārakā, and the Narration of the Fruits of Worshipping Them," in the Fourth Section on the Greatness of Dvārakā, within the Seventh Book, the Prabhāsa-khaṇḍa, of the Śrī Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a compendium of eighty-one thousand verses. || 37 ||
Śrī Prahlāda said: O grandson, listen to the majesty of Dvārakā as it is told by me; for one who hears or speaks of it, liberation from Kṛṣṇa shall surely come to pass.
Through a son one conquers the worlds; through a grandson one attains immortality; and through a great-grandson, one ascends to heaven itself.
The wise know him to be a true son whose son is pure, capable, righteous in his early years, and practices devotion to Viṣṇu. || 3 ||
Day after day, he gave a thousand tawny cows (kapilā), each with golden horns, silver hooves, accompanied by its calf, provided with a bronze milking vessel, and covered with cloth.
Whatever fruit one obtains by giving a gift to a Brāhmaṇa who has mastered the Vedas, that same fruit is obtained merely by bathing in the Gomatī on the day of Madhubhid.
But he who feeds even a single Brahmin residing in Dvārakā during a time of plenty, O best of the twice-born, his merit shall be a hundred thousandfold.
The fruit is said to be a hundred-thousandfold when alms are given during a famine in the presence of Kṛṣṇa; likewise, according to the law, one should compassionately give alms to a mendicant.
"Will there be some supreme man in our lineage who, when the Kali age has arrived, will give [offerings] on behalf of us ancestors? (8)
In Dvārakā, having honored them especially in the presence of Kṛṣṇa, he gave gifts of food to the ascetics, as well as loincloths and garments.
For them, there is no need for well-performed sacrifices nor for sacred pilgrimage sites; wherever they may be, their constant duty is to please the ascetics.

Even those such as the dog-cookers are blessed who have gone to the city of Dvārakā; for having reached it, those devotees of the Lord indeed offer oblations to their ancestors on behalf of their sons.
They will worship with devotion by means of garments and abundant gifts.
The satisfaction that arises for us through honoring the devotees of Viṣṇu is not attained by the offering of funeral cakes at Gayā. || 13 ||
Those who, in the month of Vaiśākha, shall observe the Dvādaśī vow in the presence of Kṛṣṇa, worshipping Kṛṣṇa and keeping a vigil at night; (14)
One should recite the auspicious majesty arising from Dvārakā, as well as the childhood deeds of Kṛṣṇa and the vision of Bālakṛṣṇa and the others. (15)
The sporting of Gokula itself and the play of the multitude of gopīs—the deeds of Kṛṣṇa’s incarnation should be heard again and again. (16)
Having given to a Brāhmaṇa who maintains the sacred fires for the purpose of a Homa sacrifice a cow with golden horns, silver hooves, and her tail adorned with pearls, along with her calf; || 17 ||

Whatever sin a human being commits over ten million lifetimes, it is consumed during the night vigil for Kṛṣṇa; there is no doubt about this. By even a fraction of a moment’s contact with the vigil for Kṛṣṇa, the fruit [of that merit] is attained. (18)
One should recite the *Bhāgavata Purāṇa*, the beloved of Hari, at night, as long as there is light made by the sun and as long as there is night made by the moon. (19)
As long as the earth with its oceans and the principal mountain ranges endure, for so long shall he dwell in heaven; my word is not otherwise.
The fathers clap their hands and the grandfathers rejoice, seeing their own son thus listening to that which originates from Kṛṣṇa.
And one who recites the greatness of Dvārakā during our vigil should abandon that impure place, which is like that of the Mlecchas. || 22 ||
One should abandon that holy ford where there is no Śāligrāma stone and no devotees of the Lord; one should abandon even a most meritorious sanctuary. (23)
One should likewise abandon a secret place or a forest where the vow of the twelfth day (Dvādaśī) is not observed.
Even a good country becomes censurable where the Vaiṣṇava vow is not observed; even a bad country becomes meritorious where the Bhāgavatas reside in the Kali age.
Those devotees of Madhusūdana, though born of mixed origins, are purified; whereas those who are not devotees of Janārdana are of noble birth only in name, being equal to barbarians.
Those who cause Kṛṣṇa to mount a chariot during the months of Madhu and Mādhava all attain liberation, accompanied by ten million members of their lineage.
Those who cause a chariot to be made for the sake of the son of Devakī dwell in the world of Viṣṇu along with their ancestors until the end of the kalpa.
He who causes the greatness of Dvārakā to be heard by men in the Kali age, and he who indeed generates devotion toward it, shall obtain the fruit of a hundred sacrifices. (29)
That most wicked person who does not worship the Lord and goes elsewhere—the Lord of Rukmiṇī takes away the merit accumulated over ten million births. (30)
O King of Daityas, listen as I describe the fruit that belongs to one who constantly bears upon his body the clay produced from Śaṅkhoddhāra. (31)
The man who gives to ascetics and bestows it upon the Vaiṣṇavas constantly obtains the merit of a hundred loads of gold. || 32 ||
O Balarāma, in whose house the clay of Śaṅkhoddhāra always remains, one obtains ten million times the merit of performing the daily rites.
O twice-born ones, Lakṣmī, the beloved of Kṛṣṇa, never leaves the home of one who bears on his forehead the sectarian mark known as Gopīcandana.
Neither a planet afflicts him, nor a serpent, nor a rākṣasa; neither piśācas, nor kūṣmāṇḍas, nor pretas, nor jaṃbhakas [afflict him]. || 35 ||
For him there is no fear of fire or thieves, nor imprisonment in caves; nor is there fear of lightning or meteors, nor anything arising from portents.
Neither misfortune, nor ill omens, nor any such evil portents exist when one honors a devotee of Viṣṇu or performs the worship of the Śāligrāma stone. (37)

O Brahmins, when the water from the washing of the feet has been drunk and the food offering has been consumed in the presence of Tulasī at the time of Viṣṇu’s dissolution, [the result is as follows].
Listen, what was previously spoken by the Lord: "I shall describe the worthy recipient; I am forever a servant to those who hold the Bhāgavatas dear. (39)
Having abandoned Mathurā, Kāśī, Avantī—which destroys all sins—as well as Māyāpurī, Kāñcī, and Ayodhyā, when the Kali age has arrived; || 40 ||
I dwell in Dvārakā, surrounded by my entire army, along with those observing sacred fords and vows, performers of sacrifices and acts of charity, and sages and celestial bards led by Rudra.
In the Kali age, he who desires to satisfy me through the renunciation of faith or through devotion must go to the beautiful city of Dvāravatī; there I am to be seen.
Whatever sacred fords exist in the three worlds, which have been purified by me many times over, have been deposited within the Gomatī at the exceedingly purifying Cakratīrtha.
In the Kali age, by bathing for a single day at Cakratīrtha on the Gomatī, a human being becomes as if bathed in all the holy fords originating from the three worlds.
Freed from ten million sins, that man dwells with me in my world, accompanied by ten million members of his lineage; of this there is no doubt. (45)
One shall not be smeared by even the most heinous sins committed; for hundreds of thousands of births, prosperity shall not depart from one's home. (46)

Thus ends the thirty-eighth chapter, titled "Description of the Greatness of the Vigil and Other Rites at Dvārakā and Cakratīrtha on the Banks of the Gomatī," in the fourth section (Dvārakāmāhātmya) of the seventh book (Prabhāsakhaṇḍa) of the Śrī Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a compendium of eighty-one thousand verses.
Śrī Prahlāda said: Jayā, Vijayā, Jayaṃtī, Pāpanāśinī, Unmīlinī, Vaṃjulī, Trispṛśā, and Pakṣavardhinī—[these are the eight Ekādaśīs]. || 1 ||
Those who prepare cooked food produced from sacrificial grain obtain the merit of all the Purāṇas day after day. || 2 ||
During the vigil for Padmanābha, one should offer a lamp well-cooked with ghee, provided with two wicks and filled with ghee.
Whoever should perform a vigil before the Śālagrāma stone for Viṣṇu, those who indeed perform a vigil before the Śālagrāma stone— || 4 ||
They perform dances and instrumental music for the delight of the people, and those who cover the Śāligrāma stone with flowers; (5)
O twice-born ones, one should especially [worship] an image of Viṣṇu marked with the discus, as well as sandalwood paste combined with camphor and black agallochum.
It is fitting that one who always performs anointment with musk for the God of gods during the night vigil on the twelfth lunar day [should be honored].
I shall describe its merit before you in brief: that fruit is equal to [that obtained] at Koṭitīrtha, at Ujjayinī, and at Mahālaya. || 8 ||
At Vārāṇasī, Kurukṣetra, Mathurā, and Tripuṣkara; at Ayodhyā, Prayāga, and the holy site where the ocean meets [the river].
Through all merits, at all sacred fords, and in all temples of the deities, by performing tens of thousands of sacrifices there, and through abundant vows and gifts; || 10 ||
Whatever merit is gained from the Vedas studied, from the Purāṇas mastered, from penances performed, and from the merit of properly maintaining the stages of life (āśramas); || 11 ||
O son, that fruit which has been proclaimed by the sages and by Vedavyāsa is obtained through the vigil for Viṣṇu during both the bright and dark fortnights.
In ancient times, it was proclaimed on Kailāsa by the wielder of the trident (Śiva) to Haimavatī; and formerly, it was proclaimed by Brahmā in my presence to Nārada.

Formerly, Aruṇa related this to Vajrahasta when he questioned him; O Brahmins, I have also told you the fruit of the vigil on the twelfth day. Therefore, O twice-born ones, you should perform that vigil on the day of Viṣṇu.
Sūta said: Having spoken thus to the brahmins, he then addressed his own grandson Bali: "O grandson, you too should perform the vigil for Hari with faith."

Dvārakā, when meditated upon with the mind, burns away the sins accumulated over a hundred years; through its glorification, it burns away the sins arising from a hundred lifetimes—of this there is no doubt.
For those who travel even a single step toward Dvārakā, it surely removes the sin arising from thousands of births; liberation comes from the sight of Kṛṣṇa.
When a person is unable to go to Dvārakā itself, the greatness arising from Dvārakā should be recited in his home.
It should indeed be given to the Vaiṣṇavas and listened to with a spirit of devotion; it should especially be recited during the night-vigil on the twelfth lunar day.
That person obtains the merit arising from Dvārakā through the grace of Vāsudeva; this which has been spoken is the truth, the absolute truth. (20)
Mathurā, Dvārakā, Avantī, Māyā, Prayāga, and Kurujāṅgala always abide within his house. || 21 ||
Tripuṣkara, Naimiṣa, Gaṅgādvāra, Saukaraka, Candreśa, Kedāra, and likewise Rudramahālaya; || 22 ||
Vastrāpatha, Mahādeva, and likewise Mahākāla; Bhūteśvara, Bhasmagātra, Somanātha, and Umāpati. || 23 ||
Koṭiliṅga, the three-eyed deity who wanders in the forest of Bhṛgu, Dīpeśvara, Mahānāda, and the deity Acaleśvara.
The hosts of gods beginning with Brahmā always reside in the house, as do the ancestors, nāgas, gandharvas, sages, siddhas, and cāraṇas. || 25 ||
O grandson, whatever holy places there may be, and sacrifices such as the Aśvamedha—anyone who especially observes the Kṛṣṇajanmāṣṭamī [surpasses them all]. || 26 ||
As is the scripture of the Bhāgavata, so is the man who is devoted to the Bhāgavata; there is no difference between the two, just as there is none between Hara and Hari.
He who goes to an indigo field, or he who eats a radish—there is no deliverance from hell for him even in hundreds of millions of kalpas.
If a Brāhmaṇa, deluded by greed, should engage in the work of indigo-dyeing, he does not obtain any merit; nor should he engage in the sale of liquids.
The Soul of the Universe does not become pleased when a Vaiṣṇava’s bow is insulted; indeed, he who cuts down an Aśvattha tree on every single lunar festival [is likewise punished].

O Lord of Daityas, for as many Manvantaras as there are [in the wood used], such shall be one's residence in Raurava. If anyone anywhere performs a task with the wood of the Ariṣṭa tree, the Sun does not accept his worship or the offering of the Arghya water.
O son of a Daitya, for both the one who causes the cutting and the one who is cut, poverty and sickness arise for a hundred births when it occurs on a Sunday.
That best of men who indeed plants and protects the Sūryya tree shall dwell here in the presence of Bhāskara for seven kalpas.
Whatever fruit is obtained by planting ten million billion celestial trees, that very same fruit is indeed obtained by planting a single banyan tree.

The same fruit is obtained even by planting a dhātrī tree; however, O observer of noble vows, the fruit from planting tulasī is even greater. They attain immortality—of this there is no doubt to be made. (35)
He who, having risen at dawn, recites the name of Dvārakā during the Kali age, is liberated from all sins and goes to heaven; of this there is no doubt. || 36 ||
Those who do not observe the fast on the twelfth day conjoined with Rohiṇī, even if burdened by great sins, shall attain heaven at the end of the kalpa.
What is a day without the sun? What is night without the moon? What is a village without a tree? And what is the Dvādaśī vow without [the observance of its rules]? || 38 ||
His home is hell, and the staff of Yama is his second; that place where the *Viṣṇusahasranāma* is not recited daily.
And for him there shall be a second hell, the domain of Yama's command, where in the Kali age the Bhāgavata Purāṇa is not sung; they are cast into blazing pits of darkness and into fires.
Those who hate the devotee of the Lord and do not observe the day of Hari are led away by the messengers of Yama, and likewise they are reborn upon this earth.
They do not listen to the supreme deeds of Hari when they are being recited; by the command of Yama, they are tormented with extremely sharp saws.
Those wicked ones who revile the high-souled Vaiṣṇavas shall fall into hell for as long as the dissolution of all beings lasts.
The bath there shall be even more meritorious than at Gokarṇatīrtha. Those of great merit who behold the clay of Gopīcandana obtain the fruit of bathing in the Gaṅgā; of this there is no doubt. (44)
They bestow Gopīcandana clay upon the Vaiṣṇavas, those whose forehead mark (tilaka) is made from Gopīcandana.
By applying the Gopīcandana mark on the twelfth lunar day and keeping a vigil, one shall attain liberation through the recitation of the Thousand Names of Viṣṇu.
Those who, having risen daily at dawn, perform the glorification of the Vaiṣṇavas and the recollection of the Gomatī, are undoubtedly equal to Kṛṣṇa.
Those who, rising every morning, say "Dvārakā," obtain the merit born of ten million sacred fords day after day.

Thus ends the thirty-ninth chapter, titled "Description of the Greatness of the Dvādaśī Vow and Other Observances," in the fourth section on the Greatness of Dvārakā, within the seventh part, the Prabhāsa-khaṇḍa, of the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a compendium of eighty-one thousand verses. || 39 ||
Śrī Prahlāda said: He who indeed worships the Lord of Śrī with leaves marked with his own name shall reach the seven worlds and become the sovereign of the seven continents.
Whoever always worships Hari with the leaves of the *mākanda* tree, for him there arises in this Kali age the merit of ten thousand horse-sacrifices.
Having worshipped the goddess Lakṣmī, Sarasvatī, Sāvitrī, and likewise Caṇḍikā with leaves produced from the Śrīvṛkṣa tree, one goes to heaven.
The leaf produced from the Śrīvṛkṣa (tulasī) is declared to be superior; therefore, Acyuta should always be worshipped with effort at all times. || 4 ||
Those who worship the Śrīvṛkṣa on the twelfth lunar day when it falls on a Sunday are not tainted by sins such as the killing of a Brahmin, even if they have been committed.
Just as other footprints enter into the footprint of an elephant, so do all meritorious deeds enter into the day of Hari.
With this very unstable body that perishes at every moment, why does a living being not observe the twelfth day (Dvādaśī) accompanied by a vigil? || 7 ||

By chanting "Kṛṣṇa," one may deliver all seven past generations and fourteen future generations from hell, as well as all the worlds; those men, wherever they may be situated, do not live in this world [if they do not do so].

Having arrived at Dvārakā, they are honored throughout the three worlds; in Dvārakā, they provide food and lodging for ascetics, and those men obtain the fruit of a hundred sacrifices with every morsel [of food given]. || 9 ||

O son of a Daitya, listen as I shall describe in brief the merit of those who provide ascetics dwelling within Dvārakā with loincloths, clothing, and so forth, as well as food according to their capacity. (10)
O leader of the Daityas, that fruit which one obtains by feeding ten million knowers of the Vedas who are devoted to their ancestors at Gayā—[that fruit is attained here]. 11.
O grandson, such is the fruit when even a single mendicant is fed; one should give food to the mendicant, even if it means selling oneself. (12)
Blessed are all those ascetics, O Lord of Daityas, who dwell day after day in Dvārakā during the Kali age, having taken refuge in Kṛṣṇa.
Whatever living beings die in Dvārakā in the presence of Kṛṣṇa, even if they are sinners, they go to His abode after piercing through the solar orb.
For those best of men who dwell at the Cakra-tīrtha of Dvārakā, all the servants of Yama have been restrained by Yama himself. (15)
Those who, having bathed in the Gomatī, behold Kṛṣṇa, the remover of the impurities of the Kali age—neither you shall have dominion over them, nor shall they be within our domain.
Even a worm, an insect, or the trees that depend upon it—these go to the abode of Kṛṣṇa, for they do not return again to this cycle of worldly existence.
